13 September 2026 — An exact weighted selector representation for the binary source

Status: working ordinary-degree embedding over every field and a binary modular NS source construction with an old-target endpoint. Global elimination of the resulting relations remains open.

Route obligation. The preceding wide-family example concerns a selector-valued target. This cycle returns to the old target one: it identifies an exact degree ledger for selector expressions and constructs the binary source proof with selector-valued external multipliers. Individual ENS coefficients remain inside explicitly supplied local witness certificates.

1. Substituting genuine selector products reflects ordinary degree exactly

Let \(K\) be any field. Start with old variables \(X\), and introduce formal variables \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) in an order compatible with the block dependencies. Block \(b\) has positive accuracy \(h_b\) and formal input polynomials \(\widehat g_{b,i}(X,Z_{

\[ \Phi(Z_b)=P_b=\prod_{u=1}^{h_b} \left(1-\sum_i r_{b,u,i}\Phi(\widehat g_{b,i})\right), \qquad \Phi(X)=X. \]

Give old variables weight one. Having assigned the earlier weights, put

\[ \delta_b=\max_i\deg_w\widehat g_{b,i},\qquad w_b=h_b(\delta_b+1),\qquad \deg_w Z_b=w_b. \tag{SEL-weights} \]

All degrees here are ordinary collected polynomial degrees, with no field or Boolean reduction. Zero input polynomials are ignored in the maximum.

Working theorem. For every nonzero formal polynomial \(F(X,Z)\),

\[ \deg\Phi(F)=\deg_w F. \tag{SEL-reflection} \]

In particular \(\Phi\) is injective, every nonzero formal input stays nonzero, and the weights are the actual degrees of the genuine products.

Proof. Induct on the number of selectors. The old-variable case is immediate. For the new block write \(F=\sum_jF_jZ_b^j\), and let \(D=\max_j(\deg_wF_j+jw_b)\). The substitution upper bound gives \(\deg\Phi(F)\le D\).

Choose \(k\) attaining this maximum, and an input \(g_*=\Phi(\widehat g_{b,i_*})\) of degree \(\delta_b\), using the induction hypothesis. Set other coordinates of the new coefficient block to zero and write \(\rho_u=r_{b,u,i_*}\). The ordinary coefficient of \(\rho_1^k\cdots\rho_{h_b}^k\) is

\[ \sum_{j\ge k}\binom jk^{h_b}(-g_*)^{h_bk}\Phi(F_j). \]

This extraction does not reduce fresh powers and is different from the earlier Boolean-diagonal operator. The \(j=k\) summand is nonzero and has old-variable degree

\[ \deg_wF_k+h_bk\delta_b=D-h_bk. \]

For \(j>k\), its degree is at most

\[ D-jw_b+h_bk\delta_b =D-h_bk-(j-k)w_b<D-h_bk. \]

Thus the leading old part of the \(j=k\) summand cannot cancel, regardless of binomial coefficients vanishing in \(K\). Restoring the fresh monomial adds degree \(h_bk\), so the image has degree at least \(D\). This proves equality and injectivity. The argument also covers \(k=0\), nonlinear earlier inputs, unequal accuracies, and constant nonzero inputs. All-zero tuples are excluded because their product is constant.

2. The field quotient and raw coefficients require separate treatment

The theorem is not an embedding of Boolean or field quotients. For \(G=(x,y)\), let \(Z\) name its product and set \(\chi=(1-x)(1-y)\). The nonzero formal polynomial

\[ \chi(Z-1) \]

is nonzero at the formal domain point \(x=y=Z=0\), but its concrete image vanishes after old Boolean reduction: where \(\chi=1\), both inputs are zero and the genuine product is one. Similarly \(Z^p-Z\) has a nonzero ordinary image of degree \(p\,w_Z\), although that image vanishes on the concrete field domain. No identification of formal and concrete bounded domain ideals follows from (SEL-reflection).

Distinct formal selectors must represent distinct genuine blocks with disjoint own coefficients. If two products are assigned the same coefficient family, \(Z_1-Z_2\) can map to zero. A removed constant product must likewise be replaced by its known expression rather than retained as a free formal variable.

Nor is every concrete cofactor in the selector subring. When all retained selector weights exceed one, a fresh coefficient variable has degree one and cannot be \(\Phi(F)\): reflection would force \(\deg_wF=1\), so \(F\) could use only the old variables. At accuracy one a source prefix can be exactly such a coefficient. This is why the next construction changes the source composition instead of assuming an arbitrary collected NS coefficient has a selector expression.

3. The exact binary source expressions at the chosen stage

Use the coherent, genuine direct theorem construction, with one value for each chosen formula representation and all required OR subgroup products. Before optional polynomial normalization, binary negation and MOD evaluation are affine operations on child values, while an OR contributes one named product. Therefore every value and every original block input has an affine formal expression in old variables and the appropriate selectors. Block inputs use only strictly earlier selectors; same-level OR brackets are bypassed.

This is the binary specialization of the structural argument behind the recorded selector-dependency claim, applied here explicitly to the direct NS constructor. It is not an inference from the earlier PC endpoint alone.

Apply only the standard affine PHP boundary/clause map and any needed constant-product cleanup. Deleted products become \(1\), \(1-\rho_i\), \(x_{aj}x_{a'j}\), or constants. Replace their formal variables by those polynomials. At this stage every remaining value and input has the literal form

\[ q(X)+\sum_b\alpha_bZ_b,\qquad \deg q\le2,\quad \alpha_b\in\mathbb F_2, \tag{SEL-binary-profile} \]

with only earlier \(Z_b\)'s in an input. Retained own coefficient blocks remain fresh and their products genuine, so (SEL-reflection) applies with their actual new weights. The profile is stage-specific: optional packing can replace a selector by a product of earlier expressions and destroy the affine-in-selector assertion. A further normalization requires its own representation and degree audit.

4. Genuine OR interfaces have selector-valued NS targets

Before the boundary map, let \(L\ge1\) bound all source values and the required OR subgroup values. For a binary OR interface with actual values \(a,b,c\), the relation

\[ R=c-ab \]

has an NS witness through \(3L\). This is an ordinary-NS statement, proved directly from the source prefix comparison; it does not import the earlier PC reuse bound as an NS claim.

Degree proof. For three genuine products of degrees \(s_0,s_1,s_2\), the prefix of block \(b\) has degree at most \(s_b-\delta_b\). Each term of the union certificate therefore fits \(s_0+s_1+s_2\le3L\). For a non-OR child value \(a\), use the algebraic singleton data \(g=1-a,P=a,U=1\). Its companion \(a(1-a)\) has the domain-only NS witness through \(2\deg a\). Inserting that witness into the same identity preserves the bound \(s_0+\deg a+s_2\). This adds no artificial unary OR occurrence. Constant and empty cases reduce directly.

All three values have formal selector expressions, so the witness target is \(\widehat R=\widehat c-\widehat a\,\widehat b\). Its proof may use individual coefficients, but its target does not. Booleanity modules \(B_v=v^2-v\) similarly have selector-valued targets and binary domain-only witnesses through \(2\deg v\le2L\).

For MP, apply the OR interface to the implication and write

\[ R_{\rm MP}=c-(1-a)b,\qquad b=c+ab-R_{\rm MP}. \tag{SEL-MP} \]

The external antecedent multiplier is \(b\), of degree at most \(L\). Prefixes are confined to the supplied witness for \(R_{\rm MP}\). This differs from the original flattened MP coefficient \(bU_0\); it is a new modular source construction, not a claim that the old coefficient was selector-valued.

5. A binary source derivation with selector-valued outer coefficients

Let the balanced assumption-free \(F(\mathrm{MOD}_2)\) proof have height \(H_\pi\). Let \(M_{\rm fr}\) be the maximum leaf-occurrence count of its fixed Boolean axiom frames, counting repeated and constant leaves, and put

\[ C=\max\{M_{\rm fr}+2,12\}. \]

Choose coherent values and any required OR subgroup blocks, of polynomial total inventory and without increasing the maximum structural level. The usual source bound can be used for \(L\), enlarged to cover all these values and MOD prefix sums; for fixed depth it has the form \((\ell'+1)h^{\ell'}\).

Working source theorem. The theorem value has a formal identity

\[ \widehat\tau=\sum_\alpha Q_\alpha\,H_\alpha, \qquad \deg_wQ_\alpha+\nu_\alpha \le (C+H_\pi)L, \tag{SEL-source} \]

where \(H_\alpha\) are the chosen OR-interface and Booleanity targets, and \(\nu_\alpha\le3L\) or \(2L\) is their supplied concrete NS witness ceiling. Every \(Q_\alpha\) is a polynomial in old variables and selectors. Expanding the local witnesses gives an ordinary NS source derivation with the same bound. Polynomially many factored coefficient expressions suffice; no monomial-count bound is asserted.

Boolean axiom leaves, using NS accounting. Evaluate a fixed Boolean frame formally with negation \(1-z\) and OR multiplication. If node \(t\) has \(m_t\) leaf occurrences, its formal polynomial \(F_t\) has degree at most \(m_t\). Using the actual value \(a_t\), expand

\[ a_t-F_u(b)F_v(b) =(a_t-a_ua_v)+(a_u-F_u(b))a_v +F_u(b)(a_v-F_v(b)). \]

This is the earlier frame expansion, but multiply the entire child NS certificates. Inductively a child difference costs at most \((m_u+2)L\); its multiplier \(a_v\) costs at most \(L\), while the other multiplier \(F_u(b)\) costs at most \(m_uL\). Since both child leaf counts are at least one, all terms fit \((m_t+2)L\), including the \(3L\) local gate witness. Negation adds no cost. At the root, the formal tautology polynomial has its degree-\(m\) Boolean-domain certificate; substituting the representative values and their \(2L\) Booleanity witnesses costs at most \(mL\). Thus the actual axiom value costs \((m+2)L\), and all external multipliers remain selector polynomials.

MOD leaves. The recorded recursion has a ten-leaf outer Boolean frame. In characteristic two its MOD values are affine polynomials in the last argument value \(a\) and the common prefix sum \(t\); the interpolation relation is literal. The resulting frame polynomial in \(a,t\) has degree at most ten and vanishes on their Boolean domain. Formal Boolean division and substitution cost at most \(10L\), while the NS frame-comparison calculation costs \(12L\). The empty cases have value zero. This proves the claimed uniform leaf ceiling without a MOD-arity charge and without using a PC-only proof as an NS certificate.

MP composition. In (SEL-MP), multiply the antecedent's complete modular NS certificate by the known selector-valued \(b\). If the premise ceilings are \(d_a,d_c\), the new ceiling is

\[ d_b\le\max\{d_c,d_a+L,3L\}. \]

Induction on the balanced tree gives (SEL-source). All leaf and gate expressions are polynomials in selector-valued actual nodes. Unrolling follows at most \(H_\pi\) antecedent edges, with external factors \(b\), so the factored representation remains polynomial in the source inventory. Coherence is an explicit choice; independently scoped copies require their actual comparison modules and witness ceilings.

The original direct MP expression can also be sharpened to \(\deg(bU_0)\le2L\) for a genuine nonconstant implication product. Thus the point of the new construction is the selector-valued external interface, together with its stated recurrence; it is not a claimed factor-\(h\) improvement over every sharper analysis of the old source.

6. The old PHP target and the remaining elimination problem

Apply the standard global affine boundary/clause substitution to the constructed source proof. Its target becomes one, and each original axiom image has the original-degree NS image certificate. Re-express each removed selector by its known old polynomial, and name only the remaining genuine products. The diagram between formal substitution and concrete substitution commutes. Reflection therefore gives the exact degree of every surviving formal coefficient and target.

The resulting ordinary formal identity is

\[ 1=\sum_\alpha \widetilde Q_\alpha\,\widetilde H_\alpha, \qquad \deg_{\widetilde w}\widetilde Q_\alpha+\nu_\alpha \le (C+H_\pi)L. \tag{SEL-old-target} \]

Each \(\Phi(\widetilde H_\alpha)\) has the supplied NS witness from the exact weak PHP base, retained ENS companions, and domains, through the carried ceiling \(\nu_\alpha\). Here \(L\) and those witness ceilings are inherited from the pre-substitution construction. They are not silently reset to the smaller degree of a specialized target. At the specified stage, relation targets have selector degree at most two and old-variable degree at most four, by (SEL-binary-profile). Optional packing can change that profile.

Exact module interface. More generally, if formal relations \(H_\alpha\) have concrete NS witnesses through \(\nu_\alpha\), then an identity \(t=\sum Q_\alpha H_\alpha\) satisfying \(\deg_wQ_\alpha+\nu_\alpha\le D\) gives a concrete degree-\(D\) NS derivation of \(\Phi(t)\). Conversely a concrete identity already presented with such selector-valued outer factors lifts to the formal identity by injectivity. This is not a statement about arbitrary NS coefficients or a projection of the entire concrete field ideal.

Witness ceiling and polynomial degree are different data. For example the preceding OR-union relation at \(h=1\) has formal weighted degree four but minimum concrete NS witness degree six in its Boolean-domain presentation. Treating it as a supplied degree-four witness would lose that distinction.

The old-target source interface is now proved in the binary case, with polynomially many relations and polylogarithmic weighted degree under the usual hypothetical small-Frege-proof parameters. The remaining theorem would transfer (SEL-old-target) to a forbidden base PC refutation with a suitable degree bound. Neither the injective ordinary substitution nor the source compilation establishes that elimination theorem. The degree embedding is field-general; the source compiler and affine-in-selector profile stated here are binary.

The degree checker uses three genuine selectors, including nonlinear old inputs and a later input depending polynomially on earlier selectors. Four cases over \(\mathbb F_2,\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\), with two accuracy choices in the binary case, verify all \(28\) ordinary weighted-degree equalities. The field, zero-fiber, shared-coefficient, constant-product, and bare-coefficient controls behave as described in Section 2. Their full formal polynomials and concrete images are saved.

13 September 2026 — Old local relations are harmless, but their global cancellation need not be

Status: a source-local application of the existing old-consequence theorem, and a matching-tree refinement of the recorded exponential-family obstruction. No polynomial-family design extension or new PHP lower bound is established.

Route obligation. Test extension of an old PHP design to the preceding weighted source modules. The first result removes purely old local targets from the obstruction. The second gives an explicit old-target certificate showing why local checks alone do not justify a global lift, even for relations linear in selectors. Its factorial family count remains outside the small-source regime.

1. Purely old local targets already have bounded-degree base certificates

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\), at the specified source stage, and enlarge the carried value bound to \(L\ge4\) if necessary. A local OR-interface target has an NS witness through \(\nu\le3L\) using companions from at most three genuine blocks; non-OR children use domain-only Booleanity witnesses. Booleanity modules use domains alone. Inputs of each used block have degree at most \(L\), although they may depend on many earlier coefficient variables.

Corollary of the existing old-consequence transfer. Suppose a local formal target \(H\) contains only old incidence variables, and \(s=\deg H\le4\). If \(N\ge12L-1\), then

\[ H\in\mathcal I_s(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}) \subseteq\mathcal I_4(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}). \tag{LOCAL-old} \]

The functional strengthening is explicit; this is not an assertion of the same NS certificate from the weak base. Zero targets need no proof.

Proof. An NS certificate is a PC derivation through the same ceiling. Omit all unused companion families, retain the field equations for their variables, and eliminate the at most three used blocks in reverse dependency order. The recorded arbitrary-old-target theorem, rather than the refutation-only historical theorem, has binary bound

\[ \Lambda(d,\delta,s)=\max\{d+\delta,d+s,2s\} =d+\max\{\delta,s\}, \qquad d\ge s. \]

Since \(\delta\le L\) and \(s\le4\le L\), each elimination adds at most \(L\). The target remains independent of the removed variables, and later unused families contribute no companions, so their coefficient variables are simply old free variables with domains. The result is a PC derivation of \(H\) through \(\nu+3L\le6L\). Set every remaining free coefficient variable to zero; this preserves the target, the original PHP axioms, and the degree ceiling.

Add the permitted same-row exclusions and apply functional-PHP filtration stability with \(B=6L\). The hypothesis \(N\ge2B-1\) gives \(\mathcal C_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le s}=\mathcal I_s\), proving (LOCAL-old). No augmented NS/PC equality was used.

Consequently a purely old local module can be replaced in the formal certificate by its degree-\(s\) base representation. If \(QH\) was charged \(\deg_wQ+\nu\), the replacement costs at most \(\deg_wQ+s\le\deg_wQ+\nu\). Thus these individual relations add no new constraints to a design once the functional base and its allowed multiples are included. This says nothing yet about sums of selector-dependent relations whose selector terms cancel.

The old-target transfer itself was already established earlier. The new assertion here is its application to the support and degree bounds of the current source modules; it is not a newly named elimination theorem.

2. A matching tree stays within the literal source-gate interface

The earlier exhaustive Boolean assignment tree already disproved family-count-independent ENS elimination for PHP. We refine that control by branching on one chosen hole per pigeon and expressing the resulting certificate through the current source modules.

For the exact weak base \(\mathcal F_n\), let \(S\) be a partial injection of the first \(k\) pigeons into the \(n\) holes, including \(S=\varnothing\). For every \(j\in[n]\), form the child

\[ T=S\cup\{(k+1,j)\}. \]

If \(T\) is still a matching, continue; if its new cell shares a column with an earlier cell, stop that branch. A matching of all \(n\) holes has only colliding children when the \((n+1)\)-st pigeon is considered. For a bad leaf \(T\), let \(e=(i,j)\) be its unique earlier cell in the repeated column, let \(f=(k+1,j)\), and put \(R=T\setminus\{e,f\}\). Include an auxiliary product for each such nonempty matching \(R\).

For each nonempty registered set \(A\), take the genuine proper formula

\[ \Phi_A=\bot\vee\bigvee_{e\in A}\neg p_e. \]

Under the source's TRUE-by-zero convention its input tuple is \(0,(1-x_e)_{e\in A}\). Its accuracy-\(h\) product \(P_A\) has degree \(2h\), with nonzero companions of original degree \(2h+1\). Use independent own coefficient rows and write its formal selector as \(Z_A\), of weight \(2h\). Set \(Z_\varnothing=P_\varnothing=1\), the actual false constant; no all-zero block is retained.

The false leaf lets even a one-cell set be represented by a genuine binary OR. Inputs are listed in a fixed cell order, and the coefficient scopes are canonical for the chosen formulas. The ordinary collision clause \(\neg p_e\vee\neg p_f\) is a separate subgroup formula; the standard PHP clause map sends its product to \(x_ex_f\). A bad-leaf OR can be bracketed as that collision clause OR \(\Phi_R\), including the constant case \(R=\varnothing\).

These are legitimate proper OR comparisons at the chosen stage. No same-row exclusion is used below. Optional literal normalization or span/packing passes can change this presentation; it is not claimed to survive every such pass, or to be the mandatory output of the source compiler.

3. Exact local witnesses and their costs

Every tree edge supplies the selector-linear relation

\[ H_{S,j}=Z_T-x_{k+1,j}Z_S. \tag{MT-edge} \]

Here is the ordinary NS certificate, stated for any old affine tuple \(G=(g_i)\). Write \(A=P_G\), \(C=P_{G,\,1-x}\), and use prefix coefficients \(U_i,V_i,V_*\) with

\[ 1-A=\sum_iU_ig_i,\qquad 1-C=\sum_iV_ig_i+V_*(1-x). \]

Using the corresponding companions,

\[ C-xA =E_{C,*}+x\sum_iU_iE_{C,i} -x\sum_iV_iE_{A,i} +A V_*(x^2-x). \tag{MT-edge-witness} \]

Substitute the two prefix identities: the right-hand side is \((1-x)C+xC(1-A)-xA(1-C)=C-xA\). Prefix degree is at most \(2h-1\), so the witness costs \(4h+1\) when \(A\) is genuine, and \(2h+1\) when \(A=1\). Zero input slots contribute zero companions. This is the existing OR-interface argument specialized to a literal edge.

For a bad leaf, put \(x=x_e,y=x_f\). After the standard collision-clause map the source comparison is

\[ K_T=Z_T-xyZ_R. \tag{MT-collision} \]

A sharper current witness can be supplied directly. Let \(A=P_G=P_R\), \(C=P_{1-x,\,1-y,\,G}=P_T\), with prefixes \(U_i\) for \(A\), and \(V_x,V_y,V_i\) for \(C\). Then

\[ \begin{aligned} C-xyA={}&E_{C,x}+xE_{C,y} +xy\sum_iU_iE_{C,i}-xy\sum_iV_iE_{A,i}\\ &+AyV_x(x^2-x)+AxV_y(y^2-y). \end{aligned} \tag{MT-collision-witness} \]

The first two terms equal \((1-xy)C\); the next positive sum equals \(xyC(1-A)\). The remaining terms together equal \(-xyA(1-C)\), since \(y(x^2-x)=-xy(1-x)\) and \(x(y^2-y)=-xy(1-y)\). This proves the identity. Its NS degree is at most \(4h+2\), or \(2h+2\) when \(A=1\). It uses only the retained \(A,C\) companions and old Booleanity.

This is also obtained by applying the collision normalizer to the three-product OR comparison and replacing its two removed companions by their Booleanity certificates. The improved \(4h+2\) cost is justified by the displayed current witness; it is not obtained by silently lowering an inherited cost. All remaining primitive companion degrees still equal their original \(2h+1\).

Both (MT-edge) and (MT-collision) are linear in selectors, with old coefficient degree at most two. Their actual weighted polynomial degrees are at most \(2h+1\) and \(2h+2\), respectively; their supplied NS costs are different data.

4. The complete module identity has old target one

Let \(\mathcal T\) be the internal matching nodes and \(\mathcal B\) the bad leaves. For \(S\in\mathcal T\) of size \(k\), use the original row generator \(f_{k+1}=\rho_{k+1}-1\). Directly from (MT-edge),

\[ \sum_{j=1}^nH_{S,j}+Z_Sf_{k+1} =\sum_jZ_{S\cup\{(k+1,j)\}}-Z_S. \]

Sum over the tree. Every nonroot internal selector occurs once as a child and once as a parent, giving

\[ \sum_{S,j}H_{S,j}+\sum_{S\in\mathcal T}Z_Sf_{|S|+1} =\sum_{T\in\mathcal B}Z_T-1. \]

For each bad leaf, the original collision generator \(c_T=x_ex_f\) and (MT-collision) give \(Z_T=K_T+Z_Rc_T\). Thus the full formal identity is

\[ 1=\sum_{T\in\mathcal B}K_T +\sum_{T\in\mathcal B}Z_Rc_T -\sum_{S,j}H_{S,j} -\sum_{S\in\mathcal T}Z_Sf_{|S|+1}. \tag{MT-old-target} \]

In characteristic two the displayed signs agree, but no domain reduction is used in this formal identity. Local gate coefficients are constants. Row and collision coefficients are selectors or sums of selectors, of weight at most \(2h\). Expanding the supplied local witnesses yields a concrete NS refutation of the exact weak PHP system plus this one-level literal ENS family through

\[ D=4h+2. \]

The prior exhaustive assignment-tree theorem has the slightly smaller \(4h+1\) bound; the point here is the explicit source-module presentation and smaller matching-tree inventory, not a better universal degree bound.

Write \(A_n=\sum_{k=0}^n(n)_k\), where \((n)_k=n!/(n-k)!\). There are \(A_n\) internal matching nodes and \(nA_n\) distinct edge children. Additional matching-rest helpers number at most the bad leaves, so the retained block count satisfies

\[ nA_n\le M\le2nA_n,\qquad A_n=n!\sum_{r=0}^n\frac1{r!},\qquad M=\Theta(n\,n!). \]

Each block has at most \(n+2\) input slots, including the zero slot. Thus companion count is \(O(n^2n!)\), and coefficient count adds a factor \(h\). These are factorial-size controls, not polynomial-size PHP proofs.

5. What fails in the proposed design lift

For \(n\ge8h+3=2D-1\), the functional old base has normalized designs through \(D=4h+2\), by the recorded stability theorem. Yet no normalized functional on the formal weighted degree-\(D\) space can annihilate every allowed module/base multiple above: applying it to (MT-old-target) gives \(1=0\). This also holds for any design initially supplied at a higher degree within its valid base range.

All new module targets in this example contain selectors. Therefore checking only their purely old local targets finds no obstruction, even though their full sum derives the old polynomial one. Requiring selector-linear relations, constant external gate coefficients, and small old coefficient degrees does not repair a family-count-independent lift.

Remaining gap. The actual lower-bound route has polynomially many source families and logarithmic balanced proof height. Here \(\log M=\Theta(n\log n)\). The example does not refute a bound with a suitable dependence on \(\log M\), a source-specific global lifting theorem, or the existing polynomial literal-family restriction theorem. It identifies exactly why that family/proof information cannot be discarded. General polynomially many affine proper source blocks remain uncovered.

Every field-omission control changes its ordinary polynomial identity. 13 September 2026 — In the first source-comparison band, pair moments reduce to singleton compatibility

Status: a source-compatible affine-flat presentation, an exact formal-module design reduction for \(6h\le D<8h\), a bounded-rank corollary, and exact finite controls. Singleton compatibility for general polynomial source families and the completed multilevel endpoint remain open.

Route obligation. Use the actual proper-OR relations to identify the missing global design condition. In this band, canonical sharing makes their pair constraints extendible by old-base filtration stability. The unresolved equations couple individual flat-indexed functionals through low-rank joins. This is a statement about the explicitly costed source-module system, not all ENS NS consequences or augmented PC closure.

1. Row coordinates retain the needed base filtration

Over \(\mathbb F_2\), use the explicit functional auxiliary base \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\), with \(N\ge2\). In the existing row projection, keep \(y_{ij}=x_{ij}\) for \(j<N\) and set

\[ \sigma(x_{iN})=1-\sum_{j<N}y_{ij}. \]

No hole is deleted. Let \(F'=\sigma(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun})\setminus\{0\}\), in the free coordinates \(Y\). The earlier transfer was stated for the weak base; here the extra same-row exclusions have the same degree-two image certificate as any product of cells:

\[ \sigma(xy)=xy+(\sigma x-x)y+(\sigma x)(\sigma y-y). \]

Each difference is zero or a negative row generator. For a same-row exclusion at most one cell is a pivot; both nonzero affine factors remain nonconstant for \(N\ge2\), so every nonzero quadratic image still has degree two. Pivot Booleanity has the recorded degree-two certificate.

Successive substitution of pivot variables also gives, for every polynomial \(f\) of degree at most \(k\),

\[ f-\iota\sigma(f)\in\mathcal I_k(\{\rho_i-1\}), \]

where \(\iota\) includes the nonpivot coordinates back into the old ring. Indeed, telescope one occurrence at a time; its difference is a row generator times a polynomial of degree at most \(k-1\). The generator image certificates and this identity prove

\[ \mathcal I_k(F')= \mathcal I_k(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun})\cap\mathbb F_2[Y]. \tag{FLAT-row-quotient} \]

For the reverse direction apply \(\sigma\) to an old certificate; for the forward direction replace each image generator by its degree-two old certificate. Original row generators map to zero, and no nonzero generator has acquired a smaller degree requiring an enlarged cofactor space.

Consequently, when \(N\ge2B-1\), the existing base stability theorem gives

\[ \mathcal I_B(F')\cap\mathcal P_{\le k}=\mathcal I_k(F'), \qquad \mathcal C_B(F')=\mathcal I_B(F')\quad(k\le B). \]

Restriction of old annihilating functionals is therefore surjective between these degrees, including for unnormalized functionals. Normalized ones exist. An original old design agrees with its row-projected values through its degree because it kills \(f-\iota\sigma(f)\). This is a base result, not stability of the augmented module system.

2. A compatible one-level source presentation by affine zero flats

Project the original level-one binary inputs into these row coordinates. They remain affine. Use the audited equal-span sharing and rank-\(\le2h\) packing maps, choosing one canonical affine basis for each span. The zero span has product one; a span containing one has product zero. For a consistent span \(V\) of rank \(r\), define its old Boolean zero-set indicator

\[ \chi_V(Y)=\prod_{j=1}^r(1-F_j(Y)) \]

using its chosen basis. If \(r\le2h\), packing makes this the actual product. If \(r>2h\), retain one genuine selector \(Z_V\), of weight \(2h\). A nonzero consistent affine span has no nonzero constant, so its input degree is one and its genuine product degree is exactly \(2h\). Denote the inconsistent span by \(\bot\), with value zero, and the zero span by \(0\), with value one. Write

\[ v_V=\begin{cases} 0,&V=\bot,\\ \chi_V,&r_V\le2h,\\ Z_V,&r_V>2h. \end{cases} \tag{FLAT-values} \]

This can be made compatible with the PHP endpoint, not merely with an isolated abstract family. After row projection the row-clause input span contains one, so choose its scalar zero-product rule. Collision clauses have rank at most two, hence pack using the canonical basis. Their images equal the ordinary collision polynomial modulo old Booleanity through degree two. Keep the final PHP coefficient vectors zero, so its product remains one. Its companion images are then zero or these degree-two base consequences. Their original \(2h^2+3h\) ceilings cover the images.

All level-one sharing/packing coefficient maps are affine. Their companion images have the previously verified NS ceiling \(2h+1\), and coefficient-field images fit degree two. Together with row projection this gives a global affine source substitution preserving the completed NS ceiling; every later input undergoes the same substitution. This is a compatible variant of the boundary/clause map, with those image certificates, rather than an assumption that an arbitrary later normalization preserves the earlier literal profile.

For an actual original-level-one OR comparison, the parent span is \(C=A+B\), or \(\bot\) if that sum contains one. An original level-zero non-OR child has affine value \(a\), represented by the rank-one input span \(\langle1-a\rangle\), including its constant cases. Thus the formal source relation is

\[ H_{A,B}=v_{A+B}-v_Av_B. \tag{FLAT-OR} \]

Use the uniform supplied NS witness cost \(6h\), obtained by the three-value bound with \(L=2h\) and the degree-preserving maps just described. Retained-selector Booleanity \(Z_V^2-Z_V\) costs \(4h\). Every one-level source value is an affine combination of selectors and old polynomials of degree at most \(2h\); its Booleanity is a sum of these selector equations and old Booleanity consequences through \(4h\), by Frobenius.

The finite registry need contain only the actual source subgroups and comparison triples. For any repeated unordered pair of retained children, canonical sharing gives the same parent span. No closure under all possible pairs or exponentially many bases is assumed. The uniform \(6h\) cost is part of the presentation: a certificate using a sharper local cost with additional cofactors is not automatically a certificate in the same band here.

3. Exact reduction to singleton moment equations

Put

\[ D=6h+u,\qquad 0\le u<2h. \]

Let \(\mathcal A_k=\operatorname{Ann}(\mathcal I_k(F'))\). Assume the old base has the filtration extension property through \(D\); \(N\ge2D-1\) supplies it for the projected functional PHP base. Fix a normalized \(\lambda\in\mathcal A_D\).

The formal degree-\(D\) module space uses old generator multiples through their usual degree, multiples of \(Z_V^2-Z_V\) with cofactor weight at most \(D-4h\), and multiples of (FLAT-OR) with cofactor weight at most \(D-6h=u\). It does not include every concrete ENS axiom multiple as a separate formal module.

Working theorem. A normalized functional on the formal weighted degree-\(D\) space, extending \(\lambda\) and annihilating all those allowed multiples, exists if and only if there are functionals

\[ \mu_V\in\mathcal A_{4h+u} \quad\text{for every retained }V, \]

satisfying the following equations for every indicated source comparison and every old \(q\) of degree at most \(u\):

\[ \begin{array}{ll} \mu_C(q)=\lambda(q\chi_A\chi_B), &A,B\text{ packed},\ C=A+B\text{ retained};\\[2pt] \mu_C(q)=\mu_A(q\chi_B), &A\text{ retained},\ B\text{ packed},\ C=A+B\text{ retained};\\[2pt] 0=\mu_A(q\chi_B), &A\text{ retained},\ B\text{ packed},\ A+B=\bot. \end{array} \tag{FLAT-singletons} \]

Here “packed” includes the constant values zero and one; interchange the children when necessary. A consistent parent of a retained child cannot have rank at most \(2h\). All expressions are in their stated domains: \(\deg(q\chi_B)\le u+2h\), and \(\deg(q\chi_A\chi_B)\le u+4h\).

Necessity. Given such a joint functional \(\Lambda\), define \(\mu_V(q)=\Lambda(qZ_V)\) through old degree \(4h+u=D-2h\). Old generator multiples show \(\mu_V\in\mathcal A_{4h+u}\). The three displayed source relations give exactly (FLAT-singletons).

Supply the pairs. For distinct retained \(A,B\) whose source comparison has retained parent \(C\), prescribe a pair functional on old degree at most \(u\) by \(\nu_{AB}(q)=\mu_C(q)\). Prescribe zero when the parent is \(\bot\). Canonical sharing makes this prescription unique for a fixed unordered pair. It belongs to \(\mathcal A_u\), so old filtration stability extends it to

\[ \nu_{AB}\in\mathcal A_{2h+u}. \]

Pairs with no such comparison may use the zero functional. When the children are identical, the parent is the same span and the equation is already selector Booleanity; no separate pair unknown is needed.

Assemble a joint functional. There are at most three selector occurrences in a monomial of weight \(D<8h\). Reduce repeated selector powers to their distinct support when assigning its moment. Use \(\lambda\) for empty support, \(\mu_V\) for a singleton, \(\nu_{AB}\) for a distinct pair, and the zero functional through old degree \(u\) for three distinct selectors. The component domains are

Distinct selector supportAvailable old degree
None\(6h+u\)
One\(4h+u\)
Two\(2h+u\)
Three\(u\)

A monomial with repeated selectors has an even smaller old-degree requirement, so every assigned value is defined. Each component annihilates the appropriate old NS space. Repeated-support reduction kills every allowed selector-Booleanity multiple: its cofactor has at most one selector because \(D-4h=2h+u<4h\).

An OR-module cofactor is old-only, since its weight is at most \(u<2h\). Both-retained children use the prescribed pair restriction; one-retained-child and packed-parent seeds use (FLAT-singletons). If all three values are packed or constant, their difference vanishes on the old Boolean cube and has degree at most \(4h\). Old Boolean division therefore certifies it through \(4h\), and multiplication by \(q\) fits \(4h+u\le D\). These exhaust all cases. The resulting \(\Lambda\) has the required normalization and old values, proving sufficiency.

Seeds are individually consistent. If a retained \(C\) is a sum of two packed spans, \(r_C\le4h\). Every such seed equals \(\lambda(q\chi_C)\): two representations differ by an old Boolean consequence through \(4h+u\). This restriction belongs to \(\mathcal A_u\), since multiplying an old degree-\(u\) axiom multiple by \(\chi_C\) fits degree \(D\). It extends individually to \(\mathcal A_{4h+u}\). What remains unproved is simultaneous feasibility of the low-rank join equations between those functionals, not consistency of a seed or of a high-high pair in isolation.

4. A degree-preserving bounded-rank consequence

Corollary. In this module presentation and degree band, if every retained affine span has rank at most \(4h\), every old \(\lambda\in\mathcal A_D\) extends, with no family-count charge.

Proof. For each retained \(V\), first prescribe

\[ \mu_V(q)=\lambda(q\chi_V) \qquad(\deg q\le2h+u). \]

All products have degree at most \((2h+u)+4h=D\). This functional annihilates \(\mathcal I_{2h+u}(F')\), and old stability extends it to \(\mathcal A_{4h+u}\). Every required argument \(q\chi_B\) lies in the prescribed domain. The identity of zero sets gives \(\chi_C-\chi_A\chi_B\) an old Boolean certificate through degree at most \(6h\), also when \(C=\bot\). Multiplying by \(q\) fits \(D\). Hence all equations in (FLAT-singletons) hold, and the theorem applies.

This improves degree accounting for an already manageable rank scale. The existing factor-bin construction can put up to four affine factors per row using coefficient degree at most three; its companion images cost at most \(4h+1\le3(2h+1)\). Thus rank \(O(h)\) already admits a constant-factor degree transfer. The corollary is not new asymptotic coverage of the intermediate-rank PHP source family.

5. The band and canonical sharing are substantive hypotheses

The matching-tree obstruction is consistent with the reduction. After the compatible cleanup, its literal joins are precisely equations of the form (FLAT-singletons). Old row identities preserve the flow of singleton means and collision consequences kill the bad-leaf means. Their full tree cannot be assigned consistent singleton functionals. Its factorial inventory remains outside the small-source regime; automatic pair extension does not solve that network.

At \(D=8h\), an OR-module cofactor may itself be a selector. For a genuine high-high relation \(H=Z_C-Z_AZ_B\), multiplying by \(Z_C\) requires

\[ \Lambda(Z_C^2-Z_AZ_BZ_C)=0. \]

The construction above sets the distinct triple moment to zero. If \(\mu_C(1)=1\) and \(A,B,C\) are distinct, the left side is one. Its polynomial already has weight \(6h\), but its supplied NS module cost is \(8h\). Thus this particular lower-degree design has no moment-preserving extension to degree \(8h\). Different lower-degree choices may extend; no nonexistence of degree-\(8h\) designs is asserted. This is also why formal target degree cannot replace witness cost.

Without canonical sharing, two occurrences of the same child pair could have distinct formal parents with chosen means zero and one. The two source equations would demand both values for the same \(\nu_{AB}(1)\). Such singleton choices need not have a pair extension. Sharing equal affine spans, or supplying their actual compatibility equations, is required.

Finally, the completed binary source bound from the modular compiler is not shown to lie below \(8h\), and later levels need not have affine old inputs. The result does not transfer that whole endpoint, prove an augmented PC closure statement, or project arbitrary concrete ENS NS certificates into this formal module system.

6. Exact checks, outcome, and process assessment

The checker uses four free Boolean variables, not a PHP base. An invertible dense binary map \(u_i=\sum_{j\ne i}x_j\) defines all \(81\) nonempty coordinate-assignment flats in the \(u\)'s, including the whole space; inconsistent intersections have value zero. At \(h=1\), the \(48\) flats of ranks three and four retain selectors, and ranks at most two are packed. All \(81^2=6{,}561\) ordered source comparisons are included, of which \(4{,}160\) have inconsistent intersections.

The old normalized functional is the sum over \(\mathbb F_2\) of evaluations at \(x=0,e_0,e_1\). It is nonmultiplicative: both first-coordinate means are one but their product moment is zero. Singleton moments are its zero-flat-weighted evaluations. Pair moments preserve the required restrictions through degree \(u\), while higher available squarefree moments are set to zero; these are valid old Boolean functionals in this free-base fixture. Distinct triple components are zero.

All \(94{,}198\) legal generator/cofactor checks passed, using ordinary monomials and the specified witness budgets. Each case separately verifies the nonextension polynomial and the inconsistent-parent-mean control. The reproduction record documents the complete flat registry, moment components, gate constraints, and controls. No large PHP moment system was computed.

Outcome. In this source-compatible band, the remaining condition is an explicit network of low-rank joins between singleton old functionals. A general polynomial-family solution of that network is unproved. Before increasing the moment order, compare this concrete condition with existing affine-clause proof systems and their PHP lower bounds, checking the exact rule and encoding correspondence.

Process assessment. The pair reduction isolates a source-specific compatibility obligation, while the rank corollary adds no new asymptotic coverage; existing row-projection and packing records supplied the preprocessing, so no further framework rule or tool was warranted.

13 September 2026 — The affine-clause literature does not yet supply the missing proof extraction

Status: targeted source audit, exact unary-to-bit algebraic transfer, encoding and interpretation controls, and a provenance correction. No Res(\(\oplus\)) proof or affine DAG has been extracted from the source certificate.

Route obligation. Compare the singleton join network with established affine-clause lower bounds. The flat dictionary is exact, but a module identity is not itself a clause refutation. The audited bounds require additional proof-structure and encoding hypotheses which our construction has not supplied.

1. What the audited primary sources actually provide

Gryaznov, Ovcharov, and Riazanov, arXiv:2404.08370v2, Sections 2.1 and 3.1.1, use linear clauses with resolution and semantic weakening. Their Theorem 3.4 gives tree-like size at least \(2^{n-1}\) for the ordinary unary clausal \(\mathrm{PHP}_n^m\), \(m>n\), and clause space at least \(n-1\). This is not a general DAG size lower bound. Their Section 4.1.2 explicitly flags that the extensibility proof need not survive adding functionality clauses.

Byramji and Impagliazzo, arXiv:2511.20023v1, Theorem 1.3, prove for bit PHP with \(m=n+k\), \(k\le\delta n\),

\[ \log S=\Omega\!\left( \min\left\{\frac{n^2}{d_\pi},\frac{n^4}{k\,d_\pi^2}\right\}\right). \]

Here \(d_\pi\) is proof-DAG depth. Their Section 3.2 uses affine DAGs with parity-labeled edges and affine-system node labels. Neither \(d_\pi\) nor the input encoding is our algebraic degree or fixed Frege formula depth. Lemma A.2 gives unary functional PHP a depth-\(O(n\log n)\) parity decision tree; that statement does not give polynomial proof size.

A newer-source screen found Alekseev–Gaevoy, ECCC TR26-007, concerning constrained bit PHP with conditional or restricted-system results, and Itsykson–Podolskii–Shekhovtsov, ECCC TR26-018, concerning gadget-lifted formulas and size/depth bounds. Their abstracts do not identify a theorem immediately applicable to our unlifted unary module system. These two records were screened, not proof-audited.

The audit record preserves versions, precise reading scope, and legitimate acquisition links. Both versioned arXiv papers were retrieved for local use; their nonexclusive arXiv distribution licenses do not clear republication here. A publisher DOI lookup failed with HTTP 403; the needed definitions and bounds were available from the primary sources above.

2. The local flat dictionary is valid, but has a direction

For a consistent affine input span \(V\) with basis \(F_1,\ldots,F_r\), associate the linear clause

\[ C_V=\bigvee_{j=1}^r(F_j=1). \]

Its falsifying assignments are exactly the zero flat of \(V\), and its Boolean false-indicator is \(\chi_V\). If \(V\subseteq W\), then \(C_V\) semantically implies \(C_W\). The source relation \(Z_{V+T}=Z_Vv_T\) expresses the corresponding indicator intersection. It is an identity between values; it does not assert that either clause has been proved.

A parity split on an affine \(g\) has two source relations

\[ H_0=Z_{V+\langle g\rangle}-Z_V(1-g),\qquad H_1=Z_{V+\langle g+1\rangle}-Z_Vg, \]

with the canonical constant/packed cases interpreted as before. Their exact sum gives

\[ Z_V=Z_{V+\langle g\rangle}+Z_{V+\langle g+1\rangle}-H_0-H_1. \]

If both child clauses have already been derived, this proves the parent value zero, matching same-context parity resolution. General resolution additionally aligns the two contexts by weakening. This explains why clause inferences can be represented by our algebraic relations. It does not reverse the simulation: arbitrary old polynomial cofactors, cancellations modulo the old NS spaces, and repeated value uses in a source identity have not been turned into legal clause inferences of controlled size and depth.

Balancing the Frege proof controls its own proof height. It does not establish regularity, tree structure, or comparable path depth for a Res(\(\oplus\)) proof that has not yet been constructed.

3. Row coordinates do not supply the source's proper-point hypothesis

The unary extensibility theorem concerns a linear system with a Boolean solution satisfying all hole clauses, before imposing all pigeon axioms. It cannot be applied by regarding an old NS design in our row coordinates as such a point.

Indeed, let \(V(Y)=0\) be a consistent rank-\(r\) affine system in the nonpivot row coordinates. Its lift to the original cells includes all \(n+1\) equations \(\rho_i=1\). Their affine polynomial span together with \(V\) has rank exactly

\[ n+1+r. \]

Proof. Each row generator has its own pivot cell with coefficient one, whereas the polynomials in \(V\) have no pivot cells. In a dependence all row coefficients therefore vanish first, and then the independent \(V\)-coefficients vanish. This proves the rank count.

Moreover no Boolean point satisfying all these row equations can satisfy every hole clause: each of the \(n+1\) rows has an odd, hence nonzero, number of ones, while at most one one per column allows only \(n\) ones altogether. Thus even the lifted root has no hole-proper point. Low-degree old designs still exist in the stated range; their existence is a linear-functional statement, not a point-existence statement. Both the proper-point and small-rank hypotheses of that proposed import fail.

Likewise, a zero singleton mean is not a zero functional. On four free Boolean variables take the normalized root \(\lambda=\mathrm{ev}_0+\mathrm{ev}_{e_0}+\mathrm{ev}_{e_1}\) over \(\mathbb F_2\). Weight it by the indicator of \(V=\{x_1=x_2=x_3=0\}\). Then

\[ \mu_V(1)=0,\qquad \mu_V(x_0)=1,\qquad \mu_V(1-x_0)=1. \]

The two split children both have mean one, with sum zero in the field. Discarding a zero-mean node as if it had zero probability would lose these moments. This is a control against that interpretation, not a proof that every affine-DAG extraction is impossible.

4. The bit encoding has a valid algebraic transfer

Let \(n=2^\ell\), with one \(\ell\)-bit string \(b_i\) per pigeon. For each label \(j\in\{0,1\}^\ell\), set

\[ \eta_j(b_i)=\prod_{t:j_t=1}b_{it} \prod_{t:j_t=0}(1-b_{it}),\qquad \Psi(x_{ij})=\eta_j(b_i). \]

Let \(\mathcal B_n\) consist of bit Booleanity and the standard bit-PHP collision polynomials \(\eta_j(b_i)\eta_j(b_{i'})\), \(i\ne i'\). These are the false-indicator polynomials of the bit collision clauses.

Working transfer lemma. A degree-\(d\) NS or PC refutation from the exact weak unary base, or its explicit functional strengthening, plus any leveled ENS family, maps to a refutation of \(\mathcal B_n\) plus the image ENS family through degree at most \(\ell d\). Every retained input is actually substituted; original companion/cofactor budgets are carried with the factor \(\ell\).

Base images. The partition identity

\[ \sum_j\eta_j(b_i)=\prod_{t=1}^{\ell}(b_{it}+(1-b_{it}))=1 \]

is an ordinary polynomial identity, so all row images are zero. A column collision maps to its bit-PHP generator, of degree \(2\ell\). Each Boolean image \(\eta_j^2-\eta_j\) has its domain certificate through \(2\ell\). For distinct labels \(j,k\), the product \(\eta_j\eta_k\) contains \(b_{it}(1-b_{it})\) at a differing bit, so an optional same-row exclusion has a Boolean certificate through \(2\ell\) as well.

Full proof transfer. Fix fresh coefficient variables under \(\Psi\). Every ENS companion maps exactly to the companion on the substituted inputs, and every coefficient field equation stays a field equation. The substitution has degree at most \(\ell\); every base image has an NS certificate through \(\ell\) times its original degree. Applying the original-cofactor transfer argument proves the NS bound. For PC, substitute each line and implement multiplication by an old cell as multiplication by its degree-\(\ell\) indicator polynomial; the intermediate products fit \(\ell d\). The target remains one.

This is a proof-degree transfer for algebraic systems. It does not preserve the linear-clause language or parity queries.

4a. The standard bit base does not inherit NS filtration stability

For two distinct pigeons \(i,i'\), sum their \(n=2^\ell\) collision axioms. In characteristic two, distributivity gives the exact ordinary identity

\[ \begin{aligned} \sum_j\eta_j(b_i)\eta_j(b_{i'}) &=\prod_{t=1}^{\ell} \bigl(b_{it}b_{i't}+(1-b_{it})(1-b_{i't})\bigr)\\ &=\prod_{t=1}^{\ell}(1+b_{it}+b_{i't}) =:E_{ii'}. \end{aligned} \]

Each displayed original collision axiom has degree \(2\ell\), whereas \(E_{ii'}\) has degree exactly \(\ell\). Consequently

\[ E_{ii'}\in\mathcal I_{2\ell}(\mathcal B_n) \cap\mathcal P_{\le\ell}, \qquad E_{ii'}\notin\mathcal I_\ell(\mathcal B_n). \]

Nonmembership proof. At ceiling \(\ell\), every degree-\(2\ell\) collision generator is inactive, so the NS space contains only Boolean-domain consequences. At the all-zero bit point these vanish, but \(E_{ii'}=1\). This proves the strict filtration failure, even though the sum uses only constant cofactors at its original ceiling. The same point defines a degree-\(\ell\) design that cannot extend to degree \(2\ell\).

The four exact cases \(\ell=1,2,3,4\) save the complete collision sums and separating points in the filtration-control output. This prevents transferring the unary functional base-stability theorem to this presentation without a new argument. Taking \(E_{ii'}\) as a primitive lower-degree axiom would be a different base, whose lower bound and source transfer must be checked.

5. Unary affine queries become a larger class of bit functions

Under this encoding an arbitrary unary affine form has the exact image

\[ a_0+\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}x_{ij} \quad\longmapsto\quad a_0+\sum_i f_i(b_i),\qquad f_i(b)=\sum_j a_{ij}\eta_j(b). \]

Each \(f_i\) can be any Boolean function of one pigeon label: the indicators give its truth-table expansion. Thus these are sums of arbitrary within-pigeon functions, not necessarily affine functions of the bits. In particular \(\eta_0(b)=\prod_t(1-b_t)\) has multilinear degree exactly \(\ell\), because the all-bits monomial has coefficient one. Uniqueness of multilinear Boolean normal form prevents an affine bit representation when \(\ell\ge2\).

The function space has dimension \(1+m(n-1)\): normalize each within-pigeon function to vanish at one fixed label, leaving one common constant. In an identically zero sum, independently varying one label forces its normalized function to vanish, proving independence of these parameters. Ordinary affine bit functions have dimension only \(1+m\ell\). This makes the difference explicit even after quotienting unary affine forms by their row relations.

The reverse label expression \(b_{it}=\sum_{j:j_t=1}x_{ij}\) is affine on one-hot rows. It does not make the forward map affine, nor is it an inverse on the weak row domain. For \(n=4\), the row \((1,1,1,0)\) has parity one but reconstructs label \(11\), whose indicator row is \((0,0,0,1)\). Functionality is essential to the usual label interpretation.

A further distinction is the cost of evaluating a whole flat. A deterministic parity decision tree computing the indicator of a consistent codimension-\(r\) affine flat needs depth at least \(r\), and querying a basis attains \(r\). For the lower bound, follow a point in that flat to a leaf outputting one. Its affine leaf must be contained in the flat, so the leaf's queried equations have rank at least \(r\). This only rules out treating an arbitrary source flat-value test as one cheap deterministic parity query; randomized approximation and other proof extractions require separate analysis.

6. An earlier pointwise query argument was independently rediscovered

Byramji–Impagliazzo, Remark A.4, already describes logarithmic parity search for a collision in a unary near-permutation. Our earlier design-valued attack independently reused that pointwise mechanism, with an explicit XOR-based height refinement and extension to every design with the specified first moments. The earlier proof remains valid; its pointwise idea should be attributed to the prior source. The claim index now records that relationship.

7. Checks and the remaining obligation

The compiled checker tests \(\ell=1,2,3,4\): all \(30\) indicator Booleanity certificates, \(155\) same-row exclusion certificates, \(30\) bit collision images, and eight complete ENS image blocks at accuracies one and two. It verifies the literal partition identity, the top multilinear coefficient of every selected query control, the weak-row inverse failure, and the zero-mean singleton example. All checks passed. The complete image certificates and controls are retained with reproduction and source metadata.

Verdict. None of the audited lower bounds currently closes the singleton or full-source obligation. A valid import needs an actual affine-clause/affine-DAG extraction, its native proof-depth bound, and a compatible input encoding. The algebraic bit map is valid but does not preserve affine query geometry; the unary pointwise extensibility hypothesis is absent after imposing the row coordinates.

The concrete next test is the compressed bit base with \(E_{ii'}\) as primitive equality axioms: verify a sufficient PC degree lower bound and the source connection to the original PHP target before adopting it. No NS filtration stability is assumed. Randomized evaluation of source values remains a separate possible route; the deterministic flat-query bound does not settle it.

Process assessment. The audit prevented an invalid theorem import and corrected an attribution; exact encoding and rule mismatches are now recorded, while general source coverage is unchanged, and no additional framework rule is needed.

13 September 2026 — A compact bit base retains the PHP degree barrier and the original source goal

Status: working auxiliary-base and source reductions over \(\mathbb F_2\), a transported stable consequence filtration, and exact local certificates. Full source-family elimination remains open; intrinsic NS stability of the compact bit base is not asserted.

Route obligation. Verify whether the smaller bit variable space is available without losing the original ordinary-PHP goal or its PC degree lower bound. The answer is yes for the explicitly defined compact base. The standard bit-base filtration counterexample is not bypassed: we supply a separate stable class by transport from the unary functional system.

1. Exact auxiliary system

Let \(n=2^\ell\), with \(\ell\ge2\), and take \(n+1\) pigeons, each with bits \(b_{it}\), \(1\le t\le\ell\). Define

\[ E_{ii'}(b)=\prod_{t=1}^{\ell}(1+b_{it}+b_{i't}),\qquad \mathcal Q_n=\{E_{ii'}:i<i'\} \cup\{b_{it}^2-b_{it}\}_{i,t}. \tag{CB-base} \]

Each \(E_{ii'}\), of original degree \(\ell\), is the equality indicator of two bit strings, so its equation zero asserts that they differ. This base has \((n+1)\ell\) variables and \(\binom{n+1}{2}\) collision generators. It is a different axiom presentation from the standard degree-\(2\ell\) bit base in the preceding audit.

We use the explicit functional unary base \(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}\) only to prove the required lower bound and construct a stable consequence class. Define an affine decoder

\[ \tau(b_{it})=s_{it}:=\sum_{j:\,j_t=1}x_{ij}, \]

where hole labels are the \(\ell\)-bit strings. Fresh ENS coefficients, when present, are fixed by \(\tau\).

2. Two functional rows have degree-complete state interpolation

For two distinct rows, let \(U\) contain their Boolean equations, same-row exclusions, and row sums minus one, but no cross-row collision equations. For every polynomial \(P\) in these two rows, of degree \(d\),

\[ P-\sum_{j,k}P(e_j,e_k)x_{ij}x_{i'k} \in\mathcal I_{\max\{d,2\}}(U). \tag{CB-interpolation} \]

Proof. Apply the monomial reduction behind the existing state-algebra lemma separately in each row. Powers reduce by Booleanity; a monomial involving two different cells from one row vanishes by its same-row exclusion. These operations preserve the original monomial degree. The remainder is a constant, linear terms in either row, and terms bilinear across the two rows.

Homogenize a linear term by the other row sum and a constant by both row sums. These changes have degree-two row-generator certificates; for example

\[ x_{ij}-x_{ij}\rho_{i'}=-x_{ij}(\rho_{i'}-1), \qquad 1-\rho_i\rho_{i'}=-(\rho_i-1)-\rho_i(\rho_{i'}-1). \]

The resulting bilinear coefficients are uniquely determined by evaluation at the one-hot pairs \((e_j,e_k)\), yielding (CB-interpolation). The maximum with two is needed even for a linear target. Functionality is an explicit hypothesis of this local interpolation.

3. The affine decoder preserves refutation degree

Apply (CB-interpolation) to \(P=\tau(E_{ii'})\). At \((e_j,e_k)\), the decoded bit strings are the labels \(j,k\), so \(P(e_j,e_k)=1\) exactly when \(j=k\). Since \(\deg P\le\ell\) and \(\ell\ge2\),

\[ \tau(E_{ii'})-\sum_jx_{ij}x_{i'j}\in \mathcal I_\ell(U). \]

Adding the old column-collision generators proves

\[ \tau(E_{ii'})\in\mathcal I_\ell(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}). \]

Bit Booleanity has the exact degree-two image certificate

\[ s_{it}^2-s_{it} =\sum_{j:j_t=1}(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij}). \]

Thus every primitive compact-base axiom image is certified through its original degree. The map is affine, so the original-cofactor transfer and PC substitution rule give

\[ \mathcal Q_n\vdash_{\rm NS/PC}^{d}1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}\vdash_{\rm NS/PC}^{d}1. \tag{CB-decoder-transfer} \]

The same assertion holds with any leveled ENS family attached, replacing every input by its actual decoder image and retaining all original activity budgets. This is a degree statement; no bound on monomial expansion size of the decoder certificates is required for the base lower bound.

Auxiliary PC lower bound. The audited functional-PHP bound therefore implies

\[ \deg_{\rm PC}(\mathcal Q_n)\ge n/2+1 \qquad(n=2^\ell,\ \ell\ge2). \tag{CB-PC-lower} \]

The small case \(n=2\) is deliberately excluded: its three linear compact equality axioms sum to one. The decoder image then needs degree two, as the finite control confirms.

4. A stable transported class, without assuming compact NS stability

The bit forms \(s_{it}\) are linearly independent as polynomials in the unary cells: in each row, columns whose labels are unit bit vectors isolate the individual bit coefficients. Complete these forms to a linear coordinate system. Consequently \(\tau\) is an injective ordinary polynomial-ring map and preserves every ordinary degree.

Define, on bit polynomials of degree at most \(k\),

\[ \mathcal J_k= \{f\in\mathbb F_2[b]_{\le k}: \tau(f)\in\mathcal I_k(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun})\}. \tag{CB-transport} \]

We have \(\mathcal I_k(\mathcal Q_n)\subseteq\mathcal J_k\) by the decoder image certificates. The family \(\mathcal J_k\) contains the bit Boolean consequences and is closed under multiplication within the allowed degree: if \(f\in\mathcal J_k\) and \(\deg q=t\), then \(qf\in\mathcal J_{k+t}\).

If \(0\le k\le B\) and \(n\ge2B-1\), degree preservation and unary functional filtration stability give

\[ \mathcal J_B\cap\mathbb F_2[b]_{\le k}=\mathcal J_k, \qquad \mathcal C_B(\mathcal Q_n)\subseteq\mathcal J_B. \tag{CB-stability} \]

For the first identity, transport \(f\) to the unary space, use its stability at the unchanged degree, and pull back the membership statement. For the second, replay a compact-base PC derivation under \(\tau\) and use unary \(\mathcal C_B=\mathcal I_B\). No equality between \(\mathcal J_B\) and the compact base's NS or PC space is inferred.

Every functional annihilating \(\mathcal J_k\) extends to one annihilating \(\mathcal J_B\). One proof uses finite-dimensional annihilator duality and (CB-stability). Equivalently, first extend it from the subspace \(\tau(\mathbb F_2[b]_{\le k})\) to a functional on the full unary quotient; extend that functional by unary stability, then restrict along \(\tau\). Normalization is preserved. For \(B\le n/2\), normalized such functionals exist because \(1\notin\mathcal J_B\).

This supplies a justified stable class of admissible old functionals in bit coordinates. The sufficiency construction of the singleton-to-pair module theorem can use \(\operatorname{Ann}\mathcal J_k\): its proof needs the extension property, Boolean certificates, and closure under allowed old multiplications, all established here. It remains necessary to solve the singleton equations in this class and handle the completed source degree range. Intrinsic NS filtration stability of \(\mathcal Q_n\) remains unproved.

5. The source connection preserves the original research target

Let \(C_{ii'}=\bigvee_{t=1}^{\ell}\mathrm{MOD}_{2,1}(b_{it},b_{i't})\), the linear clause saying that two bit strings differ, and let

\[ \Theta_n=\neg\bigwedge_{i<i'} C_{ii'}. \]

This compact bit-PHP tautology says that some pair among \(n+1\) labels is equal.

Boolean proof reduction. A size-\(S\), depth-\(d_{\rm F}\) ordinary-PHP Frege proof over the binary modular basis yields a proof of \(\Theta_n\) of size \(\operatorname{poly}(S,n)\) and depth \(d_{\rm F}+O(1)\). Substitute the Boolean label indicator for every incidence variable; this increases size by at most \(O(\ell)\) per occurrence and formula depth by a constant. Each substituted row disjunction is a tautology. For a fixed pigeon pair, the disjunction over common labels is equivalent to bitwise equality.

The needed equivalences have polynomial-size bounded-depth Frege proofs. Each row identity uses only \(\ell\) variables, and each pair identity only \(2\ell\). For completeness, a true constant-depth formula \(F\) on \(k\) variables has a guarded truth-table proof of size \(2^k(|F|+k)^{O(1)}\) and formula depth \(\operatorname{depth}(F)+O(1)\): under each complete assignment cube, evaluate its gates and derive the cube's implication to \(F\); eliminate opposite literal pairs from these implications as in the full assignment-clause resolution tree. The guards and accumulated clauses add only a constant number of connective layers. Here \(2^k\le n^2\). Replacing the row and pair expressions in their outer contexts and applying MP gives the stated proof reduction.

This does not use a Res(\(\oplus\)) proof translation or claim that proof height equals formula depth. Balance the resulting Frege proof only afterward, using the already audited source balancing step.

Compact source boundary. In the TRUE-by-zero approximation, a child \(\mathrm{MOD}_{2,1}(b_{it},b_{i't})\) has value \(1+b_{it}+b_{i't}\), so the clause block \(C_{ii'}\) has affine inputs

\[ g_t=b_{it}+b_{i't}. \]

Choose \(h\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil\). Pair these inputs in coefficient rows using \(1,1-g_s\); any unpaired input uses coefficient one, and spare rows are zero. The clause product becomes exactly \(E_{ii'}\). Every companion image has the explicit certificate

\[ g_tE_{ii'}=-(g_t^2-g_t)\prod_{s\ne t}(1-g_s), \]

of NS degree \(\ell+1\le2h+1\), using the two bit Booleanity equations for \(g_t^2-g_t\). Nonconstant coefficient images are affine and their field witnesses fit degree two. These are the original clause-companion and field budgets.

Set the final PHP block's coefficient vectors to zero. Its product becomes one and its companion images are the primitive \(E_{ii'}\)'s, of degree \(\ell\le2h^2+3h\), within the original boundary-companion ceiling. This is one global affine coefficient substitution; all later inputs and all cofactors change with it.

The binary modular source theorem now gives an NS refutation of \(\mathcal Q_n\) plus a valid leveled ENS family through

\[ D_{\rm bit}\le(C+H_\pi)L,\qquad C=\max\{M_{\rm fr}+2,12\},\qquad L=(d+1)h^d, \]

where \(d\le d_{\rm F}+O(1)\), \(H_\pi=O(\log\operatorname{poly}(S,n))\), and the companion inventory is polynomial in \(S,n,h\). For \(h=O(\log n)\) satisfying the packing threshold and \(S\le n^K\), the degree is polylogarithmic. The original level-one inputs are affine in the bit variables; later specialized inputs need not be affine. A removed clause value has degree \(\ell\), so the earlier unary old-degree-two value profile must not be reused unchanged.

For an original board size not a power of two, first fix a matching leaving \(n=2^{\lfloor\log_2 N\rfloor}\) holes and \(n+1\) pigeons. Constant substitution and Boolean simplification give the corresponding ordinary PHP proof with polynomial size and constant depth overhead; \(N<2n\). Hence sufficient lower bounds along this compact auxiliary route would still prove the original ordinary-PHP target for all large board sizes. This is an auxiliary reduction, not abandonment of that target.

6. Exact checks and what remains open

The compiled checker preserves \(38\) complete local NS certificates. For \(\ell=1,2,3,4\), it verifies the two-row decoder image, every decoder bit-Booleanity image, all packed clause companions, and every nonzero coefficient-field image. The equality decoder uses respectively \(4,14,60,250\) axiom multiples at degrees \(2,2,3,4\). The \(\ell=1\) case is the explicit exceptional algebraic control, not part of the same-degree lower-bound theorem or a claim of genuine unary-OR source syntax.

This is a two-row control, not a satisfying assignment of the full \(n+1\)-pigeon system.

The reproduction record explains the complete interpolation, decoder, and source-image certificates. All checks passed. No hypothetical Frege proof was instantiated, no whole PHP lower bound was computed, and no equality \(\mathcal J_k=\mathcal I_k(\mathcal Q_n)\) was tested.

Outcome. The binary source can be studied on \((n+1)\log_2n\) old variables with the same \(n/2+1\) PC barrier and a justified stable transported class. General ENS elimination and the source's singleton compatibility remain open. 13 September 2026 — The transported bit subring has no extra quadratic relations at eight or more labels

Status: an exact quadratic description of the transported consequence class, an unconditional first-boundary result for one-level affine-bit ENS families, and complete finite quotient certificates. Higher-degree and multilevel source coverage remain open.

Route obligation. Test the actual binary affine source family, rather than assume a quotient dimension. The compact-bit decoder makes its quadratic relations rigid enough to verify the earlier pair-faithfulness hypothesis for every such pair. The resulting application has the explicit ceiling \(3h+1\), not the completed source degree.

1. Exact quadratic rigidity for \(\ell\ge3\)

Use the transported class \(\mathcal J_k=\{f:\deg f\le k,\ \tau f\in\mathcal I_k(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun})\}\), with \(n=2^\ell\), \(n+1\) pigeons, and \(\tau(b_{it})=\sum_{j:j_t=1}x_{ij}\). Let \({\rm BOOL}_b\) denote the bit Booleanity equations.

Working theorem. For \(\ell\ge3\),

\[ \boxed{\mathcal J_2=\mathcal I_2({\rm BOOL}_b).} \tag{BQ-rigidity} \]

Thus the whole Boolean quadratic space in the \((n+1)\ell\) bit variables injects into the unary functional-PHP degree-two quotient. This is stronger than checking a finite collection of input pairs.

Proof. First Boolean-reduce a bit polynomial \(q\) through degree two. Decoder images of the bit Booleanity equations have old certificates through degree two, so this preserves membership in \(\mathcal J_2\). Write the resulting multilinear polynomial as

\[ q=c+\sum_i A_i(b_i) +\sum_{i<i'}b_i^{\mathsf T}M_{ii'}b_{i'}, \]

where each \(A_i\) has degree at most two, uses only one pigeon's bits, and has zero constant term. The \(M_{ii'}\) are arbitrary \(\ell\times\ell\) binary matrices.

Suppose \(\tau q\in\mathcal I_2(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun})\). On a fixed pair of distinct pigeon rows, the coefficient of the legal matching monomial \(x_{ij}x_{i'k}\), \(j\ne k\), is \(j^{\mathsf T}M_{ii'}k\), using the binary labels as vectors. The recorded NS rectangle argument therefore gives

\[ (j+j')^{\mathsf T}M_{ii'}(k+k')=0 \]

whenever the four hole labels are pairwise distinct. This uses only original degree-two NS multiples; it is not a PC-closure inference.

Fix any nonzero bit directions \(a,b\). Choose \(j=0,j'=a\), and choose \(k\) outside \(\{0,a,b,a+b\}\); then put \(k'=k+b\). At \(n\ge8\) such a label exists, and the four labels are distinct. Hence \(a^{\mathsf T}M_{ii'}b=0\) for all nonzero \(a,b\). Taking unit vectors proves \(M_{ii'}=0\) for every row pair.

The remaining \(\tau A_i\) reduces within its functional row, through degree two, to \(\sum_jA_i(j)x_{ij}\), by the state reduction. Thus

\[ c+\sum_{i,j}A_i(j)x_{ij} \in\mathcal I_2(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}) \cap\mathcal P_{\le1} =\mathcal I_1(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}). \]

The last equality is old base stability. The only old affine consequences are the row-generator span, so each \(A_i(j)\) is constant in \(j\). Since \(A_i(0)=0\), every such value is zero. Uniqueness of multilinear Boolean representation gives \(A_i=0\), and the constant term is also zero. Therefore the reduced \(q\) vanishes. The reverse inclusion follows from the decoder Booleanity certificates, proving (BQ-rigidity).

2. Four labels give exactly the compact equality relations

For \(\ell=2,n=4\), the corresponding exact statement is

\[ \mathcal J_2= \mathcal I_2({\rm BOOL}_b) +\operatorname{span}\{E_{ii'}:i<i'\}. \tag{BQ-four-labels} \]

Proof. A partition of the four labels into two disjoint pairs has the same nonzero difference in both pairs. Every nonzero direction occurs. The rectangle conditions give \(a^{\mathsf T}Ma=0\) for all \(a\), so a two-by-two cross-row matrix must be a scalar multiple of

\[ \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}. \]

The degree-two equality indicator \(E_{ii'}=(1+b_{i0}+b_{i'0})(1+b_{i1}+b_{i'1})\) has exactly this cross-row matrix, and its decoder image lies in the old degree-two NS space by the compact-base image proof. Subtract the corresponding multiple of \(E_{ii'}\) for each pair. No cross-row terms remain, and the one-row argument above finishes. These equality classes are independent modulo bit Booleanity because their cross-row matrices occur on distinct pigeon pairs.

This is a genuine boundary control for the quadratic statement. It is not a failure of the \(\ell\ge3\) theorem, and its rank-two equality tuples are below the usual source packing threshold when \(h\ge1\).

3. All one-level affine-bit families satisfy the first-boundary hypothesis

Let \(n=2^\ell\ge8\), let \(h\ge1\), put \(D=3h+1\), and suppose \(n\ge2D-1=6h+1\). Take any finite one-level ENS family of common accuracy \(h\), with affine bit inputs and complete companions and fields. There is no family-count restriction.

Corollary. Every normalized old functional annihilating \(\mathcal J_D\) extends to an ordinary degree-\(D\) design for this compact-bit augmented system. Unnormalized functionals extend with their value on one unchanged. Consequently there is no NS refutation through \(D\), and more generally

\[ \mathcal I_D(\mathcal Q_n\cup\mathcal E\cup\mathcal R) \cap\mathbb F_2[b]_{\le D} \subseteq\mathcal J_D. \tag{BQ-first-boundary} \]

The conclusion is not containment in \(\mathcal C_D(\mathcal Q_n)\), which may be smaller than \(\mathcal J_D\), and is not a transfer for augmented PC proofs.

Proof. Remove zero/unit input-span cases by their scalar coefficient specializations; these preserve degree and old targets. Apply the affine decoder to the rest. The old system is now the unary functional base, and every input remains affine with the same span relationships. Ordinary and Boolean bit polynomials both embed under the decoder: its full-rank linear map is surjective on Boolean assignments, so it introduces no new Boolean relation among the bits.

For any two input blocks, a Boolean quadratic relation between their input products which vanishes in the old \(\mathcal I_{h+1}\) quotient already vanishes in \(\mathcal I_2\), by old stability. Equation (BQ-rigidity) then says that it was a Boolean identity to begin with. This proves the faithful-pair theorem's hypothesis for every pair, regardless of overlap or nesting. Equal-span cases use that theorem's shared feasible scalar, or may first be canonically shared.

The earlier theorem now transfers every old NS consequence in the decoded augmented system into unary \(\mathcal C_D=\mathcal I_D\), giving (BQ-first-boundary). Finite-dimensional extension duality gives the claimed extension of any old annihilator of \(\mathcal J_D\). Alternatively lift that old functional to the unary quotient, use the constructive faithful-pair extension, and restrict back along the decoder. Scalar-removed blocks are restored by composing with their constant specialization. Normalized old functionals exist, so a refutation is excluded.

Actual source scope. The compact source bridge has affine original-level-one bit inputs. Its choice \(h\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) makes the compact base axioms active in this band, so the statement is not merely an inactive-axiom observation. For example \(n=16,\ell=4,h=2,D=7\) meets every condition. However, a completed source proof has additional levels and a degree bound not shown to be \(3h+1\). The proper-OR module witness of degree \(6h\) is outside this band. No full-source lower bound follows by silently discarding those features.

4. Complete quotient computations and process assessment

The checker builds the full degree-two unary functional NS quotient after Boolean, row-exclusion, and column-exclusion monomial reduction. It includes every row-generator multiple with an affine monomial cofactor. It then maps every Boolean bit monomial of degree at most two, retaining complete base-reduction traces, image-basis traces, and a full kernel basis.

These are complete NS quotient calculations, not samples or floating-point rank estimates; no augmented PC closure or full joint moment array was computed.
