13 September 2026 — The first transported bit relation has degree exactly the bit width

Status: working general proof and complete finite geometric checks; extension of the preceding quadratic theorem, not a completed ENS elimination theorem.

Route obligation and stopping point. The actual compact-bit source needs compatible extension moments over its stable old class \(\mathcal J\). The preceding quadratic result removed one source-faithfulness hypothesis. This turn tests its proposed generalization below \(\ell=\log_2n\), stopping at a proof or a failure of the coefficient argument. The initial cube idea was sketched in the preceding cycle; this entry develops and checks it.

1. Disjoint coordinate cubes below the total dimension threshold

Lemma. Let \(T_1,\ldots,T_t\) be nonempty subsets of \([\ell]\), put \(d_i=|T_i|\), and suppose \(e=\sum_i d_i<\ell\). Write \(W_i\subseteq\mathbb F_2^\ell\) for the coordinate subspace with axes \(T_i\). There are translates \(C_i=a_i+W_i\) that are pairwise disjoint.

Proof. Choose the translates greedily. There are \(2^{\ell-d_i}\) cosets of \(W_i\). Each previously occupied point forbids at most one coset, so the number of forbidden cosets is at most \(\sum_{j<i}2^{d_j}\). For positive integers \(a,b\), \(2^a+2^b\le2^{a+b}\). Thus, if any earlier cube exists,

\[ \sum_{j<i}2^{d_j} \le2^{\sum_{j<i}d_j} <2^{\ell-d_i}. \]

A free coset exists at each step; the first step has no exclusions. This proves the lemma.

Sharpness of the universal hypothesis. At \(e=\ell\), take \(T_1=\{1\}\) and \(T_2=\{2,\ldots,\ell\}\). The two subspaces are complementary. Every pair of their cosets meets in exactly one point, so a disjoint choice is impossible. This is a boundary counterexample, not a claim that every family of total dimension \(\ell\) fails.

2. No non-Boolean transported relation below \(\ell\)

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\), with \(n=2^\ell,\ \ell\ge2\), \(n+1\) pigeons, and bit variables \(b_{it}\). Use the affine decoder and transported class

\[ \tau(b_{it})=\sum_{z\in\mathbb F_2^\ell:z_t=1}x_{iz}, \qquad \mathcal J_d=\{f:\deg f\le d,\ \tau f\in\mathcal I_d(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun})\}. \]

Working theorem. For every \(0\le d<\ell\),

\[ \boxed{\mathcal J_d=\mathcal I_d({\rm BOOL}_b).} \tag{BL-rigidity} \]

Consequently the quotient has dimension \(\sum_{j=0}^d\binom{(n+1)\ell}{j}\). These are ordinary polynomial degrees and original NS consequence spaces; no augmented PC closure is used.

Boolean reduction and row support. Take \(f\in\mathcal J_d\). A bit Booleanity image is a sum of unary Booleanity generators through degree two. Multiplying these certificates shows that reducing \(f\) to its multilinear bit representative preserves membership in \(\mathcal J_d\) and costs at most \(d\). Write that representative uniquely as

\[ f=c+\sum_{\varnothing\ne S}F_S((b_i)_{i\in S}), \]

where each monomial of \(F_S\) uses at least one bit of every row in \(S\), and uses no other row. Assume some \(F_S\ne0\), and let \(t\) be the maximum such \(|S|\); then \(1\le t\le d\).

Reduce \(\tau f\) using unary Booleanity and same-row/column exclusions, leaving its matching-monomial normal form \(R\). This reduction has a certificate through the original degree \(d\). Within one occupied row, a nonempty bit monomial with axes \(T\) reduces to

\[ \prod_{a\in T}\tau(b_{ia}) \equiv\sum_z\left(\prod_{a\in T}z_a\right)x_{iz}. \]

Thus reduction preserves the occupied row set unless a repeated column kills the monomial. In particular \(\deg R\le t\), and, on any \(t\)-row set \(S\), the coefficient of the legal matching \(\prod_{i\in S}x_{i,z_i}\) is exactly \(F_S((z_i)_{i\in S})\). Because \(\tau f-R\in\mathcal I_d\), we have \(R\in\mathcal I_d\). The board condition \(n\ge2d-1\) is automatic from \(d<\ell\), so functional-base stability yields

\[ R\in\mathcal I_d\cap\mathcal P_{\le t}=\mathcal I_t. \]

Top coefficients of an original degree-\(t\) NS certificate. In matching normal form, Booleanity and exclusion multiples are zero. A row equation \(\rho_i-1\) times a matching on an already occupied row also reduces to zero. On a matching \(T\) avoiding row \(i\), it reduces to the sum of its legal one-cell extensions in row \(i\), minus \(T\). Since the cofactor degree is at most \(t-1\), the top coefficient on \(S\) can therefore only have the form

\[ F_S((z_i)_{i\in S}) =\sum_{i\in S}\psi_i((z_j)_{j\in S\setminus\{i\}}) \quad\text{for pairwise distinct labels }z_i. \tag{BL-top} \]

Here the functions \(\psi_i\) are unrestricted on legal \((t-1)\)-matchings. Arbitrary original cofactors give the same description after their matching reduction. The drop from \(\mathcal I_d\) to \(\mathcal I_t\) is essential: otherwise higher-degree row cofactors could contribute through their negative terms.

Isolate a leading bit monomial. Fix a nonzero \(F_S\) with \(|S|=t\), and choose a monomial of maximum total degree \(e\) in it. Let \(T_i\ne\varnothing\) be its bit axes in each row. Then \(\sum_i|T_i|=e\le d<\ell\). By the cube lemma, choose disjoint \(C_i=a_i+W_i\) with these axes. Every tuple in \(\prod_{i\in S}C_i\) has distinct labels, so sum (BL-top) over this product in \(\mathbb F_2\).

Every term on the right vanishes: \(\psi_i\) omits row \(i\), and \(|C_i|=2^{|T_i|}\) is even. On the left, this sum is the mixed finite difference in the selected \(e\) bit coordinates. A monomial missing a selected bit vanishes under that sum. A monomial containing all selected bits has degree at least \(e\), and maximality of \(e\) leaves only the chosen monomial itself. Its coefficient is one, and its sum is one. We obtain \(1=0\), a contradiction.

No nonconstant \(F_S\) remains. If \(f=c\), then \(c\in\mathcal I_d\cap\mathcal P_{\le0}=\mathcal I_0=0\), again by old stability; at \(d=0\) this is immediate. The multilinear representative is therefore zero, proving \(\mathcal J_d\subseteq\mathcal I_d({\rm BOOL}_b)\). Decoder Booleanity certificates give the converse and complete the proof. The dimension formula follows from the squarefree bit-monomial basis.

3. Exact first relation degree and bounded-PC consequences

The compact equality polynomial

\[ E_{ii'}=\prod_{a=1}^{\ell}(1+b_{ia}+b_{i'a}) \]

has degree exactly \(\ell\), belongs to \(\mathcal J_\ell\) by its decoder image certificate, and is not a Booleanity consequence: it evaluates to one when both rows' bits are zero. Hence the first degree with a non-Boolean member of \(\mathcal J\) is exactly \(\ell\). This extends the four-label boundary; it does not classify all relations at degree \(\ell\).

For \(d<\ell\) and \(d\le B\le n/2\), we also obtain

\[ \mathcal C_B(\mathcal Q_n)\cap\mathcal P_{\le d} =\mathcal I_B(\mathcal Q_n)\cap\mathcal P_{\le d} =\mathcal I_d({\rm BOOL}_b). \tag{BL-old} \]

Indeed, \(\mathcal C_B(\mathcal Q_n)\subseteq\mathcal J_B\), and stability restricts \(\mathcal J_B\) to \(\mathcal J_d\), now identified by (BL-rigidity). The reverse inclusion is supplied by the bit Booleanity generators themselves. This is a low-degree intersection theorem, not an equality of the full compact NS and PC spaces at degree \(B\).

4. Complete finite checks and route assessment

The new compiled coordinate-cube checker enumerates every ordered nonempty family of coordinate-axis sets with total dimension below \(\ell\), for \(2\le\ell\le6\). It saves the deterministic greedy cosets and all cube points, checks every product tuple for distinct labels, evaluates the selected leading monomial's mixed difference, and checks every point-indicator basis function of every missing-row potential. This tests the geometric and coefficient-dual step; it does not construct full higher-degree PHP quotient matrices.

13 September 2026 — Coherent low moments extend the affine-bit family range

Status: working unconditional one-level NS extension theorem in the stated degree band; exact finite mixed-moment checks on a Boolean model, not a finite PHP quotient computation.

Route obligation and stopping point. Apply the new bit rigidity theorem to an actual source-family hypothesis: simultaneous affine-block compatibility. The question is whether it improves the first-boundary theorem at \(3h+1\), with nonempty parameters after compact-clause packing. This turn stops at a proved extension range and an explicit account of its next obstruction.

1. The enlarged ordinary-NS extension theorem

Over \(\mathbb F_2\), take the compact base \(\mathcal Q_n\), \(n=2^\ell,\ \ell\ge2\), and the transported class \(\mathcal J\). Let \(\mathcal E\) be any finite one-level family with nonconstant affine bit inputs \(g_{a,j}\), disjoint fresh own coefficient variables, all companions, all coefficient Boolean equations \(\mathcal R\), and common accuracy \(h\). Retain original companion degree \(2h+1\). Zero or scalar inputs may first undergo the already justified scalar cleanup.

Working theorem. Suppose

\[ D=3h+u,\qquad 1\le u\le h,\qquad h+u+1<\ell,\qquad n\ge2D-1. \tag{COH-range} \]

Every linear functional \(\lambda\) on old \(\mathcal P_{\le D}\) annihilating \(\mathcal J_D\) extends to a functional annihilating \(\mathcal I_D(\mathcal Q_n\cup\mathcal E\cup\mathcal R)\), with unchanged old values. In particular normalized old functionals extend to ordinary degree-\(D\) designs, and

\[ \mathcal I_D(\mathcal Q_n\cup\mathcal E\cup\mathcal R) \cap\mathbb F_2[b]_{\le D} \subseteq\mathcal J_D. \tag{COH-transfer} \]

There is no block-count, fan-in, rank-separation, or equal-span hypothesis. This is an augmented NS statement. It does not put every old consequence in the compact base's own PC space, and it does not transfer augmented PC derivations.

2. Couple the supported singletons while prescribing coherent low moments

Set \(L=2h+u\) and \(H=h+u\), as in the first mixed-band equations. The required singleton domains are \(\mathcal P_{\le L}\), pair domains are \(\mathcal P_{\le H}\), and no component on three or more blocks is forced by a companion cofactor.

Because \(\lambda\) annihilates old Booleanity consequences, it factors through the degree-\(D\) part of the full Boolean function algebra

\[ \mathcal B=\mathbb F_2[b]/\langle b_v^2-b_v\rangle. \]

Extend it arbitrarily to one linear functional \(\widehat\lambda\) on all of \(\mathcal B\). This is finite-dimensional linear extension. It asserts neither positivity nor an extension annihilating the full PHP ideal.

For each block, order its inputs and use the pointwise first-success functions

\[ s_{a,j}=g_{a,j}\prod_{k<j}(1-g_{a,k}),\qquad \chi_a=\sum_j s_{a,j}. \]

In \(\mathcal B\), \(s_{a,j}g_{a,j}=s_{a,j}\), and \(\chi_a\) is one exactly where some input is nonzero. These functions may have large degree. They only prescribe finite-dimensional functional values; they are not substitutions or bounded-degree NS cofactors.

For each block seek functionals \(\nu_{a,j}\in\operatorname{Ann}\mathcal J_{L+1}\) satisfying both

\[ \sum_j\nu_{a,j}(Gg_{a,j})=\lambda(G), \quad G\in U_a^{(H)} :=\left\{\sum_i q_i g_{a,i}:\deg q_i\le H-1\right\}, \tag{COH-root} \]
\[ \nu_{a,j}(T)=\widehat\lambda(s_{a,j}T) \quad(\deg T\le u+1). \tag{COH-low} \]

Consistency proof. By finite-dimensional linear separation, the only possible obstruction is a choice of \(G\in U_a^{(H)}\) and \(T_j\in\mathcal P_{\le u+1}\) for which every

\[ Gg_{a,j}+T_j\in\mathcal J_{L+1}, \]

but \(\lambda(G)+\sum_j\widehat\lambda(s_{a,j}T_j)\ne0\). Each displayed polynomial has degree at most \(H+1<\ell\). Stability through \(D\), followed by bit rigidity, makes it a Booleanity consequence. Hence \(T_j=Gg_{a,j}\) in \(\mathcal B\), and

\[ \sum_j\widehat\lambda(s_{a,j}T_j) =\widehat\lambda\!\left(G\sum_j s_{a,j}g_{a,j}\right) =\widehat\lambda(G\chi_a) =\widehat\lambda(G) =\lambda(G). \]

The third equality holds because \(G\) is in the input ideal and vanishes wherever all inputs vanish. The last uses \(\deg G\le H\le D\). The obstruction's prescribed value is therefore zero, so all \(\nu_{a,j}\) exist. This argument uses the same \(\widehat\lambda\) for every block.

Define the supported singletons

\[ \mu_{a,j}(P)=\nu_{a,j}(g_{a,j}P) \quad(\deg P\le L). \]

Multiplication closure of \(\mathcal J\) makes them annihilate \(\mathcal J_L\). Equation (COH-low) also gives their common low prescription

\[ \mu_{a,j}(P)=\widehat\lambda(s_{a,j}P) \quad(\deg P\le u). \tag{COH-single-low} \]

For \(\deg q\le H-1\), Boolean reduction of \(g_{a,j}^2\) to \(g_{a,j}\) and (COH-root) prove the required root equation \(\lambda(qg_{a,i})=\sum_j\mu_{a,j}(qg_{a,i}g_{a,j})\). Its Booleanity certificate costs at most \(H+2\le L+1\). The own-block equation \(\mu_{a,j}(qg_{a,i}(1-g_{a,j}))=0\), for \(\deg q\le u-1\), follows from the support factor \(g_{a,j}(1-g_{a,j})\), at degree at most \(u+2\le L+1\).

3. Extend every pair from the same Boolean functional

For every unordered pair \(a<b\) and input indices \(j,k\), prescribe

\[ \phi_{ab,jk}(P) =\widehat\lambda(s_{a,j}s_{b,k}P) \quad(\deg P\le u+1). \tag{COH-pair-low} \]

Here \(\mathcal J_{u+1}\) consists only of Booleanity consequences, so the prescription annihilates it. Transported stability extends this functional to \(\operatorname{Ann}\mathcal J_H\). Different pair components have separate unknowns and can be extended independently.

For every \(\deg q\le u-1\), all products below are in the prescribed range. Thus

\[ \begin{aligned} \sum_k\phi_{ab,jk}(qg_{b,i}g_{b,k}) &=\widehat\lambda\!\left( s_{a,j}qg_{b,i}\sum_k s_{b,k}g_{b,k}\right)\\ &=\widehat\lambda(s_{a,j}qg_{b,i}) =\mu_{a,j}(qg_{b,i}). \end{aligned} \]

The other cross equation follows by interchanging the blocks. No independence of the input spans is needed, including when spans coincide but use different bases.

Assemble the old root, these singletons and pairs, and zero higher components with the historical diagonal mixed-system construction:

\[ \Lambda(P)=\lambda(P(b,0)) +\sum_{a,j}\mu_{a,j}(T_{a,j}P) +\sum_{a<b}\sum_{j,k}\phi_{ab,jk}(T_{ab,jk}P). \]

The coefficient operators remove at least \(h\) degrees per selected block. Old axiom multiples are annihilated because \(\mathcal I_k(\mathcal Q_n)\subseteq\mathcal J_k\); coefficient Booleanity reduces to zero. Root, own-block, and cross equations cover all companion cofactors: their degree is at most \(H-1<2h\), and the next complete-block range is \(D-(2h+1)-2h=u-h-1<0\). This proves the extension assertion. Old values, including normalization, are unchanged. Applying the construction to every, also unnormalized, annihilator of \(\mathcal J_D\) and using duality proves (COH-transfer).

4. Source parameters, the next kernel, and the remaining gap

The actual compact source bridge allows clause packing at \(h\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil\). In the present range,

\[ 1\le u\le\min\{h,\ell-h-2\}. \]

At \(h=\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), this reaches \(D=4h-2\) when \(\ell=2h\), and \(D=4h-3\) when \(\ell=2h-1\), provided the interval is nonempty. A strict improvement over \(3h+1\) begins at \(\ell=8\): \(n=256,\ h=4,\ u=2,\ D=14\) satisfies every hypothesis. The theorem includes retained proper affine blocks of rank greater than \(2h\), with arbitrary intersections and polynomial or larger inventory; low-rank packing is not its explanation.

At \(H+1=\ell\), a consistency relation \(Gg_{a,j}+T_j\in\mathcal J_{L+1}\) may be non-Boolean. The replacement \(T_j=Gg_{a,j}\) in the full Boolean algebra is then no longer justified. The compact equality witnesses show that non-Boolean relations are present at exactly that degree. They do not by themselves prove an incompatible singleton kernel for a source block.

The source theorem supplies the completed bound \(D_{\rm bit}\le(C+H_\pi)(d+1)h^d\), not a bound in this short mixed band. Later inputs may also use earlier selectors. Consequently the full source-family obligation is still open. A family-count-independent theorem at arbitrary degree is already ruled out by the assignment-tree control; the current theorem does not contradict it.

5. Exact tests with overlapping retained-rank blocks

The new compiled checker uses six old Boolean variables, three blocks of accuracy \(h=2\), \(u=2\), \(D=8\), and the input tuples

\[ \begin{aligned} G_A&=(y_0,y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4),\\ G_B&=(1+y_0,y_1,y_2,y_3,y_5),\\ G_C&=(y_0+y_1,y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4). \end{aligned} \]

All have affine rank five, exceeding \(2h=4\); \(A,C\) have the same span in different bases, and \(B\) overlaps them. The old system is only Booleanity, a satisfiable finite model, not \(\mathcal Q_n\). The normalized old functional is \({\rm ev}_0+{\rm ev}_{e_0}+{\rm ev}_{e_1}\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), and is not multiplicative.

Starting with first-success prescriptions, the test changes selected degree-six moments of \(\nu\), above the root-product degree five, and selected degree-four pair moments, above the prescribed cross-product degree three. Thirteen supported singleton moments and 38 pair moments actually change. Thus the tested joint functional uses freedom in the extensions rather than merely reproducing the full pointwise prescriptions.

There are 36 total variables. The program checks all \(1+36+\binom{36}{2}+\binom{36}{3}=7,807\) squarefree cofactors through original degree \(D-(2h+1)=3\), against all 15 companions: 117,105 checks, all zero. Because the functional is defined on the full Boolean quotient, all field-axiom multiples vanish identically, and arbitrary powered cofactors reduce to this enumeration without increasing degree. The original companion ceiling remains five throughout.

One deliberately corrupted low pair value produces a recorded companion violation. With the unperturbed pointwise singleton/pair prescriptions but zero triples, five of 375 complete-two-foreign-block controls violate a companion at original degree \(4h+1=9\). This is failure of the truncated construction; the finite Boolean model still has satisfying extensions. It is not a PHP lower bound or a counterexample inside (COH-range).

The encoding and reproduction record, complete moments and equation checks, and provenance retain all evidence.

What changed. The rigidity theorem now discharges simultaneous singleton/pair compatibility for the entire one-level affine-bit family in a larger, nonempty source-parameter range. Higher-degree kernels and the completed multilevel endpoint remain unproved.

13 September 2026 — The first non-Boolean bit layer consists exactly of pair equalities

Status: working boundary classification and exact coefficient-space checks; a failed greedy placement is retained and repaired by an explicit exceptional construction.

Route obligation and stopping point. The coherent singleton construction first allows non-Boolean consistency kernels when \(h+u+1=\ell\). This turn identifies the entire transported relation space at that degree and states the exact residual left in the compatibility proof. It does not claim that such a kernel exists for a retained source input.

1. Critical coordinate cubes: the only obstruction uses two complementary axis sets

Lemma. Let nonempty coordinate-axis sets \(T_1,\ldots,T_t\subseteq[\ell]\) have \(\sum_i|T_i|=\ell\). Their coordinate subspaces admit pairwise disjoint cosets unless \(t=2\) and \(T_1,T_2\) partition \([\ell]\). In that exceptional case every pair of cosets meets exactly once.

Proof. One cube is immediate. For two cubes, overlapping axes leave a coordinate outside their union; translating one cube along that coordinate separates them. Disjoint axes at the stated total dimension are complementary, giving the asserted obstruction.

For \(t\ge3\), all stages before the last have total dimension below \(\ell\), so the previous greedy argument applies. At the last stage it still works whenever

\[ \sum_{j<t}2^{d_j}<2^{\sum_{j<t}d_j}, \qquad d_j=|T_j|. \]

This is strict with at least three earlier positive dimensions, or with two earlier dimensions when at least one exceeds one. For \(t=3\), put any dimension exceeding one among the first two. Only \(t=\ell=3\), with all three dimensions one, remains.

Write the three coordinate directions as unit vectors. If all directions equal \(a\), use coset representatives \(0,b,c\), where \(b,c\) are the other coordinate directions. If direction \(a\) occurs twice and \(b\) once, use \(W_a,\ b+W_a,\ c+W_b\), where \(c\) is the remaining direction. If all directions \(a,b,c\) are distinct, use \(W_a,\ c+W_b,\ a+b+W_c\). These displayed pairs of points are disjoint; reorder them to match the original input order. This completes the proof.

Failed placement retained. The first implementation used greedy placement even in this last case. For axes \((\{1\},\{1\},\{3\})\), its first two cubes filled the first-two-coordinate plane and met every coset of the last direction. This refutes that greedy choice, not existence of disjoint translates. The explicit repeated-direction construction repairs it.

2. A degree-\(\ell\) function supported on equal labels is a scalar equality indicator

Lemma. A Boolean polynomial function \(K(z,w)\) on two \(\ell\)-bit labels, of multilinear degree at most \(\ell\), that vanishes whenever \(z\ne w\), is a scalar multiple of \(E(z,w)=\prod_t(1+z_t+w_t)\).

Proof. Change Boolean coordinates to \(v=z,\ y=z+w\). An invertible linear Boolean change preserves the degree filtration: substitution and multilinear reduction do not increase degree, and the inverse gives the reverse inequality. In the new coordinates, \(K\) is supported on \(y=0\), so uniqueness of Boolean function representation gives

\[ K(v,y)=\prod_{t=1}^{\ell}(1+y_t)\,A(v). \]

For nonzero \(A\), the two variable sets are disjoint and the displayed degree is exactly \(\ell+\deg A\). Thus \(A\) is constant. This is a Boolean function classification; it does not claim an NS certificate for an arbitrary coordinate change.

Two-row potential consequence. Suppose \(F(z,w)\) has degree at most \(\ell\), every monomial uses both rows, and \(F(z,w)=a(z)+b(w)\) for \(z\ne w\). Set \(\delta_0(z)=\prod_t(1+z_t)\). Since \(F(z,0)=F(0,w)=0\), the potential equations give \(a(z)=b(0)\) for \(z\ne0\) and \(b(w)=a(0)\) for \(w\ne0\). For \(c=a(0)+b(0)\),

\[ K=F+c(1+\delta_0(z)+\delta_0(w)) \]

is supported on \(z=w\) and has degree at most \(\ell\). The lemma makes it a scalar equality indicator; evaluating at \(z=w=0\) identifies that scalar as \(c\). Consequently

\[ F=c\bigl(E+1+\delta_0(z)+\delta_0(w)\bigr). \tag{FIRST-pair} \]

The expression in parentheses is exactly the part of \(E\) whose monomials use both rows.

3. Exact transported and intrinsic consequences through the first collision degree

Working theorem. For \(n=2^\ell,\ \ell\ge2\),

\[ \boxed{\mathcal J_\ell =\mathcal I_\ell({\rm BOOL}_b) +\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_2}\{E_{ii'}:i<i'\} =\mathcal I_\ell(\mathcal Q_n).} \tag{FIRST-classification} \]

The equality classes are linearly independent modulo Booleanity. For \(\ell\le B\le n/2\),

\[ \mathcal C_B(\mathcal Q_n)\cap\mathcal P_{\le\ell} =\mathcal I_B(\mathcal Q_n)\cap\mathcal P_{\le\ell} =\mathcal I_\ell(\mathcal Q_n). \tag{FIRST-intersection} \]

Proof. Boolean-reduce \(f\in\mathcal J_\ell\), and use the row-support decomposition \(c+\sum_S F_S\) from the previous rigidity proof. Matching normalization and functional-base stability again put its old normal form in \(\mathcal I_t\), where \(t\) is the maximum occupied row count. Thus each top \(F_S\), on injective label tuples, is a sum of potentials each missing one row. All required stability hypotheses hold because \(2^\ell\ge2\ell-1\).

If \(t\ge3\), choose a maximum-degree monomial of a nonzero \(F_S\). At degree below \(\ell\), use the previous cube lemma; at degree exactly \(\ell\), use the critical lemma just proved. Summing over disjoint cubes kills every missing-row potential and isolates the nonzero leading coefficient, a contradiction. Therefore the bit polynomial uses at most two rows per monomial.

Its unary normal form has degree at most two and lies in \(\mathcal I_2\). The top coefficients on each pair \(i,i'\) are row-plus-column potentials on unequal labels, so (FIRST-pair) identifies \(F_{\{i,i'\}}\) as a scalar multiple of the mixed part of \(E_{ii'}\). Subtract those full equality polynomials from \(f\). Their decoder certificates preserve membership in \(\mathcal J_\ell\), and the remainder has only a constant and one-row terms.

Normalize within each row and apply stability once more, now to degree one. Only the row-equation span remains. Each one-row bit polynomial vanishes at label zero and must have constant values on all labels; hence it is zero. The remaining constant is zero as well. This proves the first equality in (FIRST-classification); its reverse inclusion follows from the already proved Booleanity and equality image certificates.

At original degree \(\ell\), the compact equality generators have only constant NS cofactors, so this span is exactly \(\mathcal I_\ell(\mathcal Q_n)\). For each pair, a degree-\(\ell\) monomial using a nonempty proper subset of the bit positions in one row and the complementary positions in the other appears in its equality polynomial and in no other pair's polynomial. This proves independence. Finally transported stability and \(\mathcal C_B(\mathcal Q_n)\subseteq\mathcal J_B\) give (FIRST-intersection), with the reverse inclusions supplied by the degree-\(\ell\) base certificates.

In particular the dimension of \(\mathcal P_{\le\ell}/\mathcal J_\ell\) is \(\sum_{k=0}^{\ell}\binom{(n+1)\ell}{k}-\binom{n+1}{2}\). This extends the four-label quadratic classification to every bit width. It does not establish full intrinsic stability above the first collision degree.

4. The critical singleton kernel leaves a collision-weighted Boolean residual

Return to \(D=3h+u,\ 1\le u\le h\), now at \(H+1=h+u+1=\ell\), and assume \(n\ge2D-1\). Keep \(L=2h+u\), the input order, first-success functions \(s_{a,j}\), and the low prescriptions from the preceding coupling proof. A consistency kernel has

\[ G\in U_a^{(H)},\qquad \deg T_j\le u+1,\qquad Gg_{a,j}+T_j\in\mathcal J_{L+1}. \]

Stability reduces this membership to \(\mathcal J_\ell\). By (FIRST-classification), in the Boolean function algebra there are unique binary coefficients \(c_{j,e}\), indexed by pigeon pairs \(e\), with

\[ Gg_{a,j}+T_j=\sum_e c_{j,e}E_e. \tag{FIRST-kernel} \]

The prescribed value of the kernel is consequently

\[ \begin{aligned} \lambda(G)+\sum_j\widehat\lambda(s_{a,j}T_j) &=\widehat\lambda(R_{a,G,T}),\\ R_{a,G,T} &:=\sum_e E_e\left(\sum_j c_{j,e}s_{a,j}\right). \end{aligned} \tag{FIRST-residual} \]

Indeed, substitute (FIRST-kernel), sum against \(s_{a,j}\), and cancel \(G\sum_j s_{a,j}g_{a,j}=G\chi_a=G\). This is the precise step that previously vanished by Boolean rigidity. A root functional annihilating \(\mathcal J_D\) need not annihilate an arbitrarily high-degree Boolean multiple of an equality axiom.

Let \(\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal B\) be the span of these residuals for all blocks and all such kernels, with the input orders fixed. A full Boolean functional extending a specified \(\lambda\) and annihilating \(\mathcal K\) exists exactly when

\[ \lambda\bigl(\mathcal K\cap\mathcal B_{\le D}\bigr)=0. \tag{FIRST-consistency} \]

This is elementary linear extension from the sum of the two subspaces, taking zero on \(\mathcal K\). It is exactly the consistency requirement for the common-Boolean-functional singleton prescription. If it holds, the pair step still works because \(u+1<\ell\). A sufficient and necessary condition for this prescription to work for every old annihilator is \(\mathcal K\cap\mathcal B_{\le D}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal J_D}\), where the bar denotes the Boolean quotient image. This does not characterize all possible augmented designs.

No source obstruction has been proved merely by writing these residuals. In particular, the actual retained affine inputs have rank above their packing threshold; their leading coefficient constraints might force every \(c_{j,e}\) to vanish. Testing that possibility is the next bounded source application.

13 September 2026 — Retained affine rank removes the first collision kernel

Status: working critical-boundary NS extension theorem, using the actual scalar cleanup and affine packing map; exact leading-coefficient checks, not a completed multilevel source theorem.

Route obligation and stopping point. The preceding boundary classification left a possible collision-weighted singleton residual. This turn tests whether the affine inputs that survive source preprocessing can produce it. Stop at a rank exclusion or an explicit retained kernel, and include all original-degree image certificates before applying the result to the family.

1. Linear annihilators distinguish single equality terms from their sums

Let \(V\) be the vector space with basis \(e_{it}\), one for each pigeon bit, and use the associated graded algebra of the Boolean degree filtration:

\[ A=\mathbb F_2[e_{it}]/\langle e_{it}^2\rangle. \]

This is the exterior algebra in characteristic two: variables commute and square to zero. The top degree of a product of Boolean functions is multiplication in \(A\). Write \(A_k\) for its homogeneous degree-\(k\) part and

\[ \varepsilon_{ii'}=\prod_{t=1}^{\ell}(e_{it}+e_{i't}), \qquad \mathscr E=\operatorname{span}\{\varepsilon_{ii'}:i<i'\}, \qquad W_{ii'}=\operatorname{span}\{e_{it}+e_{i't}\}_{t=1}^{\ell}. \]

These are exactly the leading parts of the compact equality axioms and their linear difference spaces.

Lemma. For \(\ell\ge3\), a nonzero \(F=\sum c_{ii'}\varepsilon_{ii'}\) has linear annihilator \(W_{ii'}\) if its support consists of one pair, and has zero linear annihilator if its support contains at least two distinct pairs.

Proof. Decompose a linear vector as \(v=\sum_t v_t\), where \(v_t\) uses bit position \(t\) only. The components \(v_tF\) have different multidegrees: degree two in bit position \(t\), and degree one in every other position. Thus \(vF=0\) implies \(v_tF=0\) separately.

Fix an active pair \(i,i'\) and two bit positions distinct from \(t\), possible because \(\ell\ge3\). In one of them select pigeon \(i\), and in the other select pigeon \(i'\); select pigeon \(i\) in all remaining positions other than \(t\). Only the equality term for this pair contributes to that coefficient. It follows that

\[ v_t(e_{it}+e_{i't})=0 \]

in the exterior algebra on the variables at position \(t\). Two linear vectors have zero exterior product exactly when they are dependent. Hence \(v_t\in\operatorname{span}(e_{it}+e_{i't})\) for every active pair. Distinct pairs give distinct one-dimensional subspaces, with zero intersection. This proves the multi-pair assertion; for one pair these conditions are also sufficient, giving exactly \(W_{ii'}\).

Excluded-width control. At \(\ell=2\), the sum of the six equality leading terms on four pigeon rows is \((\sum_i e_{i1})(\sum_i e_{i2})\). It has a two-dimensional linear annihilator despite containing six pair terms. Thus the width hypothesis in this lemma is necessary.

2. A degree-\((\ell-1)\) multiplier can feed at most \(\ell\) affine directions into equality terms

Lemma. For \(\ell\ge3\), nonzero \(\omega\in A_{\ell-1}\), and a linear subspace \(U\subseteq V\),

\[ \omega U\subseteq\mathscr E \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dim U\le\ell. \tag{RANK-leading} \]

Proof. First, the linear annihilator of any nonzero homogeneous degree-\(k\) exterior element has dimension at most \(k\). Choose a basis for that annihilator and extend it to a basis of \(V\). Multiplication by each of its first \(r\) basis vectors vanishes only if every monomial of the element contains that vector. Thus every monomial contains all \(r\) of them, forcing \(r\le k\).

For \(v\in U\), put \(F_v=\omega v\in\mathscr E\). Since \(v^2=0\), \(vF_v=0\). If \(F_v\ne0\), then \(v\ne0\), and the preceding lemma forces \(F_v\) to be a single equality term. Two different nonzero equality terms cannot occur as \(F_v,F_w\): their sum would be \(F_{v+w}\), with nonzero annihilator \(v+w\), contradicting the multi-pair assertion. Hence the image of \(U\) under multiplication by \(\omega\) has dimension at most one. Its kernel lies in the linear annihilator of \(\omega\), of dimension at most \(\ell-1\). Rank-nullity gives (RANK-leading).

The bound is tight as a leading-coefficient statement: take \(\omega=\prod_{t<\ell}(e_{it}+e_{i't})\) and \(U=W_{ii'}\). Its image is the span of \(\varepsilon_{ii'}\), and \(\dim U=\ell\). This is not asserted to be a full low-moment kernel for a source block.

3. Retained affine inputs cannot support a non-Boolean critical kernel

Assume \(D=3h+u,\ 1\le u\le h,\ H+1=h+u+1=\ell\), \(n=2^\ell\ge2D-1\), and \(\ell\ge3\). Consider one affine input span \(V_a=\operatorname{span}\{g_{a,j}\}\), excluding one, with rank \(r>\ell\).

Working proposition. Every consistency kernel \(G\in U_a^{(H)}\), \(\deg T_j\le u+1\), \(Gg_{a,j}+T_j\in\mathcal J_{L+1}\), \(L=2h+u\), is Boolean: all \(Gg_{a,j}+T_j\) vanish in the full Boolean function algebra.

Proof. Boolean-reduce \(G\); its degree is at most \(H=\ell-1\). By first-layer classification and stability, each \(Gg_{a,j}+T_j\) is a Booleanity consequence plus a constant combination of equality axioms. If \(G\) has degree exactly \(\ell-1\), let \(\omega\ne0\) be its leading exterior part. Since \(\deg T_j\le u+1<\ell\), taking degree \(\ell\) gives

\[ \omega\,{\rm lin}(g_{a,j})\in\mathscr E \quad\text{for every }j. \]

The map taking an affine form in \(V_a\) to its linear part is injective: a nonzero kernel would be the constant one. Its image therefore has dimension \(r>\ell\), contradicting (RANK-leading). Thus the Boolean degree of \(G\) is at most \(\ell-2\). Every \(Gg_{a,j}+T_j\) now has Boolean degree below \(\ell\); transported rigidity makes it Booleanity alone. Equivalently, independence of the equality leading terms forces all critical equality coefficients to be zero. This proves the proposition.

The full Boolean functional used in the coherent construction can therefore be chosen arbitrarily subject to its old values: the critical collision residual vanishes for every retained block of rank above \(\ell\). The same singleton and pair construction applies, with unchanged domains and degree costs.

4. Pull back through the actual affine packing map

Working theorem. Let \(n=2^\ell,\ \ell\ge4\), and use any complete one-level affine-bit family of common accuracy \(h\), after scalar cleanup, with original nonconstant-affine companion degree \(2h+1\). Suppose

\[ h\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil,\qquad D=3h+u,\qquad 1\le u\le h,\qquad h+u+1\le\ell,\qquad n\ge2D-1. \tag{CRITICAL-family} \]

Every old functional annihilating \(\mathcal J_D\) extends to an annihilator of the full augmented degree-\(D\) NS space, with unchanged old values. Normalized old functionals extend to ordinary designs, and

\[ \mathcal I_D(\mathcal Q_n\cup\mathcal E\cup\mathcal R) \cap\mathbb F_2[b]_{\le D} \subseteq\mathcal J_D. \]

Proof of the preprocessing and pullback. The strict case \(h+u+1<\ell\) was already proved. At equality, perform the actual scalar cleanup and affine packing. Remove unit spans by making a factor zero. For an input span of rank \(r\le2h\) excluding one, choose a basis \(F_1,\ldots,F_r\), pack at most two forms per factor row, and specialize coefficients affinely so that the product becomes \(A=\prod_s(1-F_s)\).

If \(g_j=\sum_s a_{js}F_s\), its companion image is

\[ g_jA=-\sum_s a_{js}(F_s^2-F_s)\prod_{t\ne s}(1-F_t). \]

Each affine Booleanity proof costs two, so the image has a Boolean NS certificate through \(r+1\le2h+1\). Every coefficient-field image has a Boolean certificate through two. Constant changes of the input basis return this affine coefficient assignment to the original tuple. Thus the global map \(\sigma\) is affine, fixes old bits and compact-base axioms, and sends every removed original axiom to a residual-base NS consequence through its original degree.

Every surviving block now excludes one and has rank \(r>2h\ge\ell\). The rank proposition removes its critical kernel. The coherent singleton and pair proof consequently supplies a degree-\(D\) design over all surviving blocks from any normalized old \(\operatorname{Ann}\mathcal J_D\) functional; the same construction works without normalization.

For the original ring define \(\Lambda(P)=\Lambda'(\sigma P)\). An original legal axiom multiple \(qf\) has a substituted cofactor of degree at most \(\deg q\), while \(\sigma f\) has the just-verified certificate through \(\deg f\). Hence \(\sigma(qf)\) is in the residual degree-\(D\) NS space. This proves annihilation of every original multiple and preserves every old moment. Duality over all old annihilators gives the stated consequence containment. Equal-span sharing is optional; the argument does not require distinct spans or bound their number.

This pullback concerns the whole one-level family. If later blocks exist, their inputs must also be substituted and may become nonlinear; the theorem does not assert extension over those later blocks.

5. Parameter gain and the remaining full-source gap

At the minimum actual compact-clause accuracy \(h=\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), the upper end of (CRITICAL-family) is

\[ D_{\max}=2h+\ell-1 =\begin{cases} 4h-1,&\ell=2h,\\ 4h-2,&\ell=2h-1. \end{cases} \]

The interval is nonempty for \(\ell\ge4\). It improves the preceding coherent range by one degree; for example \(\ell=6,\ n=64,\ h=3,\ u=2,\ D=11\) and \(\ell=8,\ n=256,\ h=4,\ u=3,\ D=15\) satisfy every hypothesis. The smaller first-boundary cases retain the earlier theorem as well.

The retained-rank hypothesis was discharged by a proved preprocessing map on the actual affine-bit source inputs. No input rank, block count, or generic-position assumption remains in (CRITICAL-family). Nevertheless the completed NS source bound is \((C+H_\pi)(d+1)h^d\), and later levels are possible. The theorem still falls far short of eliminating that endpoint. Before pursuing more narrow-band improvements, the next cycle will check the same compact base's assignment-tree obstruction and identify where the polynomial source inventory must enter.

6. Full finite leading-coefficient kernels and controls

The compiled exterior checker uses four pigeon rows and all 63 nonempty graphs on their six pairs, for each \(\ell=3,4,5\). For each sum of equality leading terms it computes the entire linear multiplication kernel by exact binary elimination, saving every output monomial, input column, reduction trace, and kernel combination.

All 189 graph cases passed. In the 18 single-edge cases, the kernel is exactly the \(\ell\)-dimensional difference space of that edge. In all 171 multi-edge cases, the kernel is zero. Three additional quotient computations verify the tight rank-\(\ell\) example of (RANK-leading), with multiplication images taken modulo the full equality-leading span. The excluded \(\ell=2\) complete-graph control has the predicted two-dimensional annihilator and demonstrates the failure of the multi-edge assertion at that width.

All 193 cases, including the controls, are exact coefficient-space computations; they are not full PHP NS matrices or a finite verification of all affine source families. The theorem's universal application is the argument above. The reproduction record, complete kernel certificates, and provenance preserve the evidence. Compilation and the numerical run both passed on the first attempt.

What changed. The critical collision kernel is excluded for every retained affine source input, and the same-degree preprocessing transfers that result to the entire original one-level family. The full source degree and multilevel elimination obligations remain open.

Process assessment. Applying the classified relations immediately to retained input ranks discharged a real source hypothesis; the next task will test the method's inventory limitation rather than assume that more degree-by-degree refinement closes the full endpoint.

13 September 2026 — A factorial bit family reaches degree \(4h+1\)

Status: application and pruning refinement of the existing assignment-tree theorem; complete finite factored-tree checks; an inventory limitation, not a polynomial-size Frege construction.

Route obligation and stopping point. The critical affine theorem is independent of family size but does not cover the completed source degree. This turn checks its limit on the same compact bit base, stopping at an explicit certificate and inventory. The general assignment-tree construction is already in the record; the new work is its compact leaf witness, collision pruning, and the resulting source-route comparison.

1. Compact equality leaves have original NS cost \(2h+\ell\)

Use \(\mathcal Q_n\) with \(n=2^\ell,\ \ell\ge2\), and \(n+1\) pigeons. Query their bits in row order, completing each \(\ell\)-bit label before starting the next pigeon. A nonempty assignment prefix \(\sigma\) has the usual one-level mismatch inputs \(g_{\sigma,v}=b_v+\sigma_v\), its own fresh accuracy-\(h\) product \(P_\sigma\), and all companions \(g_{\sigma,v}P_\sigma\). Nonempty products have original degree \(2h\), and every companion has original degree \(2h+1\).

Stop a branch when a completed row first repeats an earlier label. If rows \(i,i'\) repeat, both labels are fixed by the prefix, and

\[ L_t=\prod_{s<t}(1+b_{is}+b_{i's}),\qquad E_{ii'}-1=\sum_{t=1}^{\ell}L_t (g_{\sigma,it}+g_{\sigma,i't}). \]

The equal assigned label bits cancel in each mismatch sum. This is an ordinary telescoping polynomial identity, with \(\deg L_t=t-1\). Consequently, in characteristic two,

\[ P_\sigma =P_\sigma E_{ii'} +\sum_t L_t\bigl(E_{\sigma,it}+E_{\sigma,i't}\bigr). \tag{BITTREE-leaf} \]

Every displayed original axiom multiple has degree at most \(2h+\ell\). Unqueried rows do not enter the equality polynomial, so no completion of the remaining assignment is required.

2. The pruned tree has an exact factorial inventory

At an internal bit decision, use the already proved assignment-tree splitting certificate \(P_\sigma-P_{\sigma0}-P_{\sigma1}\), of NS degree at most \(4h+1\); the empty-root split has cost \(2h+1\), with \(P_\varnothing=1\). Sum the splits. They telescope to one minus the sum of leaf products. Every branch has a collision by the time \(n+1\) labels are complete, and (BITTREE-leaf) certifies every leaf. Thus

\[ \deg_{\rm NS}(\mathcal Q_n\cup\mathcal E_{\rm bit\ tree}\cup\mathcal R) \le\max\{4h+1,2h+\ell\}. \tag{BITTREE-degree} \]

In particular \(2h\ge\ell\) gives degree at most \(4h+1\). The degree conclusion is a compact-base application of the general tree theorem; pruning supplies a smaller exact inventory.

Let

\[ A_n=\sum_{k=0}^n(n)_k =n!\sum_{r=0}^n\frac1{r!},\qquad B_n=\sum_{k=0}^n k(n)_k=(n-1)A_n+1. \]

There are \((n)_k\) legal completed prefixes of \(k\) rows. Before the next row is complete, all \(2^t\) prefixes of its first \(t<\ell\) bits are internal; we deliberately wait for a completed collision before pruning. Hence the internal-node count is \(I=(n-1)A_n\), and a full binary tree has \(2I\) nonroot nodes. There is one block at each such node:

\[ \boxed{M=2(n-1)A_n=\Theta(n\,n!).} \tag{BITTREE-inventory} \]

Each child of an internal node at depth \(k\ell+t\) has \(k\ell+t+1\) input slots. Using \(\sum_{t=0}^{\ell-1}2^t=n-1\) and \(\sum_{t=0}^{\ell-1}t2^t=(\ell-2)n+2\), the exact companion count is

\[ C_{\rm comp} =2\left[\ell(n-1)B_n+ ((\ell-1)n+1)A_n\right] =\Theta(\ell n^2n!). \]

The coefficient-variable count is \(hC_{\rm comp}\). All inputs are signed bit literals, all spans are proper and have rank equal to prefix length, and all blocks are in one level. Individual split summands use at most a parent and one child coefficient family, so the displayed coefficient-interaction graph is a binary tree of maximum degree three.

At minimum packing accuracy \(h=\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), the same-degree affine packing removes only the prefixes of lengths at most \(2h\). No collision can truncate a branch before length \(2\ell\), so their number is \(2^{2h+1}-2=O(n)\). The remaining family still has \(\Theta(n\,n!)\) blocks, all of rank above \(2h\), and still has the same refutation degree bound after the affine map. Thus the control also survives the actual low-rank preprocessing used by the critical theorem.

3. The inventory-independent band is close to its limit

At \(h=\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), under the critical theorem's board hypotheses, every one-level affine family has NS refutation degree at least \(4h\) for even \(\ell\), or \(4h-1\) for odd \(\ell\). The factorial family above has a refutation through \(4h+1\). This leaves at most one or two integer degrees between the present universal lower threshold and an explicit upper construction.

Meanwhile the compact base retains PC degree at least \(n/2+1\). With \(h=\Theta(\ell)=\Theta(\log n)\), both the augmented degree and base generator degree are logarithmic. Therefore this family rules out an elimination degree bound polynomial in \(D,h,\ell,\log n\) that ignores inventory, even for one-level signed-bit inputs and the displayed tree interaction pattern. It does not rule out an arbitrary faster-growing bound in those parameters.

Here \(\log M=\Theta(n\log n)\). A small source proof instead supplies \(M=\operatorname{poly}(n)\), with \(\log M=O(\log n)\). The counterexample therefore does not refute a bound depending polynomially on \(\log M\), and it supplies no polynomial-size Frege proof. The full source gap now explicitly requires inventory or another source constraint; continuing a family-count-independent short-band theorem cannot by itself reach the completed endpoint.

4. Complete finite trees and a satisfiable frontier

The new compiled checker builds the full pruned tree for \(n=4,\ell=2\), once with five pigeons and once with four. It retains every node, assigned-bit prefix, coefficient namespace, collision pair, ordinary leaf-cofactor polynomial, and final frontier. It verifies every leaf telescoping identity and collects the entire formal sum of splits and certified leaves. The generic split witness is reused from its cited proof and archived checks; it is not re-expanded or rerun here.

For five pigeons the collected target is one. For four pigeons it is one minus the sum of the 24 permutation-leaf products. The saved identity permutation and first-success coefficient choices satisfy the latter target; deleting its frontier would incorrectly produce value one. Accuracies \(h=1,2\) instantiate leaf costs \(4,6\) and total costs \(5,9\). These small cases verify the factored construction and ledger, not an asymptotic PHP degree separation.

Compilation and the new finite run passed. The reproduction and namespace record, complete factored certificates, and provenance preserve all evidence.

What changed. The actual compact auxiliary base has an explicit factorial-family obstruction immediately above the current universal band. This narrows task selection: the next elimination attempt must use polynomial inventory or another proved source restriction, while general affine and multilevel coverage remain open.

13 September 2026 — Polynomial inventory removes signed-bit blocks, while dense affine rank can survive

Status: working inventory-dependent restriction theorem for signed-bit inputs; exact finite restriction and probability checks; scoped dense-affine survival control, already removable by quadratic packing.

Route obligation and stopping point. The factorial-family control requires an inventory-sensitive next step. This turn constructs a restriction preserving a smaller compact PHP base, proves a simultaneous signed-bit removal bound, and tests its extension to affine inputs. It stops at the proved subclass and an exact explanation of the affine survival limitation. The unary matching-restriction theorem is a related predecessor, not the same bit-coordinate map or probability argument.

1. A coordinate restriction preserves a smaller compact PHP base

Let \(n=2^\ell\), \(N=2^s\), and \(2\le s<\ell\). Keep the label subcube \(C=\mathbb F_2^s\times\{0\}^{\ell-s}\). Choose uniformly \(N+1\) live pigeons from the \(m=n+1\) pigeons, and assign the other \(q=n-N\) pigeons bijectively and uniformly to the labels outside \(C\). Fix those pigeons' bits. On live pigeons, fix the high bits to zero and retain \(s\) free low bits, renaming live rows canonically.

This coordinate restriction maps \(\mathcal Q_n\) into \(\mathcal Q_N\). An equality between two live rows becomes the residual equality generator; two fixed rows have distinct labels, giving zero; a mixed pair has a high-bit disagreement because the fixed label is outside \(C\), also giving zero. Booleanity maps to residual Booleanity or zero. The nonzero equality image has degree \(s\le\ell\), so every base image has an NS certificate through its original degree. Apply the same restriction to every retained ENS input and proof line.

2. A finite simultaneous-removal bound for signed-bit families

Take \(M\ge1\) one-level blocks with signed-bit inputs \(b_v\) or \(1-b_v\), arbitrary repetitions, and common accuracy \(h\). Scalar inputs and opposing literals can first undergo unit/zero cleanup. Set

\[ r=2h+1,\qquad 1\le r\le q,\qquad p_{\rm live}=\frac{N+1}{n+1},\qquad \alpha=\frac{n}{q-r+1}, \]
\[ \beta=\max\left\{ p_{\rm live}+\frac{\alpha}{2}, \left(p_{\rm live}+\frac{\alpha}{n}\right)^{1/\ell} \right\}. \tag{BITRES-beta} \]

Working theorem. If \(M\beta^r<1\), some restriction above kills every block of original literal rank greater than \(2h\), by producing a constant-one input. Every remaining block is removed by affine packing. Hence an original NS or PC refutation of ceiling \(D\ge\max\{\ell,2h+1,2\}\) maps, at the same degree, to one over \(\mathcal Q_N\) and the actual images of any other retained blocks. All later inputs undergo the complete substitution; their coverage is not inferred.

One-block probability. A proper signed-bit span has rank equal to its number of distinct bit variables. From a block of rank above \(2h\), choose \(r\) distinct variables and their prescribed mismatch-zero values. Let the affected pigeon rows have \(k_1,\ldots,k_w\) chosen bits, with \(1\le k_i\le\ell\) and \(\sum_i k_i=r\). If the block has no constant-one input after restriction, every fixed affected row must receive a label matching its chosen bit pattern. A row with \(k_i\) prescribed bits has at most \(n2^{-k_i}\) compatible outside labels.

For a specified subset \(A\) of the affected rows that are live, its probability is at most \(p_{\rm live}^{|A|}\), by sampling without replacement. Conditional on the live set, the other \(t=w-|A|\) affected rows get distinct uniform outside labels. Their compatibility probability is at most

\[ \frac{\prod_{i\notin A}n2^{-k_i}}{(q)_t} \le\prod_{i\notin A}\alpha\,2^{-k_i}, \]

because \(t\le w\le r\) and \((q)_t\ge(q-r+1)^t\). Ignoring possible high-bit violations on live rows only enlarges the event. Summing over \(A\) gives the upper bound \(\prod_i(p_{\rm live}+\alpha2^{-k_i})\).

The function \(f(k)=\log(p_{\rm live}+\alpha2^{-k})\) is convex. Its chord between 1 and \(\ell\), together with the two endpoint bounds in (BITRES-beta), gives \(f(k)\le k\log\beta\) for \(1\le k\le\ell\). Thus the one-block survival probability is at most \(\beta^{\sum_i k_i}=\beta^r\). The bound does not assume independence between affected pigeon rows.

Family and proof transfer. A union bound gives probability at most \(M\beta^r<1\) that any original high-rank block survives. Choose a successful restriction. Every other proper block has rank at most \(2h\), so the affine packing map sends its companion images to Boolean consequences through \(2h+1\), with field images through two. Killed blocks use a scalar factor-zero assignment. The whole map is affine and fixes the new old variables, so it preserves original NS cofactor budgets and PC line degrees, exactly as in the previous image-certificate replay. This proves the theorem.

3. Polynomial inventory and a square-root residual

For \(M\le n^a\) with fixed \(a\ge0\), choose

\[ s=\lfloor\ell/2\rfloor,\qquad N=2^s=\Theta(\sqrt n),\qquad h=\lceil(a+1)\ell\rceil. \]

For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(r\le q\), \(\alpha=1+o(1)\), and \(p_{\rm live}=\Theta(n^{-1/2})\). The second endpoint in (BITRES-beta) dominates eventually, and \(\log\beta=-\tfrac12\log2+O(1/\ell)\). Consequently

\[ M\beta^{2h+1}\le n^{-1+o(1)}<1. \]

The accuracy is compatible with compact-clause packing, since \(h\ge\ell\). If the whole supplied family is one-level signed-bit input, a polylogarithmic-degree refutation would therefore yield a degree-\(D\) refutation of \(\mathcal Q_N\), contradicting its \(N/2+1\) PC barrier for large \(n\). This is a binary literal-family theorem; original level-one MOD-containing inputs can be general affine forms, and later levels remain separate.

4. A dense affine space can retain rank with overwhelming probability

Scoped control. Let \(r=2h+1=O(\log n)\) and \(m=n+1\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), there is a binary \(m\times r\) matrix \(C\) such that every nonzero word \(Cv\) has weight at least \(m/4\). Use the affine input tuple

\[ g_j=\sum_{i=1}^m C_{ij}b_{i0}, \qquad j=1,\ldots,r, \]

where bit position zero is retained by the subcube map. The original span has rank \(r\) and excludes one. Under the same random restriction, it still has rank \(r\) and excludes one with probability at least

\[ 1-(2^r-1)(3/4)^{N+1}. \tag{BITRES-dense} \]

For \(N=\Theta(\sqrt n)\), this tends to one faster than any fixed inverse polynomial. Thus the signed-literal small survival bound does not apply to arbitrary affine rank.

Matrix existence. Choose the rows of \(C\) independently and uniformly in \(\mathbb F_2^r\). For fixed nonzero \(v\), its word weight \(W\) is a sum of \(m\) independent fair bits. Since \(\mathbb E\,2^{-W}=(3/4)^m\), Markov's inequality gives \(\Pr(W<m/4)\le2^{m/4}(3/4)^m\). The union bound over \(2^r-1\) nonzero \(v\) is below one for \(r=O(\log n)\), proving existence. Positive minimum weight also proves column rank \(r\).

Survival proof. Let \(L\) be the \(N+1\) live rows. The restricted inputs have form \(C_L^{\mathsf T}y+c\). Rank drops only if a nonzero codeword \(Cv\) vanishes on all of \(L\). Its zero set has at most \(3m/4\) rows, so sampling without replacement gives probability at most \((3/4)^{N+1}\). Union over \(v\) proves (BITRES-dense). When \(C_L\) has full column rank, the residual affine forms are independent and have a common Boolean zero for every constant vector \(c\); consequently their span excludes one. The outside-label bijection affects \(c\), but not this conclusion.

5. This survival control is already cheaply normalizable

The control only defeats the attempt to copy the literal high-probability constant-one argument to general affine inputs, followed by rank-at-most-\(2h\) affine packing. It does not rule out a favorable adaptive restriction, a larger-degree coefficient substitution, or a proof-specific elimination. Even its residual rank \(2h+1\) is already covered by the known polynomial-coefficient packing construction.

For \(h\ge1\), group \(2h+1\) independent affine basis forms into one bin of three and \(h-1\) bins of two. Prefix coefficients within a bin are products of at most two affine complements, so every coefficient-variable image has degree at most two. The product becomes \(A=\prod_{s=1}^{2h+1}(1-F_s)\); every companion image has a Boolean NS certificate through \(2h+2\), and every coefficient-field image through four. Hence the images fit twice their original degree ceilings, \(2(2h+1)\) and \(2\cdot2\). A supplied original NS certificate of degree \(D\) transfers through at most \(2D\).

The same substitution can pack any number of such one-level blocks simultaneously, since their coefficient variables map to old polynomials and do not depend on other blocks. This is a degree ledger for the existing packing method, not a new hard family. In particular a factor-two loss is compatible with a polylogarithmic source degree on a polynomial-size residual board. The goal only requires the final base degree below its barrier; insisting on exact preservation is a stronger convenience.

6. One complete restriction exhibits both effects

The compiled checker uses \(n=1024,\ell=10,N=32,s=5,h=6,r=13\), with 64 proper signed-bit blocks. Half place ten bits in one pigeon and three in another; half spread their 13 bits across different pigeons. The complete seeded inputs, live pigeon set, outside-label bijection, and one constant-one input for every block are retained. The first restriction trial kills all 64 literal blocks.

The same record contains a dense \(1025\times13\) binary matrix and all 8,192 codeword weights. Its exact minimum nonzero weight is 457. On the selected 33 live pigeons its rank is still 13, above \(2h=12\). Full pivot combinations and a residual common-zero assignment verify that the affine span remains proper. These are Boolean affine-space witnesses, not satisfying assignments of the unsatisfiable residual PHP base.

The program checks every old equality pair: 528 map to residual equalities, 491,536 fixed pairs map to zero, and 32,736 mixed pairs map to zero. The complete restriction arrays determine each image. Exactly 165 old bit Booleanity generators remain nonzero.

A small exact rational ledger verifies the probability decisions. Instead of comparing an irrational \(\beta\) numerically, it checks both equivalent rational inequalities

\[ M(p_{\rm live}+\alpha/2)^r<1,\qquad M^\ell(p_{\rm live}+\alpha/n)^r<1. \]

The literal union bound \(M\beta^r\) is approximately \(0.765461793\). From the complete minimum code weight, dense rank failure has the exact upper bound

\[ (2^{13}-1)\frac{\binom{568}{33}}{\binom{1025}{33}} \approx 1.85107239\times10^{-5}. \]

The ledger also proves their sum is below one by rational comparisons, confirming positive probability of simultaneous literal removal and dense survival. Decimals are display values only; every decision uses exact arithmetic. Compilation, the compiled enumeration, and the rational checks all passed.

The reproduction and encoding record, complete restriction and code data, exact probability ledger, and provenance preserve all evidence.

What changed. Polynomial inventory now yields complete degree-preserving coverage for signed-bit input families on a square-root compact residual. Arbitrary affine families do not inherit the same random-killing argument, but the tested low-rank dense control is already removable with a small degree loss. The unresolved rank range must therefore be judged against the actual final-degree budget, not merely the affine-normalizer threshold.

Process assessment. Checking the survival example against existing polynomial packing prevented a limitation of one convenient method from being reported as a barrier to the goal; no additional framework rule is needed.

13 September 2026 — Mixing packing and learning covers every affine rank in one bit level

Status: working one-level NS and PC refutation-exclusion theorem; exact dimension checks passed, with local symbolic controls recorded below; no multilevel or odd-prime conclusion.

Route obligation and change of direction. The initial task was to audit the rank budget after compact restriction and polynomial packing. The earlier resistant-family template suggested new dense controls, but the important issue was the cost of combining methods. Packing and common-vanishing learning can be chosen simultaneously on old inputs, taking the maximum of their substitution degrees. A new bit-coordinate subspace is large enough to make that hybrid cover every rank at polynomial inventory. This supplies a positive one-level result instead of another obstruction to a particular sequential ledger.

1. Polynomials using at most one bit per row inject into the transported quotient

Use \(n=2^\ell,\ \ell\ge2\), \(m=n+1\), \(v=m\ell\), and the transported class \(\mathcal J\). Define

\[ \mathcal L_k= \operatorname{span}\left\{ \prod_{i\in S}b_{i,t_i}: |S|\le k \right\}, \qquad d_k=\dim\mathcal L_k =\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom mj\ell^j. \]

Working lemma. If \(k\ge1\) and \(4(k-1)<n\), then \(\mathcal L_k\cap\mathcal J_k=0\). Unlike the earlier full-subring rigidity theorem, this can hold for \(k\) much larger than \(\ell\).

Proof. For \(f\in\mathcal L_k\cap\mathcal J_k\), use the row-support decomposition and matching normal form from the bit rigidity proof. If \(t\) is its maximum occupied row count, old functional-base stability reduces the normal form's NS membership to degree \(t\). The top coefficient \(F_S\), on injective label tuples, is therefore a sum of functions each missing one of its \(t\) rows. Each monomial of \(F_S\) contains exactly one bit from each row.

Choose a nonzero monomial and its one coordinate direction in every row. Each direction has \(n/2\) two-point cosets. The already chosen lines contain at most \(2(t-1)\le2(k-1)<n/2\) points, and each such point forbids at most one coset of the next direction. Greedy choice gives pairwise disjoint lines. Summing the coefficient identity over their product annihilates every missing-row function and isolates the chosen coefficient, giving \(1=0\). The remaining constant is zero by old stability. Its degree hypotheses hold because \(4(k-1)<n\) implies \(n\ge2k-1\) for the present power-of-two boards. This proves the lemma.

Consequently \(d_k\) is a lower bound for the whole transported quotient dimension. It is close to the full Boolean degree-\(k\) dimension when \(k^2\ll n\), but the exact value remains useful beyond that regime.

2. Pack low ranks and learn from high ranks in one substitution

Let an old system \(\mathcal F\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) contain Booleanity, and adjoin a complete one-level affine-input family of common accuracy \(h\). Remove zero and unit spans by scalar cleanup. Fix \(k\ge1\), and call a block low if \(r_b\le h(k+1)\), high otherwise.

Working hybrid lemma. Suppose the augmented system has a degree-\(D\) refutation, \(D\ge2h+1\). If a multilinear polynomial \(f\) of degree at most \(k\) vanishes on the affine zero space of every high block, then

\[ f\in\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F) \quad\text{for PC},\qquad f\in\mathcal I_B(\mathcal F) \quad\text{for NS},\qquad B=k(D+1). \tag{HYB-learning} \]

No vanishing condition on the low blocks is required.

Low blocks. Choose an affine basis \(F_1,\ldots,F_r\), and distribute its \(r\le h(k+1)\) complements among \(h\) bins of size at most \(k+1\). The existing factor telescoping construction, here with no retained core, assigns coefficient polynomials of degree at most \(k\). It makes the product \(A=\prod_s(1-F_s)\). Each companion image is a Boolean consequence through \(r+1\), by the same explicit basis identity used in affine packing. After multiplying by \(f\), its certificate costs at most

\[ r+1+\deg f\le h(k+1)+1+k \le k(2h+1)+k. \]

The last inequality is \((k-1)(h+1)\ge0\).

High blocks. By the affine ideal-membership argument, choose \(a_{b,i}\) of degree at most \(k-1\) with \(H_b=\sum_i a_{b,i}g_{b,i}\) and \(f-H_b\in\mathcal I_k({\rm BOOL})\). Put these coefficients in the first factor row and set all later rows to zero. Then the product is \(1-H_b\), and

\[ f g_{b,i}(1-H_b) =g_{b,i}\bigl[f(1-f)+f(f-H_b)\bigr] \in\mathcal I_{2k+1}({\rm BOOL}). \]

Since \(2k+1\le k(2h+1)+k\), these images fit the same ledger. All low and high coefficient assignments use only the original old variables, so the simultaneous substitution has degree at most \(k\); the two costs do not multiply.

Weighted replay. Multiply every substituted proof line by \(f\). A coefficient-field image has a Boolean certificate through \(2k+\deg f\le3k\). Old axioms become their multiples by \(f\). The same PC replay as in the earlier learning lemma fits \(kD+k\): at a multiplication step the original preceding degree is at most \(D-1\), and the substituted multiplier has degree at most \(k\).

For NS, an original degree-\(e\) axiom has cofactor image of degree at most \(k(D-e)\). The weighted image certificates above cost at most \(ke+k\), including \(e=2\) fields and the old axioms. Every substituted NS summand therefore fits \(kD+k\). The final weighted image of one is \(f\), proving (HYB-learning). This argument uses one level essentially: the inputs do not change when another block's coefficients are specialized.

3. A finite criterion for arbitrary mixtures of affine ranks

Return to \(\mathcal Q_n\). Write \(b_k(w)=\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom wj\), with binomial coefficients zero beyond \(w\). For the same low/high partition, assume

\[ 4(k-1)<n,\qquad n\ge2k(D+1)-1,\qquad \sum_{b:\ r_b>h(k+1)}b_k(v-r_b)<d_k. \tag{HYB-dimension} \]

Working theorem. Under these hypotheses there is no augmented degree-\(D\) NS or PC refutation, for any number of low blocks.

Proof. Restriction to a high block's affine zero space, of dimension \(v-r_b\), maps \(\mathcal L_k\) into a Boolean polynomial space of dimension at most \(b_k(v-r_b)\). This follows from an invertible affine coordinate change, which preserves Boolean degree over \(\mathbb F_2\). The last strict inequality gives a nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\) vanishing on all high zero spaces.

A putative refutation would put \(f\) in the old \(\mathcal I_B\) or \(\mathcal C_B\), for \(B=k(D+1)\). The transported class contains old \(\mathcal C_B(\mathcal Q_n)\), and its stability gives \(\mathcal J_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le k}=\mathcal J_k\). Thus \(f\in\mathcal L_k\cap\mathcal J_k=0\), a contradiction. This is nonmembership of a nonzero old polynomial, not construction of an old refutation of one. No augmented NS/PC equality or extension of a prescribed old design is assumed.

4. Polynomial inventory makes the criterion hold for every rank mixture

Suppose \(h\ge2\ell\), and put \(r_*=2\ell(k+1)+1\). Every high block has rank at least \(r_*\). For the parameter range below, \(w=v-r_*\ge3k-1\), so \(b_k(w)\le2\binom wk\). Moreover

\[ \frac{\binom{v-r_*}{k}}{\binom mk\ell^k} =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1} \left(1-\frac{r_*-(\ell-1)j}{v-\ell j}\right) \le\left(1-\frac{k}{m}\right)^k \le e^{-k^2/m}. \]

The middle inequality uses \(r_*-(\ell-1)j\ge\ell k\) and \(v-\ell j\le m\ell\). Hence \(k^2\ge m\log(4M)\) implies

\[ \sum_{\text{high }b}b_k(v-r_b) \le2M e^{-k^2/m}\binom mk\ell^k \le\tfrac12\binom mk\ell^k<d_k. \]

Asymptotic consequence. An empty family reduces to the base barrier. Otherwise let \(1\le M\le n^a\), take logarithmic \(h\ge2\ell\) and \(D=\operatorname{polylog}n\), and choose, with natural logarithm,

\[ k=\left\lceil\sqrt{(n+1)\log(4M)}\right\rceil =O(\sqrt{n\log(M+1)}). \]

For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(w\ge3k-1\), \(4(k-1)<n\), and \(B=k(D+1)=\sqrt n\,\operatorname{polylog}n<n/2\). Therefore every polynomial-size one-level affine-bit ENS family admits no polylogarithmic-degree NS or PC refutation over the compact PHP base. The claim covers all affine rank mixtures and arbitrary overlaps, not only literals or a fixed high-rank fraction. If a proposed degree is below the proper companions' original degree \(2h+1\), scalar cleanup and projection of unused coefficients reduce it to the base barrier directly.

This is compatible with the factorial-family control: its \(\log M=\Theta(n\log n)\) makes the required \(k\) and old degree unaffordable. For a hypothetical small source proof, \(h\ge2\ell\) can still be logarithmic and the supplied source degree and inventory remain polylogarithmic and polynomial. The conclusion applies if the retained family is one-level affine. Later inputs depending on earlier products are outside the hybrid lemma and remain the main binary source gap.

5. A separate NS bookkeeping observation from the initial audit

The initial rank-budget audit also gives a useful global NS observation. Suppose a polynomial map \(\sigma\), of degree at most \(T\), sends the old bits to a residual Boolean system with compact width \(s\), and every original equality image is Boolean-equivalent to zero or a residual equality. Suppose all other axiom images, after multiplication by a chosen old polynomial \(f\), vanish modulo residual Booleanity. In a supplied degree-\(D\) NS refutation over \(\mathcal Q_n\), each old equality cofactor \(q_e\) has original degree at most \(D-\ell\). Therefore

\[ f\equiv\sum_e \overline{f\,\sigma(q_e)}\,E'_e \pmod{{\rm BOOL}}, \]

where the bar is multilinear reduction and zero images are omitted. Reconstructing this identity as an ordinary NS certificate costs at most

\[ \deg f+s+T(D-\ell). \tag{HYB-old-cofactor} \]

Indeed, the displayed non-domain terms have that degree, and their difference from \(f\) is a Booleanity consequence with a degree-nonincreasing division certificate. The discarded image certificates need not be charged separately in this global argument. For \(f=1\) it refines the coarse \(TD\) bound for a complete Boolean normalizer; for the present hybrid it can refine the NS budget. The theorem above deliberately uses the common \(k(D+1)\) ceiling, valid for both NS and PC. This observation requires a supplied NS identity and the stated vanishing images; it is not a PC-reuse argument or an automatic multilevel transfer.

6. Exact local, geometric, and dimension controls

The mixed-image checker uses \(k=3\), accuracies \(h=1,2\), and five blocks in each fixture: a rank-\(4h\) packing block, two opposing rank-one low blocks, and two rank-\((4h+1)\) learning blocks. The high blocks share \(f=x_0x_1x_2\) as a vanishing polynomial; one membership identity has a nonzero Booleanity remainder, testing that step as well. The two opposing low zero spaces cover the entire Boolean cube, so requiring a nonzero predicate to vanish on all blocks would be impossible.

All 166 complete ordinary Boolean NS certificates passed. They include every weighted companion image, every coefficient-field image, old domain multiples, affine membership, and a maximal field-cofactor image. The simultaneous coefficient map has degree three, whereas multiplying the separate packing and learning degrees would give six. Omitting the weight or omitting low-rank packing gives recorded nonzero controls. The maximal image reaches \(B=18\) at \(h=1,D=5\), and \(B=24\) at \(h=2,D=7\); this is sharpness of that individual image's degree, not optimality of the whole refutation transfer.

The row-line checker verifies all 1,035 coordinate-direction multisets on six, seven, or eight rows at bit width five, covering ordered families up to row permutation. All 182,400 product tuples are injective, each chosen coefficient is one, and every saved missing-row basis parity is zero. These degrees exceed the bit width. A separate boundary control at \(n=4,\ell=2,k=2\), outside \(4(k-1)<n\), sums the three pair equalities on three rows to a nonzero member of \(\mathcal L_2\); the row-repeated terms cancel. Thus the row-line hypothesis is not being silently discarded.

The integer dimension checker evaluates every required binomial sum exactly, retaining the full integer dimensions and margins. It does not instantiate the enormous polynomial spaces or a hypothetical refutation.

The controls fail different parts of the chosen common criterion; they do not construct refutations, and the last row does not rule out a sharper NS-specific ledger. The reproduction and encoding record links the complete local certificates, full line-cube duals, exact dimensions, and their provenance.

What changed. The polynomial-inventory binary one-level affine problem is now covered at the full polylogarithmic source degree, with no rank-range or overlap hypothesis. The retained source may still have multiple levels. Under this map, high first-level products become \(1-H_b\), with \(H_b\equiv f\) modulo Booleanity, while low products become exact affine-flat indicators. A later input is therefore generally nonlinear; its learning and degree hypotheses are the next obligation.

Process assessment. Comparing the proposed obstruction with existing tools exposed an unnecessary multiplication of two simultaneous substitution costs; resolving that issue and using the smaller bit-variable quotient produced a positive all-ranks theorem without adding a framework rule.
