14 September 2026 — All-prime affine exclusion, complete power-input transfer, and the two MOD polarities

Status: working proofs extending the binary affine-family argument to every fixed prime, with an actual nonlinear one-level application and exact finite checks over \(\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\). General complemented MOD inputs and the full Frege source remain open.

Question and stopping point. Does the odd-prime obstruction come from the lower-bound engine or from the shape of actual modular inputs? We first check the signs and field domains in the engine, then test both source polarities. The result is a complete all-prime affine theorem and a factor-two transfer for entire systems with inputs \(L_i^{p-1}\). A large-zero-set example limits the complementary-predicate rank argument, but that example itself also admits a degree-preserving transfer.

1. Matching extension and old PC stability over every field

Use the functional unary system on \(m\) rows and \(N\) columns over an arbitrary field \(\mathbb K\): Booleanity, same-row and same-column exclusions, and \(\rho_i-1\). Assume \(m\ge B\), \(N\ge1\), and \(N\ge2B-1\). The ordinary matching normal form works in every characteristic. Its complete remaining constraints are

\[ \sum_{j\notin{\rm col}(T)}z_{T\cup\{(i,j)\}}=z_T, \qquad |T|<B,\quad i\notin{\rm row}(T). \tag{OP-marginals} \]

To extend prescribed moments from degree \(k\) to \(B\), perform the earlier row-set construction with orientations. For an \(s\)-row set \(S=\{i_0<\cdots<i_{s-1}\}\), orient each matching by increasing row order. Give a prescribed \((s-1)\)-matching missing row \(i_j\) the chain coefficient \((-1)^jz_T\). This is the boundary that the new top matching moments must realize.

For a face missing rows \(i_a,i_b\), \(a<b\), the two boundary contributions have signs \((-1)^{a+b}\) and \((-1)^{a+b-1}\). Their marginal sums are the same previously assigned moment, so they cancel. At \(s=2\), the reduced augmentation is the difference of the two equal row totals. Thus the prescribed chain is a reduced cycle, including outside characteristic two.

The primary BLVZ Theorem 1.1 gives \((s-2)\)-connectivity of the \(s\times N\) chessboard complex when \(N\ge2s-1\). Consequently its reduced homology in degree \(s-2\) vanishes over every field. A filling supplies exactly (OP-marginals): the top boundary and the prescribed chain have the same \((-1)^j\) factors. New top matchings belong to unique row sets, so independent fillings respect all shared lower moments. Degree one is filled by assigning each row its prescribed total. This is a field extension of our earlier argument, not a new topological theorem.

Every normalized degree-\(k\) design therefore extends. Normalized designs span the annihilator once one normalized design is fixed. Duality, followed by the ordinary-PC multiplication argument, gives

\[ \mathcal I_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le k}=\mathcal I_k,\qquad \mathcal C_B=\mathcal I_B. \tag{OP-stability} \]

For the second equality, a nonzero predecessor multiplied by a variable within degree \(B\) has degree at most \(B-1\); the first equality places it in \(\mathcal I_{B-1}\). Its multiplication stays in \(\mathcal I_B\). The converse follows by deriving each NS multiple within its ordinary degree. These are statements about the old functional system, with no augmented ENS equality.

2. The compact encoding and signed row-linear separation

For a prime \(p\), \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), and \(m=n+1\), define the appropriate compact base over \(\mathbb F_p\) by

\[ \mathcal Q_{n,p}=\{E^{(p)}_{ii'}\}\cup{\rm BOOL}_b,\qquad E^{(p)}_{ii'}=\prod_{t=1}^{\ell} \left(1-(b_{it}-b_{i't})^{p-1}\right). \tag{OP-base} \]

These collision equations have original degree \(\gamma=(p-1)\ell\). On Boolean labels each factor tests equality of the corresponding bits. The binary polynomial is recovered at \(p=2\); it must not simply be reused unchanged at odd primes.

The decoder remains \(\tau(b_{it})=\sum_{z:z_t=1}X_{iz}\). Boolean images have degree-two certificates using unary Booleanity and same-row exclusions. For a collision image, work first in the two involved rows with their Booleanity, exclusions, and row equations. Any polynomial of degree \(d\) in those rows reduces to its row-state interpolation through degree at most \(\max(d,2)\). Indeed powers collapse, conflicting same-row cells vanish, and a constant or one-row term can be completed to two occupied rows using the missing row sums, at cost at most two. The interpolation coefficient at states \(z,w\) is the value of the polynomial on those states.

For \(\tau E^{(p)}_{ii'}\), that coefficient is one exactly when \(z=w\). Thus its difference from \(\sum_zX_{iz}X_{i'z}\) has an ordinary NS certificate through \(\gamma\ge2\), and column exclusions kill the latter sum through degree two. All original-degree axiom images are certified. Affine PC replay therefore sends compact consequences through \(B\) to old functional consequences through \(B\).

3. Signs preserve the separating functional

Let \(\mathcal L_k\) consist of bit monomials with at most one coordinate from each occupied pigeon row, and suppose \(1\le k\le B\), \(4(k-1)<n\), and \(n\ge2B-1\). Its dimension is \(\sum_{j\le k}\binom{n+1}{j}\ell^j\) over every field. For a nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\), choose a monomial of maximum row degree \(t\), with rows \(S\) and selected coordinate \(a_i\) in row \(i\).

As in the binary dual construction, choose disjoint coordinate edges \(C_i\) of the Boolean label cube. There are \(n/2\) edges in each direction and at most \(2(t-1)\) forbidden ones at a greedy step. Orient each edge from bit \(a_i=0\) to bit \(a_i=1\), giving its endpoints weights \(-1,+1\). Delete their \(2t\) columns and take a normalized residual design \(\lambda\) through \(B-t\); Section 1 applies because \(n-2t\ge2(B-t)-1\).

Define the moment of a matching to be zero unless it contains every selected row on its assigned edge and its other rows avoid the deleted columns. In the remaining case set

\[ \mu(X_T)= \left(\prod_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i(T(i))\right) \lambda(X_{T|_{\overline S}}), \qquad \varepsilon_i\in\{-1,+1\}. \tag{OP-signed-tensor} \]

Boolean power reduction and collision zeroes extend this to ordinary polynomials. If a marginal is missing one selected row, its two endpoint terms cancel; if more are missing, all terms are zero. Incorrect selected labels or forbidden columns remain zero after extension. Once all selected rows are present, the marginal is exactly that of \(\lambda\), multiplied by the fixed edge signs. Hence \(\mu\) annihilates all of \(\mathcal I_B=\mathcal C_B\).

Only the chosen top row set can contribute to \(\mu(\tau f)\). The signed sum on its edges is the mixed finite difference isolating the chosen nonzero coefficient. Rescale \(\mu\) if a value of one is desired. Constant \(f\) is separated by a normalized design. Thus every nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\) is excluded from the compact PC consequences through \(B\), with the same degree and line-selection conditions as before.

4. One-level affine-bit exclusion for every fixed prime

Working theorem. Fix a prime \(p\). Let \(n=2^\ell\), choose accuracy \(h=3(p-1)\ell\), and take polynomially many complete one-level ENS blocks over \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\), all inputs affine in the old bits. For sufficiently large \(n\), this system has no ordinary-PC refutation of polylogarithmic degree \(D\). Its coefficient domains are \(r^p-r\), not Boolean equations when \(p\ne2\).

Proof. Remove zero/unit spans by scalar cleanup and let \(M\ge1\) count the remaining blocks. Put \(v=(n+1)\ell\) and \(k=\lceil\sqrt{(n+1)\log(4M)}\rceil\). A block is low if \((p-1)r\le h(k+1)\), and high otherwise. Every high block has rank at least \(r_*=3\ell(k+1)+1\).

Restrict \(\mathcal L_k\) as ordinary polynomials to each high zero flat in \(\mathbb F_p^v\). The image dimension is at most \(\binom{v-r+k}{k}\). The same dimension computation is field-independent:

\[ \frac{\binom{v-r_*+k}{k}}{\binom{n+1}{k}\ell^k} =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1} \left(1-\frac{r_*-1-(\ell+1)j}{v-\ell j}\right) \le e^{-k^2/(n+1)}. \]

The sum over high blocks is smaller than \(\dim\mathcal L_k\). Therefore a nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\) is identically zero as an ordinary polynomial on every high flat. Affine coordinates give literal expressions \(f=\sum_i a_i g_i\), \(\deg a_i\le k-1\), for each high tuple.

Use \(p-1\) coefficient rows \((\alpha a_i)_i\), one for every nonzero \(\alpha\in\mathbb F_p\), and zero remaining rows. The high product becomes

\[ \prod_{\alpha\ne0}(1-\alpha f)=1-f^{p-1}. \]

Weight by \(f\) itself, retaining row-linear separation. A weighted companion is \(fg_i(1-f^{p-1})=g_i(f-f^p)\), with an old Boolean NS certificate through \(pk+1\). The identity \(t^p-t\) has a Boolean certificate through \(p\deg t\): use Frobenius on its monomials and \(b^p-b=(b^2-b)\sum_{j=0}^{p-2}b^j\). Weighting by \(f^{p-1}\) is unnecessary.

For low rank, use the historical factor-packing lemma on all \((p-1)r\) factors \(1-\alpha F_j\), where \(F_j\) is an affine basis. Distribute them into \(h\) bins of size at most \(k+1\). Prefix telescoping gives coefficient degree at most \(k\) and exact product \(Z=\prod_j(1-F_j^{p-1})\). Since \(F_jZ=(F_j-F_j^p)\prod_{t\ne j}(1-F_t^{p-1})\), every companion image has a Boolean NS certificate through \((p-1)r+1\).

There is one simultaneous old-only substitution \(\sigma\). The needed weighted axiom ceilings are

\[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{image multiplied by }f&\text{old NS ceiling}\\ \hline \text{high companion}&pk+1\\ \text{low companion}&(p-1)r+1+k\le h(k+1)+1+k\\ \text{coefficient field}&(p+1)k\\ \text{old axiom }F&\deg F+k . \end{array} \]

Each fits \(k(e+1)\), where \(e\) is its original axiom degree: affine companions have \(e=2h+1\), coefficient fields \(e=p\), and old degrees are retained. For instance \(h(k+1)+1+k\le k(2h+2)\) for \(k\ge1\), and \(pk+1\le k(2h+2)\) here.

Replace each PC line by \(f\sigma(\text{line})\). At multiplication, the source predecessor degree is at most \(D-1\); multiplying its already derived weighted image by the variable's degree-at-most-\(k\) image stays within \(B=k(D+1)\). Expand polynomial multiplications into primitive PC steps. The putative refutation ends at the old polynomial \(f\). Polynomial \(M\) and polylogarithmic \(D\) give \(B=\sqrt n\,\operatorname{polylog}n<n/2\) and \(4(k-1)<n\) eventually, contradicting Section 3. If no proper blocks remain, old stability already excludes the refutation. No augmented NS/PC equality or expanded-monomial size bound is used.

5. A complete coefficient transfer for nonlinear power inputs

Consider an entire one-level family whose inputs in each block are \(g_i=L_i^{p-1}\), with \(L_i\) affine in the old Boolean bits. Its original product weight is \(hp\), companions have degree \(hp+p-1\), and coefficient fields degree \(p\), after constant cases are cleaned up. Introduce one fresh affine block on the \(L_i\)'s, with coefficients \(R_{ui}\) and product \(P_A\). Map every old coefficient by

\[ \Phi(r_{ui})=R_{ui}L_i. \tag{OP-power-map} \]

This degree-two map sends the original factor to \(1-\sum_iR_{ui}L_i^p\). Its difference from the affine factor \(1-\sum_iR_{ui}L_i\) has an old Boolean NS certificate through \(p+1\). Telescoping the \(h\) factors gives

\[ \Phi(P)-P_A\in\mathcal I_{h(p+1)}({\rm BOOL}_b). \]

Consequently the companion image is the sum of \(L_i^{p-1}(\Phi(P)-P_A)\) and \(L_i^{p-2}(L_iP_A)\). Its certificate degree is at most \(h(p+1)+p-1\), bounded by twice its original degree. For every coefficient domain,

\[ (R_{ui}L_i)^p-R_{ui}L_i =L_i^p(R_{ui}^p-R_{ui})+R_{ui}(L_i^p-L_i), \]

which has an NS certificate through \(2p\). Old axioms remain unchanged. All blocks use disjoint fresh coefficient sets, so these maps are simultaneous. Every original axiom image has its required certificate through twice its original degree; hence ordinary NS and PC replay send a degree-\(D\) refutation to one of degree at most \(2D\). This covers arbitrary use of the original coefficients, not only a preselected modular witness.

Working corollary. Polynomial-inventory one-level families of affine-power inputs \(L_i^{p-1}\), at \(h=3(p-1)\ell\), have no polylogarithmic-degree PC refutation over \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\). Affine blocks may coexist with these blocks. Section 4 excludes the resulting affine family at degree \(2D\). A constant factor is sufficient for the endpoint; no degree-preserving global map is needed.

6. Actual negative MOD children have profiles within their original source weight

Under the recorded source convention, formula approximations are zero for truth and an OR block uses inputs \(1-A^{\rm ap}\). A first-layer MOD child has approximation \(L^{p-1}\); its negation has \(1-L^{p-1}\). Thus an OR of negative MOD children has exactly the power inputs in Section 5. The affine \(L\) comes from its literal children and source offset. This matches the earlier signed source audit.

There is also stronger local cost information. Let \(P_A\) be the new affine product, with exact prefixes \(1-P_A=\sum_iU_iL_i\), \(\deg U_i\le2h-1\). For the actual inputs \(g_i=L_i^{p-1}\), choose value \(P_A\), prefixes \(V_i=U_iL_i\), input bounds \(\mu_i=p-1\), and cost \(s=2h+p-1\). Then

\[ 1-P_A-\sum_iV_ig_i=\sum_iU_i(L_i-L_i^p) \in\mathcal I_s,\qquad g_iP_A=L_i^{p-2}(L_iP_A)\in\mathcal I_s. \]

Furthermore \(\deg V_i+\mu_i\le s\), and \(P_A^2-P_A=-\sum_iU_i(L_iP_A)\) has a certificate through \(4h\le2s\). For odd \(p\) and \(h\ge2\), \(s\le hp\), the original product weight. These are complete costed NS profiles in the sense of the existing definition. Their identities hold with the necessary companion axioms; a general ENS product is not Boolean over its coefficient domains alone at odd primes. Section 5 separately supplies the complete-system transfer.

7. Complementary modular predicates: a rank obstruction that is itself removable

Positive MOD children instead produce inputs \(1-L_i^{p-1}\). Their common zero set says every \(L_i\ne0\); it is not a single affine zero flat. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), take independent old Boolean bits \(x,b_1,\ldots,b_m\) and

\[ L_i=1+x+b_i,\qquad g_i=1-L_i^2=xb_i-(x^2-x)-(b_i^2-b_i). \tag{OP-positive-example} \]

The \(L_i\) have affine rank \(m\), witnessed by their identity minor on the \(b_i\) columns. On the Boolean cube, their complementary predicates have \(2^m+1\) common zeroes out of \(2^{m+1}\): all points with \(x=0\), and the single point with \(x=1\), every \(b_i=0\). Thus underlying affine rank alone gives no shrinking-codimension estimate for this source polarity. Using the unchanged affine product on the \(L_i\)'s also fails: wherever all \(L_i=0\), its value is one and every \(g_i=1\).

A complete transfer for this example

The example is not a hardness claim. Introduce an affine block on \(b_1,\ldots,b_m\), with product \(P_A\), prefixes \(U_i\), and companions \(b_iP_A\). Put \(V=1-x+xP_A\), \(s=2h+1\), and \(\mu_i=2\). With \(B_x=x^2-x\), \(B_i=b_i^2-b_i\), the exact witnesses are

\[ 1-V-\sum_iU_ig_i=\sum_iU_i(B_x+B_i), \]
\[ g_iV=x(b_iP_A)+B_x\bigl(b_i(P_A-1)-V\bigr)-B_iV, \]
\[ V^2-V=B_x(P_A-1)^2+x(P_A^2-P_A). \]

The respective NS ceilings are \(s\), \(s+2\), and \(2s\), and \(\deg U_i+2\le s\le3h\) for \(h\ge1\). This gives a costed profile within the original positive-MOD product weight.

Here even the entire raw coefficient system transfers without degree loss. Rename its coefficients to those of the affine block. On old Boolean inputs, its product is \(\prod_u(1-x\sum_iR_{ui}b_i)=1-x+xP_A\), as an identity modulo old Booleanity. Degree-nonincreasing reduction of old bits therefore certifies the product difference through original degree \(3h\); coefficients \(R\) need no reduction. Multiply this difference by \(g_i\) and use the companion witness above: the original companion image has an NS certificate through \(3h+2\). Coefficient domains are just renamed. Ordinary NS/PC replay preserves \(D\).

Accordingly these common-bit blocks can coexist with the other handled one-level classes at \(p=3\). The general positive-MOD tuple and later dense nonlinear source still require new arguments. A large common zero set by itself does not imply a large proof degree.

8. Complete finite evidence and what changed

The moment checker now accepts an explicit prime while preserving its default binary output. The new \(\mathbb F_3\) run uses endpoint signs \((-1,+1)\) and residual pair coefficients \((1,-1,1)\) on the earlier three-cell path. It verifies 69,468 nonzero moments and 299,784 potentially nonzero marginal rows over the two fixtures \((n,k,B)=(8,2,4),(32,6,8)\), including every selected bit-axis evaluation. Unlisted constraints have zero on both sides by complete sparse support construction. Removing a top moment breaks four/eight marginals; replacing all nonzero moments by one also fails. The \(k>\ell\) fixture retains repeated directions on different rows.

The ordinary-polynomial checker saves all axioms, products, coefficient maps, targets, and NS cofactors. The initial run verified 51 certificates; the strengthened run verifies 72 across six local cases: negative MOD profiles and high-factor maps over \(\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\), low-rank packing over \(\mathbb F_3\), and the positive-MOD common-bit family. It checks the original degree ceilings and every raw source companion and field image.

Nonvacuous controls include a missing high factor, an omitted low-rank residue factor, a non-Boolean coefficient assignment showing that companion axioms are needed for product Booleanity, and a valid affine-core model refuting the naive complementary-input replacement. A complete 64-point table for \(m=5\) has the predicted 33 common zeroes. The finite cases verify the local algebra and moment witnesses; they do not instantiate the asymptotic rank threshold or prove a finite PHP size lower bound.

Both accepted NS outputs and the complete signed moment output are retained with commands, schema, source scope, hashes, and timing evidence. All mathematical checks passed. Preliminary indentation warnings were corrected before the corresponding runs.

Route assessment. Odd primes are no longer missing from the one-level affine lower-bound engine, and a complete nonlinear source class reaches that endpoint with affordable degree. This does not cover unrestricted MOD polarities, the dense multilevel Frege family, or the ordinary-unary proof conversion. The existing binary bit-PHP Res(\(\oplus\)) consequence is unchanged.

Next bounded question. Test an actual odd-prime clause calculus whose lines are disjunctions of affine disequalities. Include Boolean-domain clauses explicitly, audit a \(p\)-premise affine cover, and derive its rule and initial-value PC costs. Keep its scope separate from standard disjunctions of affine equations and from Boolean-semantic inference. Stop at a complete forward simulation or a concrete obstruction.

Process assessment. Checking a complete coefficient transfer exposed an affordable factor-two route beyond the local profiles; the existing endpoint-first guidance handled this adjustment, so no additional framework rule is needed.

14 September 2026 — A complete odd-prime clause application with explicit Boolean domains

Status: working forward simulation and superpolynomial bit-PHP size bound for the explicitly defined affine-disequality calculus \(\mathcal R_p^{\ne}\), for every fixed prime. At \(p=2\) this recovers the recorded Res(\(\oplus\)) consequence. General odd-prime equation clauses and the full Frege goal remain open.

Question and stopping point. Determine whether a concrete odd-prime proof system reaches the newly excluded affine endpoint, with every rule and Boolean-domain assumption accounted for. The simulation below uses only one affine ENS level and degree \(\max(2h+(p-1)\ell,4h+p-1)\), independently of proof-DAG height. Complete local traces and composed controls accompany the argument.

1. The precise calculus and its scope

Fix a prime \(p\). A line of \(\mathcal R_p^{\ne}\) is a clause \(C=\bigvee_i(g_i\ne0)\), with affine \(g_i\) over \(\mathbb F_p\). Its falsifying set \(Z(C)=\{g_i=0\ \forall i\}\) is an affine subspace or empty. The basic rules are full-field semantic weakening \(C\models_{\mathbb F_p}D\) and the \(p\)-way split

\[ \frac{\bigl(C_a\vee(u-a\ne0)\bigr)_{a\in\mathbb F_p}} {\bigvee_{a\in\mathbb F_p}C_a}, \qquad u\text{ affine}. \tag{DC-split} \]

All premises and conclusions are interpreted on the full \(\mathbb F_p\) space for these rules. A Boolean variable \(b\) is constrained by the explicit initial clauses

\[ b-a\ne0,\qquad a\in\mathbb F_p\setminus\{0,1\}. \tag{DC-domains} \]

These clauses have algebraic initial proofs below; they are not silently built into semantic weakening. A general sound inference from at most \(p\) premises on the full field is an equivalent rule convention, by Section 2.

The calculus contains ordinary Boolean resolution with constant overhead for fixed \(p\): represent a positive literal by \(b\ne0\), a negative literal by \(b-1\ne0\), and supplement the two usual resolution premises with the \(p-2\) domain clauses for the other residues in (DC-split). Adding literals is a valid weakening. More generally, a full assignment tree proves completeness for unsatisfiable affine-disequality inputs with domains: each leaf is weakened from an initial clause falsified by its assignment, and the splits remove the assignment coordinates.

This is a definition for the present result, not an identification with a standard odd-prime system. The Part–Tzameret primary report describes \({\rm Res}({\rm lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\) using disjunctions of affine equations. At \(p=2\), equations and disequalities are interchangeable by switching the residue. At odd primes an equation is a conjunction of \(p-1\) disequalities. We have not supplied a polynomial simulation of that broader system. The primary record was used for this terminology check, not to import its lower-bound proofs.

The full-field clause conversion has an exact exponential example

On \(w\) unrestricted field coordinates, let \(C=\bigvee_{i=1}^w(y_i=0)\). Its falsifying set is \((\mathbb F_p^\times)^w\). An affine subspace contained in this set must be a point: a nonconstant coordinate on an affine subspace takes every field value, including zero. If a conjunction of affine-disequality clauses in these same coordinates is exactly equivalent to \(C\) on the full field, each clause's falsifying affine subspace lies in that set and covers at most one point. At least \((p-1)^w\) clauses are required.

The bound is attained by \(\bigwedge_{\alpha\in(\mathbb F_p^\times)^w}\bigvee_i(y_i-\alpha_i\ne0)\). This is an exact obstruction to that full-field line conversion, not to every proof conversion. Boolean-domain information or additional variables change the question; no lower bound for all domain-aware simulations is inferred.

2. At most \(p\) semantic premises reduce to one affine split

Suppose \(A_1\wedge\cdots\wedge A_q\models_{\mathbb F_p}D\), \(q\le p\), and set \(W=Z(D)\). Then \(W\subseteq\bigcup_jZ(A_j)\). Empty \(W\) is a tautology. If one \(Z(A_j)\) contains \(W\), a single weakening suffices.

Otherwise each \(W\cap Z(A_j)\) is a proper affine subspace of \(W\), with at most \(|W|/p\) points. Covering \(W\) with at most \(p\) of them forces \(q=p\), every set to be an affine hyperplane of \(W\), and the sets to be pairwise disjoint. Distinct nonparallel affine hyperplanes intersect, so these hyperplanes are parallel. They are the fibers \(u=a\), \(a\in\mathbb F_p\), of a common nonconstant affine coordinate on \(W\), extended affinely to the ambient space.

After reindexing, \(A_a\models_{\mathbb F_p}D\vee(u-a\ne0)\). Derive these \(p\) weakenings and apply (DC-split), identifying repeated copies of \(D\). This uses at most \(p\) auxiliary clauses per inference. The cardinality argument and affine containment witnesses also make the fixed-\(p\) semantic rule checkable by linear algebra.

Every clause can be replaced by a basis of its affine falsifying system, containing at most \(v+1\) forms on \(v\) variables. This preserves full-field semantic consequences; the preceding reduction supplies the basic rules afterward. Thus a polynomial number of proof lines has polynomial total descriptions and block inventory. If fresh propositional variables are allowed, first fix them to Boolean constants: semantic implications survive restriction, their domain clauses become tautologies, and a constant-pivot split reduces to weakening. No proof-size advantage from such unconstrained fresh variables is assumed away.

3. The ordinary-PC simulation of the rules

Give each clause \(C\) a fresh complete accuracy-\(h\) affine ENS block on its listed forms \(g_{C,i}\). Write \(P_C\) for its product, \(E_{C,i}=g_{C,i}P_C\) for its companions, and \(U_{C,i}\) for the exact prefixes. Then

\[ 1-P_C=\sum_iU_{C,i}g_{C,i},\qquad \deg P_C\le2h,\quad \deg U_{C,i}\le2h-1. \]

All coefficient domains are \(r^p-r\). Clause values \(P_C=0\) will be derived PC lines, not extra axioms of the global augmented system. The empty clause has value one and no coefficient block.

Weakening. If \(C\models_{\mathbb F_p}D\) and \(Z(D)\ne\varnothing\), every \(g_{C,i}\) is a constant linear combination of the \(D\)-forms. Derive \(g_{C,i}P_D\) from the \(D\)-companions through \(2h+1\), then use

\[ P_D=P_CP_D+\sum_iU_{C,i}(g_{C,i}P_D). \]

A completed proof of \(P_C\) through \(K\) therefore yields \(P_D\) through \(\max(K,4h)\). If \(Z(D)\) is empty, a constant combination of its forms equals one, and the same combination of companions derives \(P_D\) through \(2h+1\).

The \(p\)-way split. Let \(A_a=C_a\vee(u-a\ne0)\) be the premises and \(T=\bigvee_aC_a\). Assume each \(P_{A_a}\) is already derived through \(K\). Its prefix identity and the available \(T\)-companions give

\[ R_a=P_T-U_{a,*}(u-a)P_T =P_{A_a}P_T+ \sum_{i\in C_a}U_{a,i}(g_{a,i}P_T) \quad\text{through }\max(K,4h). \tag{DC-prefix} \]

Put \(\chi_a(u)=1-(u-a)^{p-1}\). The ordinary identities \(\sum_a\chi_a(u)=1\) and \(\chi_a(u)(u-a)=-(u^p-u)\) imply

\[ \chi_a(u)R_a-U_{a,*}P_T(u^p-u)=\chi_a(u)P_T. \tag{DC-residue} \]

Since \(u\) is affine in old Boolean bits, \(u^p-u\) has a Boolean NS certificate through degree \(p\). Multiplication in (DC-residue) costs at most \(4h+p-1\): both the prefix-product correction and the selector times (DC-prefix) meet this ceiling. Summing the completed residue lines derives \(P_T\) through \(\max(K,4h+p-1)\).

The argument reuses completed premise lines; it does not multiply their entire earlier derivations. Polynomial multiplication expands into monomial variable multiplications and linear combinations within the stated degree. Thus proof height contributes no additional factor. No implicit Boolean reduction or extra inference rule is used.

4. Every required initial clause has its own degree certificate

Boolean domains. For \(a\notin\{0,1\}\), put \(g=b-a\), and let \(q(b)\) be the affine interpolant with \(q(0)=(-a)^{-1}\), \(q(1)=(1-a)^{-1}\). For a constant \(c\), \(q(b)g-1=c(b^2-b)\). Consequently the domain clause's value has the exact proof

\[ P=q(b)(gP)-c(b^2-b)P, \]

through \(2h+2\). Only the old Boolean equation and this block's companion are needed. On the unrestricted field point \(b=a\), the clause is false; its validity genuinely uses the explicit domain axiom.

Compact PHP pairs. For \(n=2^\ell,\ell\ge2\), use the initial clauses

\[ C_{ii'}=\bigvee_{t\le\ell}(b_{it}-b_{i't}\ne0) \]

with the domain clauses above. Let \(g_t=b_{it}-b_{i't}\), \(E=\prod_t(1-g_t^{p-1})\), and \(V_t=g_t^{p-2}\prod_{s<t}(1-g_s^{p-1})\). The correct old system is \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\) from the preceding entry, with original collision degree \(\gamma=(p-1)\ell\). Telescoping gives

\[ P_C=EP_C+\sum_tV_t(g_tP_C), \]

an NS, hence PC, derivation through \(2h+\gamma\). The collision polynomial has not been treated as affine.

Usual CNF. A standard bit-PHP clause forbids two pigeon labels from both equaling a particular Boolean word \(z\). Its literals are \(b_{it}-z_t\ne0\) and \(b_{i't}-z_t\ne0\). Its falsifying set is contained in \(Z(C_{ii'})\) on the full field, so \(C_{ii'}\) implies it by weakening. Algebraically \(b_{it}-b_{i't}=(b_{it}-z_t)-(b_{i't}-z_t)\). Therefore a short proof of the usual CNF with the explicit domains also gives a short proof from the compact pair clauses.

5. Complete forward transfer and working size consequence

Working theorem. A size-\(S\) DAG-like \(\mathcal R_p^{\ne}\) refutation of bit PHP with \(n+1\) pigeons and \(n=2^\ell\) holes, \(\ell\ge2\), gives a complete one-level affine-bit ENS family of polynomial inventory and an ordinary-PC refutation over \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\) through

\[ D=\max\{2h+(p-1)\ell,\ 4h+p-1\}. \tag{DC-transfer} \]

Introduce all clause and auxiliary blocks in one fixed family. Initial values follow from Section 4. Follow the proof DAG using Section 3, replacing local premise-value assumptions by their actual earlier proofs. The final empty-clause value is one. The Boolean-domain cost \(2h+2\) is below \(4h+p-1\), and the semantic-cover convention adds only fixed-\(p\) inventory overhead.

For every fixed \(p,K\), choose \(h=3(p-1)\ell\). A hypothetical size-\(n^K\) refutation then supplies polynomial inventory \(M\) and

\[ D=(p-1)(12\ell+1). \]

The all-prime affine exclusion forbids this endpoint. Explicitly \(k=\lceil\sqrt{(n+1)\log(4M)}\rceil\) gives \(B=k(D+1)=O_p(\sqrt n\,(\log n)^{3/2})<n/2\) and \(4(k-1)<n\) eventually, while the signed old functional annihilator excludes the learned target. Thus sufficiently large bit-PHP instances have no size-\(n^K\) refutation in the defined calculus, including the usual CNF presentation.

This reaches an actual unbounded-width, DAG-like clause family over each prime. At \(p=2\) it recovers the earlier natural-system result. For odd \(p\), it remains essential that the lines are disequality clauses and inference is sound on the full field with Boolean domains explicit. The theorem does not settle usual equation-clause \({\rm Res}({\rm lin}_{\mathbb F_p})\), ordinary unary encodings, or \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege.

6. Primitive PC evidence and scope controls

The new checker uses the existing exact ordinary-PC kernel. It generates and replays 31 full traces over \(\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\), at \(h=1,2\). Each saved line is an axiom introduction, a two-term field-linear combination, or multiplication by one variable. Corrupting the final polynomial of every trace is rejected.

Rule or initial valueVerified degree ceiling
\(p\)-way cut\(4h+p-1\)
Affine-span weakening\(4h\)
Tautological affine clause\(2h+1\)
Each excluded Boolean residue\(2h+2\)
Two-row compact initial clause, \(\ell=2\)\(2h+2(p-1)\)

Cut fixtures include a genuinely field-valued pivot and, separately, a sum of old Boolean bits realizing every residue. The latter checks the actual degree-\(p\) old Boolean certificate, rather than adding the pivot domain as an unexplained axiom. Satisfying models verify nonvacuity; deleting any one residue premise permits conclusion value one. Coefficient assignments use the inverse of a nonzero input, so values outside \(\{0,1\}\) are exercised.

All non-Boolean residues of \(p=3,5\) have domain-clause traces. Removing the old Boolean equation permits \(b=a\) and conclusion value one. The compact initial fixtures use two rows and distinct Boolean labels; removing their collision equation permits equal labels and a false conclusion. These are satisfiable local checks, not small unsatisfiable PHP instances.

A three-premise semantic example over \(\mathbb F_3\), with forms \(u-a+az\), derives \(z\ne0\) through the cover construction. Its implication is also checked at all nine full-field points. Four composed refutations use the artificial inconsistent residue partition \(\{1-(u-a)^{p-1}=0:a\in\mathbb F_p\}\); their premise values are actually derived from initial axioms before the cut, with no added premise-value axioms. The source is explicitly not PHP, and removing any initial equation restores a typed model.

The complete traces, block data, domains, models, and full-field checks are retained with commands and source scope, hashes, and measured evidence. Compilation and all checks passed. Finite traces verify the local simulation and its composition; the asymptotic consequence uses the stated internal lower-bound chain.

Route assessment. The odd-prime affine endpoint now has a complete clause-calculus application, including the previously explicit domain and rule-convention obligations. The remaining gap to general modular equation clauses is the complementary-predicate structure, not a missing \(p\)-way cut identity.

Next bounded question. Test positive-MOD tuples \(1-(a_i t+b_i+c_i)^{p-1}\) where \(t\) is one shared old affine form and each \(b_i\) is a Boolean literal. Determine whether conditioning on the \(p\) values of \(t\) replaces the complete coefficient system by a constant number of affine blocks at affordable degree, including all field images. Stop at a complete transfer or a concrete obstruction.

Process assessment. Checking the primary terminology before the simulation kept the new calculus separate from a broader open system, while the existing PC kernel supplied all needed traces without additional framework machinery.

14 September 2026 — Positive MOD inputs with one shared affine probe reduce to affine blocks

Status: working complete NS/PC transfer and one-level exclusion for an actual positive-MOD source class; exact image certificates and dependent-literal controls over \(\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\). General positive-MOD tuples and multilevel sources remain open.

Question and stopping point. Can a shared affine component be handled without assuming that it is independent of the other input bits? The answer is yes for the class below: \(p\) residue branches replace one complete source block by at most \(p\) affine blocks, with degree \(D\mapsto pD\). Every companion and coefficient-field image is certified. This extends the earlier common-bit example to arbitrary old affine probes; that special example retains its sharper degree-preserving bound.

1. The source class and its literal branches

Fix an odd prime \(p\) and an old polynomial system \(\mathcal G\) containing Boolean equations for its bit variables. For one accuracy-\(h\) ENS block, suppose its actual inputs are

\[ g_i(b)=1-\bigl(a_i t(b)+q_i(b)+c_i\bigr)^{p-1}, \qquad a_i,c_i\in\mathbb F_p, \tag{SP-inputs} \]

where \(t\) is one shared old affine form and each \(q_i\) is an old Boolean literal, either a bit or its complement. Repeated literals are allowed, and \(t\) may contain those same bits with arbitrary coefficients. These are exactly the OR inputs of positive first-layer MOD children with the displayed affine pre-power forms. Neither the number of inputs nor the support of \(t\) is bounded.

Identically zero coordinates can be removed, and a constant-one coordinate makes a block scalar-normalizable. For the remaining nonconstant inputs, the original degree is \(p-1\), product weight \(hp\), companion degree \(hp+p-1\), and coefficient-field degree \(p\). A polynomial that merely vanishes on Boolean inputs is not silently discarded as the zero ordinary polynomial.

For each \(\alpha\in\mathbb F_p\), define the two values

\[ d_{i,\alpha,0}=1-(a_i\alpha+c_i)^{p-1},\qquad d_{i,\alpha,1}=1-(a_i\alpha+1+c_i)^{p-1}, \]

and the affine old-bit input

\[ G_{i,\alpha}(b)=d_{i,\alpha,0} +(d_{i,\alpha,1}-d_{i,\alpha,0})q_i(b). \]

On old Boolean assignments with \(t=\alpha\), \(g_i=G_{i,\alpha}\). Both \(d\)'s are zero or one, so these branch inputs are literals or constants. The claim is pointwise on the actual old cube, including any dependencies between \(t\) and the \(q_i\)'s.

2. One simultaneous map of the complete coefficient system

Introduce a fresh complete affine ENS block \(A_\alpha\) on \((G_{i,\alpha})_i\), with coefficients \(R_{\alpha,u,i}\), product \(P_\alpha\), all companions \(G_{i,\alpha}P_\alpha\), and domains \(R_{\alpha,u,i}^p-R_{\alpha,u,i}\). All new coefficient sets are disjoint. Define

\[ \chi_\alpha(t)=1-(t-\alpha)^{p-1},\qquad \Phi(r_{u,i})=\beta_{u,i} =\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb F_p} \chi_\alpha(t)R_{\alpha,u,i}, \qquad V=\sum_\alpha\chi_\alpha(t)P_\alpha. \tag{SP-map} \]

The map fixes old variables and has degree at most \(p\). The canonical value has degree at most \(2h+p-1\). On an old Boolean assignment, the selectors choose exactly its actual residue \(t=\alpha\). As polynomials in the still-formal \(R\)'s, \(\Phi(P)\) and \(V\) then both equal \(P_\alpha\). Therefore

\[ \Phi(P)-V\in\mathcal I_{h(2p-1)}({\rm BOOL}_b). \tag{SP-product} \]

For completeness, this is an ordinary NS statement: divide only by the old equations \(b_j^2-b_j\), treating all \(R\)'s as coefficient variables. The multilinear remainder is identically zero because it is zero at every old Boolean point as a polynomial in the \(R\)'s. Division does not increase joint degree. Each mapped factor has degree at most \(2p-1\), while \(2h+p-1\le h(2p-1)\) for \(h\ge1\). No new companion or coefficient-domain equation is used in this product comparison.

Likewise, old Boolean division gives

\[ \chi_\alpha(t)\bigl(g_i-G_{i,\alpha}\bigr) \in\mathcal I_{2(p-1)}({\rm BOOL}_b). \tag{SP-input} \]

The selector either vanishes or selects the residue at which the two inputs agree. This proof uses the actual dependent old variables; it does not introduce an independent probe variable or impose \(t^2-t=0\).

3. Every original axiom image fits the claimed transfer

Companions. The exact decomposition

\[ g_i\Phi(P)= g_i(\Phi(P)-V) +\sum_\alpha\chi_\alpha(t)(G_{i,\alpha}P_\alpha) +\sum_\alpha \bigl[\chi_\alpha(t)(g_i-G_{i,\alpha})\bigr]P_\alpha \]

supplies an NS certificate over the common retained system. Its three parts cost at most \(h(2p-1)+p-1\), \(2h+p\), and \(2h+2p-2\), respectively. The first dominates for \(p\ge3,h\ge1\), and is at most \(p\) times the original companion degree \(hp+p-1\).

Coefficient fields. Frobenius gives

\[ \beta_{u,i}^p-\beta_{u,i} =\sum_\alpha \chi_\alpha(t)^p (R_{\alpha,u,i}^p-R_{\alpha,u,i}) +\sum_\alpha (\chi_\alpha(t)^p-\chi_\alpha(t))R_{\alpha,u,i}. \]

The second sum has old Boolean certificates, while the first uses genuine prime-field domains for the new coefficients. Both fit degree \(p^2\), exactly \(p\) times the original domain degree. The new coefficients and their images need not be Boolean.

Old base generators are unchanged. Consequently an NS cofactor of original degree at most \(D-e\) has image degree at most \(p(D-e)\), and multiplying the degree-\(pe\) axiom-image certificate stays within \(pD\). For ordinary PC, replay the certified axiom images; a source multiplication has predecessor degree at most \(D-1\), and its variable image has degree at most \(p\). Primitive polynomial multiplication therefore also stays within \(pD\).

Working complete-transfer theorem. For a one-level family of blocks of type (SP-inputs), each with its own shared old affine probe if desired, apply (SP-map) simultaneously with disjoint fresh branch coefficients. A degree-\(D\) NS or PC refutation over \(\mathcal G\) transfers to a degree-at-most-\(pD\) refutation over \(\mathcal G\) and at most \(p\) times as many complete affine blocks, with the same accuracies. All coefficient uses are covered, not only prescribed modular witnesses. Zero/unit branch tuples can subsequently be cleaned up by the existing scalar maps.

This differs from the older probe-normalizer theorem, which assumes a supplied refutation after zeroing probes and extracts an old target. Here no such refutation is assumed; the result retains several fresh affine blocks. It also differs from old row-profile elimination, whose coefficient representatives lie entirely in the old row algebra.

4. Actual positive-MOD source coverage

Take \(\mathcal G=\mathcal Q_{n,p}\), \(n=2^\ell,\ell\ge2\), and \(h=3(p-1)\ell\). If a polynomial-inventory one-level family of (SP-inputs) had a polylogarithmic-degree PC refutation, the preceding theorem would give a polynomial-inventory affine family at degree \(pD\), still polylogarithmic for fixed \(p\). The all-prime affine exclusion forbids it.

Thus this positive-MOD family is excluded without a low bound on its underlying affine rank: the forms \(a_it+q_i+c_i\) can have arbitrarily large rank through their individual literal coordinates. The shared probe can involve many pigeon rows. For example, with all slopes one and all offsets zero, residues of \(t\) other than \(0,-1\) make every input zero; the method still works because it keeps the appropriate affine branches instead of requiring small zero sets.

Affine blocks and the already handled power-input blocks may coexist with this family: their maps use disjoint new coefficient sets, and the largest degree factor is at most \(p\). This does not cover arbitrary collections of positive-MOD affine forms lacking the shared-probe presentation, or later inputs with unrestricted nonlinear selector dependence.

5. Full image certificates and controls using dependent literals

The exact compiled checker verifies three fixtures: \(\mathbb F_3,h=1\); \(\mathbb F_3,h=2\) with varied slopes and an input that vanishes only modulo old Booleanity; and \(\mathbb F_5,h=1\). The shared probe is the sum of all old bits and includes every literal's variable, including a complemented literal. Every field residue occurs on the old Boolean cube.

The retained output has 57 complete ordinary-NS certificates and 41 satisfying-model records. It includes every branch input, source and branch products, selectors, coefficient images, all domain/companion axioms, every NS cofactor, and original-degree ceilings. Product and conditional-input differences are certified using old Boolean equations only. Every source companion and every source coefficient-field image is checked.

All 32 old Boolean states across the fixtures are checked, with new coefficient assignments satisfying the full retained family. Fixing every coefficient to branch zero fails on a valid retained-system model. Omitting the last residue also fails, despite the remaining coefficient images still being field-valued. Separate models make an actual mapped coefficient equal two while satisfying every companion and field domain. These controls distinguish correct conditioning from independent-variable assumptions, missing branches, or an invalid Boolean coefficient restriction.

The checker caches the fixed companion images used repeatedly during model evaluation. A protected rerun of the optimized code produced byte-for-byte identical complete output; the canonical certificate and model file is retained with reproduction commands and schema, hashes, and timing. All builds and mathematical checks passed. One guessed reading anchor was absent; the indexed passages were then read. The local fixtures have satisfiable typed domains and are not finite PHP refutations.

Route assessment. A complete family of actual positive-MOD inputs now reaches the affine endpoint with constant degree inflation and constant inventory overhead. The nonlinear source gap narrows by a structural class, while arbitrary positive-MOD tuples and the full dense multilevel source remain open.

Next bounded question. Test the branching construction on a bounded-depth binary source with a small span of nonlinear selector contributions in each block. Track complete companion and coefficient-field images and polynomial inventory, using a case with many dependent input positions to demonstrate coverage beyond the earlier sparse-position condition. Stop at a valid degree/inventory bound or a concrete obstruction.

14 September 2026 — Adapted source bases replace a position count by nonlinear rank

Status: working source-profile refinement and accuracy-dependent rank obstruction; exact original-input certificates and controls. The result concerns the coherent compact binary source with its stated compiler hypotheses. General Frege size lower bounds remain open.

Question and change of route. We considered branching on the few nonlinear values in a source block. Reading the existing affine-intersection machinery exposed a sufficient source-specific route: choose an adapted basis, keep its old affine part in one fresh block, and handle only the remaining independent inputs exactly. The missing step was pulling its prefixes back to the original input list without losing individual degree bounds. That step is proved below. A general multilevel raw-coefficient branching theorem is not claimed in this cycle.

1. The relevant rank is visible in the formal source

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) with the coherent compact source after the virtual clause boundary, before unrelated packing or conditioning. Its retained inputs have the exact form

\[ \widehat g_{a,i}(b,Z_{<a}) =L_{a,i}(b)+\sum_{c<a}\alpha_{a,i;c}Z_c, \qquad r_a=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2} (\alpha_{a,i;c})_{i,c}. \tag{RANK-source} \]

Here \(L_{a,i}\) is old-affine, \(Z_c\) names an earlier genuine selector product, and \(r_a\) counts the dimension of the nonlinear contributions, not their number of positions. Keep a single fixed coherent registry, including the subgroups required by the compiler. Uniform accuracy \(h\ge2\) gives input degrees \(d_{a,i}\), \(\delta_a=\max_i d_{a,i}\), and product weight \(w_a=h(\delta_a+1)\). Scalar/constant cases are cleaned up as before.

The ordinary weighted reflection theorem identifies these formal weighted degrees with actual polynomial degrees. In particular a nonzero selector contribution has degree at least \(h\). Let \(V_a\) be the constant-coefficient span of the input forms and let \(K_a\) be its intersection with the old affine forms. Projection onto the formal selector coordinates gives

\[ \dim V_a-\dim K_a=r_a. \]

Choose a basis \(A_1,\ldots,A_q\) of \(K_a\). Extend it by processing the original input list in nondecreasing weighted degree; the additional vectors \(G_1,\ldots,G_{r_a}\) can be chosen from the original inputs themselves. Every original input of degree \(d_i\) then has a constant-coefficient representation using only basis elements of degree at most \(d_i\). This applies the earlier full affine-intersection construction; the new use retains an affine core of arbitrary rank instead of requiring that the entire basis fit a packing bound.

2. The profile and the original-prefix pullback

Proceed in source dependency order. Interpret each earlier selector by its already constructed value of degree at most its original weight. Every current original input then still has degree at most \(d_i\). The \(A_j\)'s remain old-affine, because their selector coordinates cancel formally. Put \(\Delta_j=\deg_wG_j\); since each \(G_j\) was selected from the original list, it retains that input's individual degree bound.

If \(K_a\ne0\), introduce one fresh accuracy-\(h\) affine block on its basis, with product \(A\), exact prefixes \(U_j\), companions \(A_jA\), and cost \(s_A=2h\). If \(K_a=0\), use \(A=1,s_A=0\). Set

\[ v=A\prod_{j=1}^{r_a}(1-G_j),\qquad s=s_A+\sum_{j=1}^{r_a}\Delta_j. \tag{RANK-value} \]

All selected \(G_j\)'s are binary source inputs on earlier values. Boolean-domain division supplies \(G_j^2-G_j\) through \(2\Delta_j\), avoiding the new core's own coefficients. The existing product-profile argument therefore gives, for the basis inputs, companions through \(s+\deg_w(\text{basis input})\), Booleanity through \(2s\), and the exact prefix identity

\[ 1-v=\sum_{\nu=1}^q U_\nu A_\nu +\sum_{j=1}^{r_a} A\prod_{t<j}(1-G_t)\,G_j. \tag{RANK-prefix} \]

For example, an affine companion is multiplied by the exact tail. A selected companion uses \(G_j(1-G_j)=-(G_j^2-G_j)\), multiplied by the other factors. These witnesses hold over one common final system consisting of the old base and the fresh old-affine blocks.

The important pullback. Write \(A_\nu=\sum_i\beta_{\nu i}g_i\) in the original inputs, and write \(G_j=g_{i_j}\), using its selected original position. The original-input prefix is

\[ W_i=\sum_\nu\beta_{\nu i}U_\nu +\sum_{j:i_j=i}A\prod_{t<j}(1-G_t). \tag{RANK-original-prefix} \]

It gives the exact identity \(1-v=\sum_iW_i g_i\). An affine prefix has degree at most \(2h-1\), even if its affine basis vector was formed using original inputs of large degree. Consequently

\[ 2h-1+d_i\le h(\delta_a+1)=w_a, \]

because \(d_i\le\delta_a\) and the difference is at least \((h-1)(\delta_a-1)\). A selected-input prefix contributes only to its own original position, and its input-weighted degree is at most \(s\). Hence \(\deg W_i+d_i\le w_a\) whenever \(s\le w_a\). Using an arbitrary basis without this pullback would not supply the required original-input profile.

For original companions, use the adapted inverse representations. An input \(g_i\) uses only basis degrees at most \(d_i\), so \(g_iv\) has an NS certificate through \(s+d_i\le w_a+d_i\). The value has degree at most \(s\), and its Booleanity certificate fits \(2s\le2w_a\). Thus it is a complete costed profile of cost \(w_a\) for the original tuple, including its individual input bounds. A unit span uses value zero with its constant linear prefix witness; the zero tuple uses value one.

3. Rank below accuracy suffices throughout the source

Working source theorem. Suppose every retained block in the coherent compact binary registry satisfies \(r_a\le h-1\). Then all values have the preceding profiles within their original weights over one one-level affine-bit ENS family, with no increase in block or input inventory.

If \(r_a=0\), the block is already old-affine, and its profile costs at most \(w_a\). If \(r_a>0\), weighted reflection gives \(\delta_a\ge h\), so

\[ s\le2h+r_a\delta_a \le2h+(h-1)\delta_a \le h(\delta_a+1)=w_a. \tag{RANK-budget} \]

Induction in the strict source order now closes: preceding values stay within their original weights, the next adapted basis retains the degree bounds used above, and the next value has its profile in the same final system. There is at most one new affine core per original block, and its basis has no more members than the original input list. The full nonlinear input rank may be small even when every original input position depends on selectors.

The costed modular NS reconstruction preserves a supplied source NS degree \(D\). Alternatively, with source depth parameter \(d\) and \(L=(d+1)h^d\), the existing direct PC compiler gives degree

\[ D\le cL,\qquad c=\max(M_{\rm fr},10), \tag{RANK-PC-endpoint} \]

on the original proof DAG. Literal negation, aligned MOD2 scalars, coherent copies, and the original compact-clause residuals are retained. No proof-height factor is added. This refines the earlier dependent-position condition using its profiles and the older basis machinery.

The scope remains source-specific: no degree-preserving map of arbitrary raw source coefficients has been proved here. The modular witnesses are reconstructed, or the original logical proof is compiled using the new profiles. This distinction is why the prefix pullback to the original tuple matters.

4. Larger accuracy lowers the common-vanishing degree

The affine lower-bound engine can also be used beyond logarithmic accuracy. Let \(n=2^\ell,\ell\ge2\), \(m=n+1\), \(v=m\ell\), \(M\ge1\), and

\[ h\ge2(\ell+1),\qquad k=\left\lceil \sqrt{\frac{2m\ell\log(4M)}h} \right\rceil,\qquad B=k(D+1). \tag{RANK-accuracy} \]

Assume \(k\le m\), \(4(k-1)<n\), and \(n\ge2B-1\). Then a complete one-level affine-bit ENS family of at most \(M\) blocks and accuracy \(h\), over \(\mathcal Q_n\), has no degree-\(D\) PC refutation.

Proof. The ordinary-restriction argument uses low rank \(r\le h(k+1)\) and high threshold \(r_*=h(k+1)+1\). If \(r_*>v\), there are no high blocks. Otherwise

\[ \frac{\binom{v-r_*+k}{k}}{\binom mk\ell^k} =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1} \left(1- \frac{h(k+1)-(\ell+1)j}{v-\ell j}\right) \le \exp\left(-\frac{hk^2}{2m\ell}\right). \tag{RANK-dimension} \]

Indeed \(h\ge2(\ell+1)\) makes each subtracted numerator at least \(hk/2\), and each denominator is at most \(m\ell\). The definition of \(k\) makes the sum of high restriction dimensions at most one quarter of \(\binom mk\ell^k\), strictly below \(\dim\mathcal L_k\). A nonzero row-linear old \(f\) therefore vanishes ordinarily on every high flat.

The simultaneous packed/high-rank map and the weighted PC replay are unchanged: low coefficient degree is at most \(k\), high products become \(1-f\), and every weighted axiom image fits \(k\) times its original degree plus \(k\). The old consequence \(f\) would be derived through \(B\), contradicting row-linear separation and old stability under the displayed conditions. This refines the earlier sufficient parameter choice; it does not assume logarithmic \(h\) or polylogarithmic \(D\) in the finite statement.

5. A polynomial rank requirement for a hypothetical short compact proof

Fix a coherent compact binary proof, its source depth bound \(d\ge2\), and its formal registry after the virtual boundary. The coefficient matrices in (RANK-source) come from literal/MOD2 syntax and do not change merely because the approximation accuracy \(h\) changes. Bases may be recomputed for the new weights. This accuracy invariance is asserted for this fixed source construction, not for arbitrary optional preprocessing or for rank before Boolean label substitution.

Let \(R=\max_a r_a\). We may choose

\[ h=\max\{2(\ell+1),R+1\}. \]

Section 3 then supplies the one-level PC endpoint of degree \(D=O(h^d)\). The registry is built from formula occurrences and coherent groups; increasing \(h\) adds coefficient rows and changes product polynomials, rather than creating one block for each expanded monomial. Thus polynomial proof size and polynomially bounded \(h\) keep the affine inventory polynomial, so \(\log(4M)=O(\log n)\). Equation (RANK-accuracy) gives

\[ B=O\left(\sqrt n\,(\log n)h^{d-1/2}+h^d\right). \]

Suppose, for contradiction, that a sequence of polynomial-size compact proofs of fixed source depth has

\[ R\le\frac{n^{1/(2d-1)}}{(\log n)^2}. \tag{RANK-small} \]

For sufficiently large \(n\), the chosen accuracy is at most a constant times the right side. Consequently

\[ B= O\left( \frac{n}{(\log n)^{2d-2}} +\frac{n^{d/(2d-1)}}{(\log n)^{2d}} \right)=o(n). \]

Also \(k=o(n)\), so all conditions of Section 4 hold eventually. This is a contradiction. Therefore, for fixed proof-size exponent and fixed \(d\ge2\), every sufficiently large hypothetical compact proof satisfying the source hypotheses must have a retained block with dependent-selector rank greater than the bound in (RANK-small). Depth one is already the affine case.

This is a necessary structural condition on the compiled compact source. It does not exclude blocks with high nonlinear rank, prove those blocks essential by a separate certificate-support argument, or give a superpolynomial size bound for general Frege. In particular the ordinary-to-compact label conversion can introduce many selector directions; no invariance of the pre-conversion rank is claimed.

6. Exact source-profile and parameter evidence

The compiled checker uses two genuine old-affine bottom blocks \(B_0,B_1\) at \(h=2\), each on two old bits. Put \(F=P_{B_0}+P_{B_1}\), of original degree four, and take the parent tuple

\[ g_0=b_0,\qquad g_i=b_i+F\quad(1\le i\le4). \]

Four positions depend on selectors, but their coefficient matrix has rank one. Its full old-affine intersection has basis \(g_0,g_2+g_1,g_3+g_1,g_4+g_1\); the selected nonlinear basis input is \(g_1\). The complete rank, forward, and inverse matrices are saved. The parent weight is ten; the constructed value \(A(1-g_1)\) has cost eight. Every original prefix is checked against the individual degree list \((1,4,4,4,4)\).

Nine complete NS certificates verify earlier-input Booleanity, the exact original prefix residual, all five original companions, affine-core Booleanity, and value Booleanity. The earlier-input certificate avoids the new core's coefficients. All 512 old Boolean assignments have explicit satisfying extensions to the retained affine family; both value zero and value one occur. Omitting the affine-to-original prefix correction fails on a saved satisfying model, as does dropping the nonlinear tail.

An ungraded basis can express the degree-one input as a sum of degree-four vectors, violating the adapted-degree hypothesis; the saved control is a failure of that degree ledger, not a minimum NS-degree claim. Thus mere equality of input spans is not used as a substitute for individual source accounting.

Four exact integer dimension controls use \(n=64,\ell=6,M=1\). The triples \((h,k)=(14,9),(28,7),(56,5)\) satisfy \(4\binom{v-r_*+k}{k}<\binom{65}{k}6^k\). At \((h,k)=(4,17)\), the accuracy hypothesis is absent and this quarter bound fails. Counts are computed in guarded 128-bit arithmetic and stored as decimal strings. These check the dimension comparison only; no final small-board PHP degree contradiction is claimed.

The complete polynomials, matrices, NS cofactors, all models, and dimension counts accompany reproduction commands, hashes, and measured evidence. Compilation and all checks passed. The earlier shared-kernel optimization was completed and committed separately before this mathematical cycle.

Route assessment. The source collapse now measures independent nonlinear directions, with correct original-input prefixes, and adjustable accuracy turns it into a polynomial rank requirement at fixed depth. The full dense nonlinear family can still exceed that rank; the original Frege goal remains open.

Next bounded question. Test whether the actual first affine ENS level preserves a useful space of old row-linear targets at the degree budgets needed for continuation. Check a nonzero target rather than only a refutation, and identify the limitation when targets depend on selector values. Stop at a precise target-separation theorem or a counterexample.

14 September 2026 — The first affine level preserves old row-linear targets

Status: working old-target separation and partial-moment extension over every fixed prime; explicit selector-scope obstructions and exact finite controls. This does not yet remove a later nonlinear level or extend arbitrary selector moments.

Question and stopping point. Refutation exclusion alone does not describe which nonzero polynomials the first affine ENS level can derive. We prove separation for the old row-linear subspace and obtain an existential extension theorem for its moments. The product used in the proof need not itself be row-linear. Avoiding the leading target rows prevents Boolean annihilation, while a slightly broader cube detector proves the final contradiction.

1. A top row-linear monomial is enough for the old dual witness

Let \(n=2^\ell,\ell\ge2\), and let \(R(b)\) be an ordinary old-bit polynomial of degree \(u\le B\). Suppose some degree-\(u\) monomial with nonzero coefficient uses exactly one bit in each of \(u\) different pigeon rows. Other monomials of \(R\) may use several bits or powers within a row. Assume

\[ 4(u-1)<n,\qquad n\ge2B-1. \tag{TARGET-top-range} \]

Then \(\tau R\notin\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun})\), where \(\tau\) is the affine bit decoder. A nonzero constant is separated by an old normalized design.

Proof. For \(u\ge1\), use the signed two-point construction on the selected \(u\) rows and coordinates. Its disjoint coordinate edges remove \(2u\) labels, and a normalized residual matching design exists through \(B-u\), since \(n-2u\ge2(B-u)-1\). The resulting functional annihilates every old matching marginal, hence the full old \(\mathcal I_B=\mathcal C_B\).

Every monomial of \(R\) has degree at most \(u\). A monomial involving all selected \(u\) rows must therefore have degree exactly \(u\) and use one bit per selected row, with no other variables. All other monomials vanish against the supported matching moments. On the remaining terms, the mixed signed edge difference isolates the chosen bit-coordinate coefficient. Its nonzero value gives the contradiction. Thus the earlier dual proof detects a row-linear top-degree term, without requiring every term to be row-linear.

2. Choose the multiplier away from one leading target monomial

Let \(0\ne q\in\mathcal L_t\), the old span with at most one bit per row in each monomial, and put \(s=\deg q\le t\). Choose a degree-compatible monomial order. Its leading monomial occupies a set \(S_q\) of exactly \(s\) rows. Consider

\[ \mathcal V_{q,k}= \operatorname{span} \left\{\prod_{i\in S}b_{i,a_i}: S\subseteq[m]\setminus S_q,\ |S|\le k\right\}, \qquad m=n+1. \]

For any nonzero \(f\in\mathcal V_{q,k}\), the ordinary leading monomial of \(fq\) is the product of the two leading monomials. Their row sets are disjoint, so this is a row-linear monomial of degree \(\deg f+s\), with nonzero coefficient. The detector above applies whenever its board and degree bounds hold.

This reuses the earlier leading-row avoidance argument. Other terms of \(q\) may use multiplier rows and produce non-row-linear terms in \(fq\); they do not invalidate the top-term argument. Avoiding the entire support of \(q\) is unnecessary and could leave no useful multiplier variables.

The restriction is important. With \(q=1-b\) and \(f=bz\), both factors are nonzero Boolean functions, but \(fq=-z(b^2-b)\) is a Boolean consequence. An arbitrary nonzero multiplier can erase a nonzero target. No degree drop after Boolean reduction is silently treated as proof of nonvanishing.

3. Complete one-level affine systems have no such old consequences

Work over \(\mathbb F_p\) with the correct compact base \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\), and let \(\Gamma\) add a complete one-level affine-bit ENS family with at most \(M\ge1\) blocks and common accuracy

\[ h\ge h_0=3(p-1)\ell . \]

Coefficient domains are \(r^p-r\). If \(h>h_0\), setting the extra factor rows to zero restricts a proof to accuracy \(h_0\) without increasing degree or changing an old target. We may therefore use \(h_0\) in the construction.

Let \(0\le t\le D\), and choose an integer \(k\) satisfying

\[ k\ge\max\left\{1,\,2t,\, \left\lceil\sqrt{m\log(4M)}\right\rceil\right\}, \qquad k\le m-t,\qquad B=k(D+1). \]

Assume further that

\[ 4(k+t-1)<n,\qquad n\ge2B-1. \tag{TARGET-range} \]

Working theorem. Under these conditions,

\[ \mathcal C_D(\Gamma)\cap\mathcal L_t=\{0\}. \tag{TARGET-separation} \]

Proof. Suppose \(\Gamma\) proves a nonzero \(q\in\mathcal L_t\) through degree \(D\). Use the multiplier space \(\mathcal V_{q,k}\). It has dimension \(\sum_{j\le k}\binom{m-s}{j}\ell^j\), with \(s=\deg q\le t\).

First apply the same scalar cleanup to zero and unit spans as in the all-prime hybrid proof. Classify the remaining proper affine blocks: low rank has \((p-1)r\le h_0(k+1)\), while high rank begins at \(r_*=3\ell(k+1)+1\). If \(r_*>v=m\ell\), there are no high blocks. Otherwise the ordinary restriction image of \(\mathcal V_{q,k}\) on a high zero flat has dimension at most \(\binom{v-r+k}{k}\), and

\[ \frac{\binom{v-r_*+k}{k}}{\binom{m-t}{k}\ell^k} =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1} \left(1- \frac{r_*-1-\ell t-(\ell+1)j} {(m-t)\ell-\ell j}\right) \le e^{-k^2/m}. \tag{TARGET-dimension} \]

The subtracted numerator is at least

\[ (2\ell-1)k-\ell t+4\ell+1\ge\ell k, \]

because \(k\ge2t\) and \(\ell\ge2\). Denominators are at most \(m\ell\). The sum of high restriction dimensions is thus at most one quarter of the displayed top multiplier dimension. A nonzero \(f\in\mathcal V_{q,k}\) vanishes as an ordinary polynomial on every high flat.

Use the same simultaneous old-only coefficient substitution as in the refutation theorem. Low blocks are packed with coefficient degree at most \(k\). High blocks use \(p-1\) factor rows, giving product \(1-f^{p-1}\). Multiply every substituted line of the proof of \(q\) by \(f\). The previously certified weighted companion and field images and primitive PC replay stay within \(B=k(D+1)\). Since the target is old, the final polynomial is \(fq\), not a substituted selector value.

Its degree is at most \(k+t\le B\). Section 2 gives a nonzero row-linear top-degree monomial, and (TARGET-range) supplies the detector's conditions. The old compact proof of \(fq\) would decode to a forbidden functional-PHP PC consequence through \(B\). This proves (TARGET-separation). Only the target changed from the earlier hybrid argument; no old conditioned axiom or augmented NS/PC equality was introduced.

For every fixed prime, polynomial \(M\), and polylogarithmic \(D,t\) with \(t\le D\), these conditions hold eventually with the displayed \(k\). Hence the qualitative consequence exclusion holds throughout that range, over the complete original affine family.

4. Arbitrary values on that old subspace extend

The degree-\(D\) PC consequence space is a linear subspace of the finite-dimensional space of polynomials through degree \(D\). Equation (TARGET-separation) makes its sum with \(\mathcal L_t\) a direct sum. For any linear functional \(\lambda\) on \(\mathcal L_t\), define a functional on this sum to be zero on \(\mathcal C_D(\Gamma)\) and equal to \(\lambda\) on \(\mathcal L_t\), then extend it linearly to the whole degree-\(D\) space.

Thus every prescribed \(\lambda\) on the old row-linear subspace extends to an annihilator of all degree-\(D\) PC consequences of \(\Gamma\). If \(\lambda(1)=1\), the extension is normalized and also annihilates every legal degree-\(D\) NS multiple. This is an existential partial-moment extension, with no positivity, multiplicativity, or efficient sampler claimed.

It does not preserve an arbitrarily specified full old degree-\(t\) functional: moments with multiple bits in a row are outside the prescribed subspace. It also does not assert that augmented PC and NS spaces coincide. The earlier critical-band theorem preserves all old moments in its narrower NS range; the two results have different hypotheses and coverage.

The complete power-input and shared-probe transfers fix old bits and cost only a constant factor in degree for fixed \(p\). Therefore the same qualitative old row-linear consequence exclusion, and its partial-moment corollary, apply to those original one-level source classes at polylogarithmic degree. No such raw-target transfer is inferred merely from the source-specific rank-profile interpretation.

5. Selector coordinates have additional relations

A nonconstant selector already depends on old moments. For a block on the single Boolean input \(b\), write \(1-P=Ub\). The ordinary identity

\[ P-(1-b)=bP+U(b^2-b) \]

has an NS certificate through \(2h+1\). Therefore, once that degree fits, every normalized annihilator satisfies \(\Lambda(P)=1-\Lambda(b)\). The old choice \(\Lambda(b)=0\) cannot be combined with an independent choice \(\Lambda(P)=0\). Both selector values occur on satisfying models; this is a coupling constraint, not just a forced constant.

Even a proper noninitial selector can be forced to zero. Take an affine input tuple containing all pair-difference forms \(g_t=b_{it}-b_{i't}\), possibly with additional independent affine inputs. With \(E^{(p)}_{ii'}\) in the old compact base,

\[ P=E^{(p)}_{ii'}P+ \sum_t g_t^{p-2} \prod_{s<t}(1-g_s^{p-1})\,(g_tP) \]

derives \(P=0\) through \(2h+(p-1)\ell\). This reuses the initial/weakening witness. The tuple can have rank above a scalar or low-rank packing threshold by adding extra forms. Such a block may be removed by a suitable old-base-aware preprocessing step, but it cannot be treated as a freely assignable selector coordinate before that step.

These examples locate the remaining limitation: the theorem supplies old row-linear freedom, while later source inputs involve selector values and their mixed moments. A useful extension must specify the selector relations it preserves.

6. New target checks reuse complete moment evidence

The compiled checker reads the already verified complete moment files from the binary audit and signed \(\mathbb F_3\) audit. It does not rerun their marginal enumeration. New evaluations use the saved top matching moments, with powers and same-row products decoded by the functional row normal form.

For each of the \(n=8\) and \(n=32\) fixtures, choose an old linear target whose leading coordinate is in row zero, whose other term uses a different bit in row one, and whose constant term is one. Its multiplier is the product of the selected coordinates in the other witness rows. The product has a within-row quadratic term, but also the required row-linear top term. Its moment value is one over \(\mathbb F_2\) and two over \(\mathbb F_3\), matching the chosen leading coefficient.

The four corresponding zero-divisor controls use \((1-b)\,bz=-z(b^2-b)\), with a complete old Boolean NS witness and zero moment value. Two full selector NS controls per field verify the old-coordinate relation and a rank-three proper selector forced to zero. The latter adds a literal to a two-row compact pair tuple; removing its old collision equation restores a satisfying model with selector value one. Four typed selector models per field and explicit incompatible partial-moment assignments are retained.

Three exact dimension cases, repeated in both field runs, use \(n=64,\ell=6,k=10\). Excluding zero or five leading rows satisfies the quarter-dimension bound; excluding 55 rows fails it. These are component checks of the available multiplier dimension, not finite instances of the final PC budget inequalities.

The complete new binary output and signed output accompany commands and source-data references, hashes, and timing. All mathematical checks passed; a preliminary indentation warning was corrected.
