14 September 2026 — A genuine obstruction to universal Boolean-domain normalization

Status: working method obstruction for complete three-level sources, over every prime; the PHP-relative and proof-specific routes remain open. Cycle 149.

Obligation and outcome. Test the general local-profile step proposed in cycle 148, rather than another special tensor. A universal normalization that certifies its source images using Booleanity alone is too strong: a polynomial-size approximate-majority circuit gives a complete three-level source that forbids the required old-degree budget. The same example rules out universally small profiles over one affine family when their identities hold over the Boolean domain without the PHP axioms. This is a restriction on the proposed method, not a Frege upper bound or a proof that such a circuit must occur essentially in a short PHP proof.

1. The certifying-polynomial obstruction

A Boolean function \(C:\{0,1\}^v\to\{0,1\}\) is an \((a,v-a)\)-approximate majority if \(C=0\) on weights at most \(a\), and \(C=1\) on weights at least \(v-a\). Kopparty and Srinivasan's Definition 2.1 and Lemma 3.3 give the binary certifying-polynomial obstruction. We use its elementary Boolean-cube argument over an arbitrary field.

All-field form. Every nonzero multilinear polynomial of degree at most \(a\) meets both Hamming balls, so its nonzero support cannot have constant \(C\)-value. Indeed, choose an inclusion-minimal nonzero monomial coefficient \(c_S\). Evaluation at the indicator of \(S\) gives \(c_S\ne0\), at weight at most \(a\). Replacing all variables by \(1-x_i\) preserves degree and nonzeroness and gives a nonzero point in the opposite ball. This proof works over every field. These are imported mathematical ideas, not a new circuit lower bound.

Partial-representation consequence. Let \(W\) have nonzero Boolean remainder, and suppose a polynomial \(V\) agrees with \(C\) wherever \(W\ne0\). Then

\[ \deg W+\deg V\ge a+1. \tag{CP-partial} \]

To prove this, Boolean-reduce \(WV\) and \(W(1-V)\). Their sum is the nonzero Boolean remainder of \(W\), so at least one is nonzero. Its support is contained in one output class of \(C\), and its degree is at most \(\deg W+\deg V\). Apply the preceding obstruction. No requirement that \(W\) be a Boolean-valued polynomial is needed.

2. A polynomial-size source in the actual affine-in-selector grammar

For completeness, the needed nonuniform depth-three approximate-majority circuit has the following probabilistic existence proof. This is a standard type of approximate-counting construction; the source application below is the point of this entry. Let \(v\ge8\), and put

\[ t=\lceil3\log_2v\rceil,\qquad r=\left\lceil4v(3/2)^t\right\rceil. \]

Form \(v\) independently sampled DNFs. Each has \(r\) terms, each term an AND of \(t\) independently sampled positive input variables, with replacement. Let \(C\) be the AND of these DNFs.

For an input of weight at most \(v/3\), one DNF accepts with probability at most \(r3^{-t}\le4/v^2+3^{-t}<1/4\). All \(v\) accept with probability at most \(4^{-v}\). For weight at least \(2v/3\), one DNF rejects with probability at most \(\exp[-r(2/3)^t]\le e^{-4v}\), so \(C\) rejects with probability at most \(ve^{-4v}\). A union bound over all old inputs has failure probability at most

\[ 2^v(4^{-v}+ve^{-4v})<1. \]

Thus a fixed choice computes an \((a,v-a)\)-approximate majority for \(a=\lfloor v/3\rfloor\). Since \(r\le7v^3\), it has polynomial gate and wire count, with three AND/OR layers. Repeated sampled literals can be deleted inside a term without changing the function.

Complete evaluation source. Use any common positive accuracy \(h\), over any \(\mathbb F_p\). A bottom block \(Z_{ab}\) has inputs \(1-x_{i(a,b,j)}\). A middle block \(Y_a\) has inputs \(Z_{ab}\), for the terms in its DNF. The top block \(Z\) has inputs \(Y_a\). Retain every companion and every own coefficient field equation.

On every solution of these source equations extending an old Boolean input, a product is one if all its inputs are zero, and zero otherwise: the first assertion follows from its defining product, and the second from a nonzero input's companion. Inducting through the three levels gives

\[ Z_{ab}=\bigwedge_j x_{i(a,b,j)},\qquad Y_a=1-\bigvee_b Z_{ab},\qquad Z=C(x). \tag{CP-evaluation} \]

Such a solution exists for every old input. At each nonzero tuple choose a first-row coefficient making that row's linear sum one, and set unused rows to zero; for a zero tuple any coefficient choice works. Thus this is a genuine satisfiable evaluation source, not an inconsistent model invented by omitting a field equation.

Its inputs are old-affine or individual earlier selectors, a subclass of the full compact source grammar. The original product weights are

\[ w_1=2h,\qquad w_2=h(2h+1),\qquad w_3=h\bigl(h(2h+1)+1\bigr). \tag{CP-source-weights} \]

For \(h=3\ell\) and \(v=(n+1)\ell\), inventory is polynomial in \(n\) and the weights are polylogarithmic. No claim is made that every normalized short PHP proof contains this source. It refutes a proposed universal theorem covering all complete sources of the displayed grammar; a narrower proof-specific theorem would need its own coverage argument.

3. A universal Boolean-domain old-only map cannot meet the required budget

Working obstruction. Let \(\sigma\) fix the old bits and send every coefficient of the source in Section 2 to an old polynomial. Let \(W\) be an old polynomial with nonzero Boolean remainder. Suppose every weighted source axiom image \(W\sigma(F)\) vanishes on the old Boolean cube. Then

\[ \deg W+\deg\sigma(Z)\ge\lfloor v/3\rfloor+1. \tag{CP-map-barrier} \]

In particular, if coefficient images have degree at most \(T\ge1\), any ledger \(B=TD_0+\deg W\) with \(D_0\ge w_3\) must satisfy \(B\ge\lfloor v/3\rfloor+1\).

Proof. At an old Boolean point where \(W\ne0\), all substituted source equations hold. Equation (CP-evaluation) therefore forces \(\sigma(Z)=C\) at that point. Apply (CP-partial). The degree substitution bound \(\deg\sigma(Z)\le Tw_3\le TD_0\) gives the ledger conclusion. This argument allows the map and weight to depend arbitrarily on the complete source. \(\square\)

For compact PHP, \(v=(n+1)\ell\), so the recent target \(B\le n/4\), and more generally \(B=o(n)\), contradict this lower bound for sufficiently large \(n\). The obstruction still applies if the old PHP axioms are appended but the non-base images are certified by Booleanity alone. Merely adding \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\) to the written base does not change that hypothesis.

What can escape. Images certified using genuine old PHP consequences need not vanish on all old Boolean assignments, so (CP-evaluation) need not hold on the weight's support. Likewise a proved normalization of the source of a short PHP proof might avoid these circuits. Neither escape is established here. The theorem does not exclude PHP-relative certificates, justified restrictions that preserve a sufficient old barrier, or proof-specific source transformations.

4. The same obstruction reaches small profiles over one affine family

Let \(\Gamma_{\rm dom}\) contain old Booleanity and a complete one-level old-affine ENS family, with at most \(M\ge1\) proper blocks after constant cleanup. It does not include the PHP collision axioms. The following is the domain-only part of the existing affine construction.

Write \(a_p=p-1\), and assume

\[ 3\le k=\left\lceil\sqrt{v\ln(4M)}\right\rceil\le v/2,\qquad \delta=a_pk,\qquad T=2a_p(k+1)-1. \tag{CP-affine-map} \]

There is a nonzero Boolean-valued old weight \(F\) of degree at most \(\delta\), and an old-only coefficient map \(\theta\) of degree at most \(T\), such that every point with \(F=1\) extends through \(\theta\) to a model of \(\Gamma_{\rm dom}\).

Proof of the needed construction. In the full homogeneous squarefree degree-\(k\) space, an affine flat of rank \(r\ge2k+3\) has ordinary restriction-image dimension at most

\[ \binom{v-r+k}{k}\le e^{-k^2/v}\binom vk. \]

The ratio is a product of \(k\) factors \(1-(r-k)/(v-j)\). Summing over high blocks costs at most one quarter of the domain dimension. A common nonzero multilinear \(f\) therefore vanishes ordinarily on every high flat, with literal representations \(f=\sum_i c_i g_i\), \(\deg c_i\le k-1\). Put \(F=f^{p-1}\). On a high block choose first-row coefficients \(c_i f^{p-2}\), giving product \(1-F\). On a low block of rank \(r\le2(k+1)\), telescope the factors \(1-\alpha L_j\), \(\alpha\in\mathbb F_p^*\), into one row, giving the exact flat indicator \(\prod_j(1-L_j^{p-1})\) with coefficient degrees at most \((p-1)r-1\le T\). Pull back basis coefficients to the original tuple and set all later rows zero. Unit and zero spans use their constant maps.

The weight is Boolean-valued on old Boolean points and is nonzero because \(f\) is nonzero multilinear. On its support every companion and every genuine coefficient field equation holds. This uses no old PHP axiom and no old-target separation theorem. \(\square\)

Profile lower bound. Suppose a polynomial \(V\) of ordinary degree at most \(s\) equals the approximate-majority value on every model of \(\Gamma_{\rm dom}\) over each old input. Then

\[ \delta+Ts\ge\lfloor v/3\rfloor+1. \tag{CP-affine-profile-barrier} \]

Indeed \(\theta(V)\) agrees with \(C\) on \(F=1\), and (CP-partial) applies. For fixed \(p\), quasipolynomial \(M\), and polylogarithmic \(s\), the left side is \(\sqrt v\,\operatorname{polylog}v=o(v)\), which is impossible. More quantitatively \(s\ge(\lfloor v/3\rfloor+1-\delta)/T\) whenever the numerator is positive.

Complete costed profiles for the evaluation circuit, whose prefix and companion identities hold over \(\Gamma_{\rm dom}\), force their interpreted values to compute the corresponding gates on its models. Consequently they satisfy the hypothesis for the root \(V\). This rules out universally polylogarithmic-cost Boolean-domain profiles even with quasipolynomially many new affine cores, and even if the values use raw coefficients. The construction in cycle 148 remains valid; its cost cannot always be improved to the required small bound while keeping this stronger domain-validity property.

Profiles over \(\Gamma_{\rm dom}+\mathcal Q_{n,p}\) are different. That full system has no Boolean models, so semantic correctness on its models is vacuous. Their usefulness must come from the original-degree NS witnesses. The current compiler permits such PHP-relative residuals; obtaining them efficiently is a real remaining route, rather than a consequence of the Boolean-domain construction.

5. An earlier interface control: bare profile data also forget free parameters

The first test in this cycle found a separate, weaker obstruction to a closure lemma stated for arbitrary costed profiles. It is retained because it identifies a different missing assumption.

Degree control. Let \(\Gamma\subseteq\mathbb F_2[Y]\), let \(z_1,\ldots,z_q\) be new Boolean variables, and suppose \(1\notin\mathcal I_{s+1}(\Gamma)\). There is no cost-\(s\) profile for the tuple \((z_1,\ldots,z_q)\), with declared input bounds \(\mu_i=1\), over \(\Gamma+{\rm BOOL}_z\) if \(s<q\).

Choose a normalized linear functional on \(\mathcal P_{\le s+1}(Y)\) annihilating \(\mathcal I_{s+1}(\Gamma)\), and apply it coefficientwise in \(z\) to the proposed prefix and companion identities. Original NS degree accounting makes every \(\Gamma\)-multiple vanish and leaves only Boolean multiples in \(z\). The resulting polynomial \(v(z)\), of degree at most \(s\), obeys \(v(0)=1\) and \(z_i v=0\) on every Boolean point. Its unique multilinear representative is \(\prod_i(1-z_i)\), of degree \(q\), a contradiction. This argument continues to hold after adjoining further helpers that do not involve \(z\), as long as the displayed base non-refutation assumption holds.

Each individual value \(z_i\) has a cost-one profile on input \(1-z_i\). Conversely the joint zero-test has a cost-\(q\) profile using \(v=\prod_i(1-z_i)\), prefixes \(U_i=\prod_{j<i}(1-z_j)\), and companions

\[ z_i v=-(z_i^2-z_i)\prod_{j\ne i}(1-z_j). \]

Booleanity has its product-profile certificate through \(2q\). Thus the bound is exact over a satisfiable Boolean base; over a PHP base only the stated degree-window lower bound is asserted.

These directions can be genuine coefficient directions. A proper affine block on \((x,y,x+y)\) has, in each row, the invertible linear coefficient change

\[ r_1=u_1+z,\quad r_2=u_2+z,\quad r_3=z,\qquad r_1x+r_2y+r_3(x+y)=u_1x+u_2y. \]

The product loses \(z\); its third companion is the sum of the first two. The three coefficient Boolean equations become \({\rm BOOL}_{u_1}+{\rm BOOL}_z\), \({\rm BOOL}_{u_2}+{\rm BOOL}_z\), and \({\rm BOOL}_z\). The inverse change has the same degree-one property, so the complete system is exactly a two-input affine block plus a free Boolean parameter per row, with original degrees preserved. Repeated blocks give arbitrarily many such parameters without zero or duplicate inputs in the displayed triple.

This does not make the values \(z_i\) legitimate selector-valued logical children. The actual source values, and the present adapted-basis profiles, are built from old bits and whole selector products. Raw coefficient prefixes and witnesses need not have that form. The earlier selector-scope warning already distinguishes them. Section 4 supplies the stronger obstruction even after this source distinction is restored.

6. What selector-valuedness does, and what it does not give

Over \(\Gamma_{\rm dom}\), every old assignment has an extension, and each whole affine product equals the indicator of the common zero flat of its inputs. Hence an expression in old bits and whole products has the same value for all coefficient choices extending a fixed old input. This is a semantic observation, not a low-degree certificate allowing every product to be replaced by its flat indicator.

There is also a useful representation consequence. Suppose \(V=H(b,A_1,\ldots,A_M)\) is an ordinary polynomial in distinct genuine affine products with disjoint own coefficients, after constant cleanup, and \(\deg V\le s\). By ordinary degree reflection, \(\deg_w H\le s\), so its unweighted formal degree is at most \(s\). Boolean-reduce the formal variables for the purpose of evaluating the induced function. There are at most \(\sum_{j\le s}\binom{v+M}{j}\) surviving monomials. Each is the indicator of an intersection of affine flats and old conditions \(b_i=1\). Thus, over \(\mathbb F_2\), the induced function is an XOR of at most that many affine-flat indicators.

With quasipolynomial \(M\) and polylogarithmic \(s\), this is a quasipolynomial representation. It permits cancellations outside the final support, so it is not a DNF or a cover by monochromatic flats. No lower bound for DNF of parities was imported as a bound on this representation. Moreover a PHP-relative profile need not compute the intended Boolean gate on all models of \(\Gamma_{\rm dom}\); one must not infer such a circuit representation of the original function merely from identities using the unsatisfiable PHP base.

7. Evidence, scope, and the resulting route change

The reproduction note and complete exact output retain a fixed eight-bit depth-three circuit with eight DNFs, 1,231 terms each, sampled width nine, and seed 1490001. All 256 old assignments satisfy the required weight-two/weight-six conditions. Every term mask and every truth-table value is saved.

They certify that no nonzero polynomial of degree at most two has monochromatic support. Two higher-degree nonzero certifiers and their full supports provide positive controls. This is a local Boolean circuit fixture, not a PHP instance. The three-level source degree ledgers are symbolic; the checker does not claim to enumerate that large source's coefficient assignments.

15 September 2026 — What the PHP-relative escape still requires

Status: interface audit, a working formal-input limitation, and reuse of existing relative normalizers; no new general source compression. Cycle 150.

Obligation and stopping point. After the Boolean-domain obstruction, test whether using old PHP residuals supplies a new affordable source step. Check the existing tools first, and distinguish a new construction from merely replacing the name of the base ideal.

1. The compiler already permits the needed kind of residual

The costed profile definition is relative to a fixed system \(\Gamma\). It permits \(\Gamma=\mathcal Q_n+\mathcal E_{\rm aff}+{\rm BOOL}\); it never required all witnesses to use Booleanity alone. Prefix residuals, companions, and Booleanity must still have supplied ordinary NS certificates at their declared costs. The product and OR identities retain those residuals, and the logical PC compiler uses their costs. No new compiler theorem is needed merely to allow an old collision term.

The earlier relative-learning theorem also already allows \(f-H_a\in\mathcal I_c(\mathcal F)\), rather than Boolean vanishing. Its remaining condition is the existence of a shared old class outside the affordable old ideal, with a sufficient replay budget. The relative quotient criterion and its finite controls explicitly left that existence condition open.

Reused input-replacement argument. If \(g_i-g_i'\) has an explicit old-base NS certificate through the original input degree \(d_i\), and \(\deg g_i'\le d_i\), the existing telescoping proof gives

\[ P-P'\in\mathcal I_{w_a},\qquad g_iP=g_i'P'+(g_i-g_i')P'+g_i(P-P'), \qquad w_a=h_a(\delta_a+1). \]

The old companion is thus derivable from the new one through its original degree \(d_i+w_a\); own fields are unchanged. This works with certified PHP residuals. It does not supply an arbitrary degree-preserving normal form modulo the full PHP ideal. Higher current polynomials also need not retain the original affine-in-selector syntax after such replacements.

2. Old-base rewriting alone cannot change the formal selector coefficients

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\). Let \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb F_2[b]\) contain old Booleanity and satisfy \(1\notin\mathcal I_B(\mathcal F)\). Give independent formal variables \(Z_j\) fixed positive integer weights. Let \(\mathcal I_B^w\) charge each ordinary generator multiple at its weighted degree, including any formal equations \(Z_j^2-Z_j\).

Working rigidity observation. Suppose

\[ G=L(b)+\sum_j\alpha_jZ_j,\qquad G'=L'(b)+\sum_j\alpha_j'Z_j,\qquad G-G'\in\mathcal I_B^w(\mathcal F+{\rm BOOL}_Z), \tag{RI-formal} \]

where \(L,L'\) are old-affine and the selector coefficients are constants. Then \(\alpha_j=\alpha_j'\) for every \(j\), and \(L-L'\in\mathcal I_B(\mathcal F)\).

Proof. Set all formal selectors to zero in the supplied certificate. This gives \(L-L'\in\mathcal I_B(\mathcal F)\). Set only \(Z_j=1\), and all others zero, and subtract the two certificates. This gives the constant \(\alpha_j-\alpha_j'\) in the same old space. A nonzero such constant would give a degree-\(B\) old refutation. Every substitution preserves old degrees and sends formal Boolean equations to zero, so no NS multiplication closure was assumed. \(\square\)

For the compact binary PHP base, the old row-linear separation also excludes nonzero old-affine members in this range when \(B\ge1\) and \(n\ge2B-1\). Thus \(L=L'\) there. Entrywise old-certified changes of this formal form do not reduce the selector rank.

A related one-way old-target projection. Let \(G_i=L_i(b)+\sum_j\alpha_{ij}Z_j\), and let \(A\) be the full old-affine intersection of their constant-coefficient span. If an old polynomial \(f\) belongs to \(\mathcal I_B^w(\mathcal F+G+{\rm BOOL}_Z)\), then

\[ f\in\mathcal I_B(\mathcal F+A). \tag{RI-old-target} \]

If \(1\in A\), the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise choose an affine basis for \(A\) and extend it by input combinations \(H_1,\ldots,H_r\) whose selector coefficient rows are independent. A constant right inverse lets us assign the formal \(Z_j\)'s old-affine polynomials making every \(H_j\) zero. Each original input then becomes a constant combination of \(A\). Old variables are fixed. This substitution does not increase weighted degree, and an image \(\ell(b)^2-\ell(b)\) of a formal Boolean equation has an old Boolean certificate through two, within its original weight \(2w_j\). Applying the substitution to the supplied NS witness proves (RI-old-target). If \(A=0\), there is no nontrivial old class beyond \(\mathcal I_B(\mathcal F)\).

This is a forward filtered implication, not an equality of ideals at the same degree. Pulling an affine basis back to higher-degree original generators can cost more, as the earlier exact NS/PC degree control illustrates.

Scope that matters. These statements concern independent formal selectors. An actual identity whose cofactors and named generators all lie in the genuine selector subring can be lifted using ordinary degree reflection, under its nonzero-tuple and disjoint-coefficient hypotheses. Arbitrary raw coefficient-domain witnesses cannot be lifted this way. Nor may actual ENS products be assigned arbitrary affine values just because the formal \(Z_j\)'s can. The existing quotient warning remains essential.

Accordingly this rules out one shortcut: reduce the formal linear inputs using only old-base identities and expect their nonlinear coefficient matrix to shrink. It does not rule out reinterpreting earlier products, using their genuine ENS relations, or constructing PHP-relative profiles with raw internal witnesses.

3. The natural collision-relative control is an existing mechanism

The column-state normalizer already gives degree-preserving coefficient maps for arbitrary polynomial inputs in a single unary PHP column, using its collision equations. That was the first natural positive candidate in this cycle, so it is treated as reused work.

Its compact binary version is transparent. For a fixed label \(\lambda\), let \(\chi_i\) be the degree-\(\ell\) Boolean indicator that pigeon \(i\) has label \(\lambda\). Then

\[ \chi_i\chi_j-\chi_i E_{ij}\in\mathcal I_{2\ell}({\rm BOOL}), \qquad \chi_i\chi_j\in\mathcal I_{2\ell}(\mathcal Q_n). \]

The first polynomial vanishes on the Boolean cube and has degree at most \(2\ell\), so ordinary Boolean division supplies its certificate. For \(v_\lambda=1-\sum_i\chi_i\),

\[ 1-v_\lambda=\sum_i\chi_i,\qquad \chi_i v_\lambda =-(\chi_i^2-\chi_i)-\sum_{j\ne i}\chi_i\chi_j \in\mathcal I_{2\ell}(\mathcal Q_n). \]

Binary Booleanity of \(v_\lambda\) fits \(2\ell\). Thus the literal old-input tuple has a cost-\(\ell\) PHP-relative profile. If it comes from label-selector bottoms of original weight \(2h\), \(2h\ge\ell\), retain input bounds \(2h\) and profile cost \(2h\), rather than silently resetting those source bounds.

This is not a Boolean-domain-valid profile: at an assignment where exactly two pigeons have label \(\lambda\), \(v_\lambda=1\) and the corresponding companion is nonzero. The collision equation supplies the missing certificate. This shows that the escape from cycle 149 is real, but it does not enlarge the general source coverage beyond the existing column mechanism.

4. Checks that did not supply the general step

A sparse-support refinement would not address the complete source boundary. If all collision residuals in a profile package involve only \(q\le n\) pigeon rows, fix those rows to distinct labels. Those residuals vanish, the remaining affine helpers stay affine, and the package becomes Boolean-domain-valid on \(v'=v-q\ell\) free bits. The restricted approximate-majority circuit still has the two Hamming balls of radius at least \(\lfloor v/3\rfloor-q\ell\). For \(q=o(n)\), the previous obstruction remains linear in \(v'\). However the actual compact-clause boundary uses all pigeon pairs, so its residual support is already global. Developing this sparse condition would not discharge the current obligation.

A targeted primary-source check also prevented a misleading literature inference. Lu, Santhanam, and Tzameret (2025) study a DNF family expressing hardness of algebraic proof lower bounds. Their abstract states that small \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege proofs fail infinitely often, while whether that DNF family consists of tautologies remains open. This is not an unconditional lower bound for a known PHP tautology family. Only the versioned abstract and scope were checked; no theorem from its diagonalization proof is imported.

5. What changed and what remains

No new general compression was obtained. PHP-relative residuals were already allowed by the formal interfaces, and the positive column construction was already available. The new formal-input observation excludes a tempting old-ideal rewriting shortcut. The missing step is still a cheap interpretation or coupled witness construction that uses both the PHP base and the genuine earlier ENS relations, with enough control to apply to the full compiled source.

The next cycle should test such coupling at the complete source-module level, using the earlier moment and joint-selector interfaces where their hypotheses hold. A formal free-selector calculation or another isolated column family is not a substitute for that application. The degree budget and the approximate-majority obstruction remain the stopping tests.

The audit note records the exact reused sources, proof scope, and abstract-only literature check. No new numerical suite was needed for the linear-algebra and certificate arguments above.

15 September 2026 — Third-party chessboard filling interface and a route to its proof

Status: checked Lean statement and tentative proof plan; H is not proved or assumed as an axiom.

Assignment. The user prioritized the third-party boundary of the bit-PHP publication route, requested a separate third-party claim directory with cross-imports, and asked for an exact formal interface and an initial dependency order. This turn states that interface and plans its proof; it does not assert a new homology theorem or change the main Frege research objective.

H: the precise prior-literature claim

The new indexed target third-party:BLVZ-chessboard-filling is the needed consequence of Björner–Lovász–Vrećica–Živaljević, Theorem 1.1. Let \(\mathcal M_k(s,N)\) be the set of \(k\)-cell matchings on an \(s\times N\) board: finite cell sets with injective row and column projections. Put \(C_k=\mathbb F_2^{\mathcal M_k(s,N)}\). These are chains of reduced simplicial degree \(k-1\); in particular \(C_0\) is the empty-face augmentation coordinate.

For \(k\ge1\), define the boundary by

\[ (\partial_k c)(T)=\sum_{\substack{S\in\mathcal M_k(s,N)\\T\subset S}}c(S) \qquad(T\in\mathcal M_{k-1}(s,N)). \]

All incidence signs are one over \(\mathbb F_2\). The boundary from \(C_1\) sums the vertex coefficients; the outgoing map at \(C_0\) is zero. The target is

\[ s\ge2,\ N\ge2s-1,\ c\in C_{s-1},\ \partial_{s-1}c=0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \exists b\in C_s:\ \partial_s b=c. \]

MathResearch.ThirdParty.ChessboardFilling in ChessboardFilling.lean defines exactly this proposition. Faces use Fin s × Fin N, chains are functions on the finite face type, and the boundary tests codimension-one inclusion. The zero-cell-count branch of the boundary definition handles the augmentation endpoint; H itself restricts to \(s\ge2\). A transparent face-type abbreviation permits Lean to infer finiteness. There is no declaration asserting H, no custom axiom, and no sorry. The general boundary-squared-zero proof remains a planned task.

Proposed dependency route

The Third-party boundary section now prioritizes thirteen steps: augmented chain infrastructure; boundary-squared-zero; relabeling and inclusion maps; cone contractions; simplex-boundary vanishing; finite cover double-complex exactness; the homological cover lemma; first-row star coverage; intersection descriptions; the nerve identification; induction arithmetic; the homological chessboard bound; and specialization to H.

The plan follows the paper appendix and is a guide, not a correctness audit of every proposed intermediate lemma. It deliberately includes the stronger intermediate range \(\nu(a,b)=\min(a,b,\lfloor(a+b+1)/3\rfloor)\), with reduced acyclicity through \(\nu-2\): star intersections have the form \(\Delta_{a-1,b-t}\) and do not all remain in H's narrow column range. A direct finite-chain proof may later shorten or replace the cover machinery. No stronger homotopical connectivity theorem is required. Matching-moment construction remains the consumer-side obligation after H is proved.

Integration and evidence. Lake now builds claims/ and third-party-claims/ using its Lean configuration, which supports the quoted hyphenated module name. Imports in both directions were checked with temporary fixtures. Separate sanity checks confirmed the empty-face zero map and vertex augmentation; those checks are not a proof of H. The verifier recognizes Status: statement-only, prints the proposition definition, and reports it separately from proof files. The complete report and reproduction record preserve this distinction and the setup diagnostics. Existing proof dependencies were unchanged.

15 September 2026 — Signed row trades and full old matching moments

Status: working all-field trade-spanning lemma and all-prime relative moment-preservation theorem for one complete affine ENS level; exact finite controls. Cycle 151.

Question and stopping point. The first remaining-route obligation asks for a PHP-relative construction that respects genuine ENS relations. Can the old-moment interface retain the full relevant old degree window, instead of only row-linear targets or the earlier small Boolean window? This cycle proves such an interface for one affine level. It does not construct the mixed selector moments needed to join several levels, and it does not claim a new unrestricted Frege bound.

1. A rank cutoff does not define compatible selector moments

A tempting assignment gives low-rank affine-flat selectors their old semantic moments and sets high-rank selector moments to zero. The comparison of a flat with its codimension-one subflat already defeats that prescription. Over the Boolean field, let \(G=(x_1,\ldots,x_R)\), let \(x=x_{R+1}\), and take the old point functional at zero. At a rank cutoff \(R\), the prescription gives

\[ \Lambda(P_G)=1,\qquad \Lambda(xP_G)=0,\qquad \Lambda(P_{G\cup\{x\}})=0. \]

It therefore assigns value \(-1\) to \(P_{G\cup\{x\}}-(1-x)P_G\), although the genuine ENS comparison has a certificate through \(4h+1\). This is a failure of the proposed Boolean-domain moment assignment, not a PHP-design counterexample. Selector moments must satisfy their relations jointly. The theorem below obtains an extension by duality without prescribing those mixed moments.

For the stated degree, write \(P=P_G\), \(Q=P_{G\cup\{x\}}\), \(1-P=\sum_iU_i g_i\), and \(1-Q=\sum_iV_i g_i+V_xx\), with prefix cofactors of degree at most \(2h-1\). The literal identity

\[ Q-(1-x)P=\sum_iU_i(g_iQ) -\sum_i(1-x)V_i(g_iP) -V_xP\,x(1-x)+P(xQ) \]

uses the two blocks' actual companions and old Booleanity through \(4h+1\). Thus the incompatibility is present in the genuine source module at that ceiling, not merely in its high-degree semantic closure.

2. Disjoint two-label trades span all zero-marginal arrays

Fix \(r\ge1\) labelled rows and \(N\) columns over a field \(\mathbb K\). Let \(V_{r,N}\) be the space of arrays on injections \([r]\hookrightarrow[N]\). Let \(Z_{r,N}\) consist of arrays whose sum over each missing row is zero, for every fixed injection on the other \(r-1\) rows. A row trade chooses two labels \(a_i,b_i\) in each row, all \(2r\) labels distinct, and has coefficient array

\[ T=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r(\mathbf e_{a_i}-\mathbf e_{b_i}). \]

Lemma. If \(N\ge2r\), these trades span \(Z_{r,N}\) over every field.

Proof. Each trade has zero marginals. For spanning, induct on \(r\), and for each fixed \(r\) induct on \(N\ge2r\). At \(r=1\), zero-sum vectors are spanned by the differences \(\mathbf e_a-\mathbf e_b\).

Given \(z\in Z_{r,N}\), slice it at row \(i\) taking label \(N\). This slice is a zero-marginal array on \(r-1\) rows and \(N-1\) columns. By row induction, write it as a sum of trades, each using \(2r-2\) columns. For each such trade choose a spare label \(a\ne N\) outside its support and lift it by the row-\(i\) factor \(\mathbf e_N-\mathbf e_a\). There is a spare label because \(N-1\ge2r-1\). Subtracting these lifts cancels the slice at \((i,N)\) without introducing label \(N\) in any other row. Repeat for all \(i\). The remainder \(z'\) avoids column \(N\).

If \(N>2r\), column induction finishes. At the boundary \(N=2r\), slice \(z'\) by the label \(j\ne N\) of row 1. Its slice \(z'_j\) is a zero-marginal array on the other \(r-1\) rows and the \(2r-2\) columns avoiding \(j,N\). Row induction again spans it by trades. Extend all slices by zero to a common array space. The row-1 marginal equation says \(\sum_jz'_j=0\), so

\[ z'=\sum_{j\ne N}(\mathbf e_j-\mathbf e_N)\otimes z'_j. \]

Every summand is a sum of full disjoint-label trades. This proves the lemma without division or characteristic assumptions.

The width hypothesis matters. At \(N=2r-1\), \(r\ge2\), there are no disjoint-label trades but there are nonzero zero-marginal arrays: take the six-cycle

\[ (1,2)-(1,3)+(2,3)-(2,1)+(3,1)-(3,2) \]

on two rows and three labels, and tensor it with \(r-2\) disjoint row differences on the remaining \(2r-4\) labels. This also works in characteristic two. The lemma is an elementary spanning argument here; bibliographic novelty is not asserted.

3. Every nonzero old matching class has a constant row difference

Let \(\mathcal F^{\rm fun}_{m,N}\) be the functional unary system: Booleanity, same-row and same-column exclusions, and \(\rho_i-1\). Use its ordinary NS spaces \(\mathcal I_t\). Assume \(m\ge t\), \(N\ge\max(1,2t)\), and let \(q\) have degree at most \(t\), with \(q\notin\mathcal I_t\).

Lemma. There are a matching-normal-form polynomial \(R\), a degree \(\kappa\le t\), and \(\kappa\) rows \(U\), such that \(q-R\in\mathcal I_t\), \(\deg R=\kappa\), and either \(R\) is a nonzero constant, or a disjoint two-label trade in the rows \(U\) gives a nonzero constant signed difference of \(R\), independent of all remaining rows.

Proof. First reduce powers and row/column collisions through degree \(t\), using the ordinary matching normal form. At a positive top degree \(\kappa\), group coefficients by the exact \(\kappa\)-row set \(U\). For such a row set, let \(A_U\) be the marginal matrix on its injections into the \(N\) columns. Its kernel is \(Z_{\kappa,N}\).

If the top coefficient vector annihilates \(\ker A_U\), finite-dimensional linear algebra puts it in \({\rm im}(A_U^{\mathsf T})\). Those vectors are exactly the top matching parts of

\[ X_T(\rho_i-1),\qquad {\rm row}(T)=U\setminus\{i\},\quad |T|=\kappa-1, \]

after removing their column collisions through degree \(\kappa\). If this happens for every \(U\), subtract the corresponding ordinary NS multiples and lower the degree. Continue. The process cannot end at zero, since that would put \(q\) in \(\mathcal I_t\).

Otherwise a top vector pairs nontrivially with \(Z_{\kappa,N}\). By the spanning lemma, it pairs nontrivially with a disjoint-label trade. Apply the associated signed row difference to \(R\). Terms missing any row of \(U\) vanish. A matching monomial of degree at most \(\kappa\) that contains every row of \(U\) has no other row, so the result is a scalar, and its value is the nonzero pairing. All changes from \(q\) to \(R\) carried ordinary certificates through the original ceiling \(t\).

This detector concerns nonzero classes modulo the matching ideal. It does not assert that every Boolean-nonzero old polynomial survives: collision polynomials already belong to that ideal.

4. One complete affine level preserves the full transported old window

Fix a prime \(p\), \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), \(m=n+1\), and \(v=m\ell\). Let \(\Gamma\) be the correct compact base \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\) together with at most \(M\ge1\) complete one-level old-affine ENS blocks. Each block has common accuracy \(h\ge h_0=3(p-1)\ell\) and its own genuine coefficient equations \(r^p-r\). Write

\[ \tau(b_{it})=\sum_{z:z_t=1}X_{iz},\qquad J_t=\{q\in\mathcal P_{\le t}^{\rm old}: \tau q\in\mathcal I_t(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun})\}. \]

Choose integers \(0\le t\le D\) and \(k\) such that

\[ k\ge\max\!\left\{1,2t, \left\lceil\sqrt{m\ln(4M)}\right\rceil\right\}, \qquad k\le m-t,\qquad B=k(D+1), \]
\[ 4(k+t-1)<n,\qquad n\ge2B-1. \tag{REL-range} \]

Working theorem. Under these conditions,

\[ \mathcal C_D(\Gamma)\cap\mathcal P_{\le t}^{\rm old} \ \subseteq\ J_t. \tag{REL-old} \]

The same inclusion holds for ordinary NS consequences. The conclusion uses the transported matching ideal \(J_t\); equality with the compact base's own degree-\(t\) NS space is not asserted.

Proof: target and common multiplier. Suppose a degree-\(D\) PC proof ends at \(q\notin J_t\). Apply the preceding lemma to \(\tau q\). It gives \(R\), a row set \(U\) of size \(\kappa\le t\), and a constant nonzero signed difference \(c_q\), with \(\tau q-R\in\mathcal I_t\). In the constant case take \(U=\varnothing\). The range supplies the lemma's width hypotheses.

Use the space of homogeneous degree-\(k\) row-linear bit polynomials involving no row of \(U\). Its dimension is \(\binom{m-\kappa}{k}\ell^k\). Clean up zero and unit affine spans as in the all-prime affine proof. Set \(r_*=3\ell(k+1)+1\). Proper blocks of rank at least \(r_*\) are high; all others satisfy \((p-1)r\le h_0(k+1)\). If \(r_*>v\), there are no high blocks. Otherwise ordinary restriction to any high zero flat has image dimension at most \(\binom{v-r_*+k}{k}\), and

\[ \frac{\binom{v-r_*+k}{k}}{\binom{m-t}{k}\ell^k} =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1} \left(1-\frac{r_*-1-\ell t-(\ell+1)j} {(m-t)\ell-\ell j}\right) \le e^{-k^2/m}. \]

Indeed the subtracted numerator is at least \((2\ell-1)k-\ell t+4\ell+1\ge\ell k\), and its denominator is at most \(m\ell\). The sum of high restriction dimensions is at most one quarter of the multiplier dimension. Thus a nonzero homogeneous row-linear \(f\), independent of \(U\), vanishes as an ordinary polynomial on every high flat. This is the earlier row-excluded restriction estimate, now used with the row support of a matching-class detector.

Proof: complete source images and degree. If \(h>h_0\), first set surplus coefficient rows to zero; this does not increase proof degree. Apply the existing simultaneous affine substitution. A high block has \(f=\sum_i a_i g_i\), \(\deg a_i\le k-1\), and uses the \(p-1\) coefficient rows \((\alpha a_i)_i\), \(\alpha\ne0\), to make its product \(1-f^{p-1}\). Low blocks pack all \((p-1)r\) basis factors into \(h_0\) bins of size at most \(k+1\), so all coefficient images have degree at most \(k\).

Weight every substituted line by \(f\) itself. The old Boolean NS ceilings are \(pk+1\) for high companions, at most \(h_0(k+1)+1+k\) for low companions, and \((p+1)k\) for coefficient fields. Each fits \(k(e+1)\) for that axiom's original joint degree \(e\). Old axioms cost \(e+k\le k(e+1)\). Proper nonconstant affine blocks have actual companion degree \(2h_0+1\); zero/unit cleanup is retained, so no loose input-degree ceiling is treated as an equality. Primitive PC replay stays within \(B=k(D+1)\) and ends at \(fq\).

The affine decoder gives an old functional-PHP proof through \(B\). Since \(\tau f(\tau q-R)\in\mathcal I_{k+t}\subseteq\mathcal I_B\), it would prove \(\tau f\,R\) through \(B\).

Proof: a separated weighted target. Choose a nonzero monomial of \(f\), using one specified bit in each of \(k\) rows \(T\) disjoint from \(U\). Reserve the \(2\kappa\) labels of the \(R\)-trade. For each row of \(T\), choose a coordinate edge in its specified bit direction, avoiding all reserved labels and earlier edges. Each direction has \(n/2\) disjoint edges, and fewer than \(2\kappa+2(k-1)<n/2\) labels are forbidden. Thus these choices exist.

The combined trades use \(u=\kappa+k\) marked rows and \(2u\) distinct labels. On the residual board take a normalized matching design through \(B-u\), using the all-field matching-extension theorem. Here \(m\ge B\), \(B\ge u\), and

\[ n-2u\ge2(B-u)-1. \]

The packing inequality also leaves residual labels. Define moments exactly as in the signed residual construction: zero unless every marked row is present on its own two-label support and all other rows avoid the reserved labels; otherwise use the product of its row signs times the residual moment. Every marked row has total sign zero, so all missing-row marginals hold. This argument needs two-label supports, not coordinate edges in the rows \(U\). Boolean and collision reductions give a functional annihilating \(\mathcal I_B=\mathcal C_B\) of the old system.

Apply the \(U\)-differences first. Since \(f\) avoids \(U\), the result is \(c_q\tau f\). The coordinate differences in \(T\) then give the chosen nonzero coefficient \(c_f\) of \(f\): a degree-\(k\) row-linear monomial must contain all \(k\) selected bits to survive. The target functional therefore has value \(c_qc_f\ne0\) on \(\tau f\,R\), contradicting its old PC derivation. This proves (REL-old).

5. Full old moments, eligible zero clamps, and the remaining gap

Moment corollary. Every linear functional on \(\mathcal P_{\le t}^{\rm old}\) annihilating \(J_t\) extends to a functional on the full joint-variable space \(\mathcal P_{\le D}\) annihilating \(\mathcal C_D(\Gamma)\). Define it first on the sum of the old subspace and \(\mathcal C_D(\Gamma)\), giving the latter value zero; (REL-old) makes this well-defined. Extend linearly. A normalized old functional remains normalized.

For every fixed \(p\), polynomial or quasipolynomial inventory \(\ln M=\operatorname{polylog}n\), and \(D=\operatorname{polylog}n\), one can take \(t=D\): \(k=\sqrt n\,\operatorname{polylog}n\) and \(B=\sqrt n\,\operatorname{polylog}n\) satisfy the finite conditions eventually. These are arbitrary matching-compatible old moments throughout that window. The earlier Boolean-ideal conclusion applied only to a smaller window; the relative theorem makes no claim that every Boolean-consistent functional is matching-compatible.

Eligible joint clamps. The same statement permits adjoining \(P_a=0\) for any selected proper affine blocks with rank at least \(r_*\). The weighted image of each such axiom is \(f-f^p\), with a Boolean NS certificate through \(pk\), fitting its original degree \(2h_0\) under the same replay budget. One common \(f\) already handles all these blocks. No low-rank selector is assigned an arbitrary value.

For a concrete enlargement of scope, let \(\chi_{i,\lambda}=\prod_t b_{it}^{\lambda_t}(1-b_{it})^{1-\lambda_t}\). This degree-\(\ell\) full-label indicator is outside the earlier row-linear class and the old \(t\le\ell-2\) window. Row-state reduction gives \(\tau\chi_{i,\lambda}-X_{i,\lambda}\in\mathcal I_\ell\). Pin row \(i\) to \(\lambda\), delete that label, and take a normalized residual design through \(t\); since \(n-1\ge2t-1\) here, it gives value one to \(X_{i,\lambda}\) while annihilating \(\mathcal I_t\). Thus \(\chi_{i,\lambda}\notin J_t\) whenever \(t\ge\ell\) in the stated range. Conversely, old collision equations remain allowed consequences in \(J_t\).

What changed. The one-affine-level endpoint now retains the complete old matching-moment window needed at a chosen polylogarithmic proof degree. The unresolved next step is a compatible extension when the new inputs use earlier genuine selectors. Preserving old moments alone does not prescribe mixed selector moments, make later inputs affine, or yield an induction on source depth. The failed cutoff prescription is a concrete warning against that inference. The universal Boolean-domain obstruction remains in force.

15 September 2026 — Elementary matching fillings and the unresolved selector coupling

Status: working elementary proof of a known matching-complex vanishing statement; source-interface audit without a new multilevel extension. Cycle 152.

Question. Can the new full old-moment interface be applied to a further complete source level? The intended stopping point was a sufficient extension argument or a precise obstruction to the proposed interface. The audit below identifies the additional compatibility statement but does not prove or refute it. A short consequence of the row-trade lemma supplies a direct proof of the old matching-filling dependency, removing the need to import that vanishing result from topology.

1. The required extension allows joint choices

Fix a final degree ceiling \(D\). Let \(\Gamma_1\) be the compact PHP base plus the complete first affine level, and let \(\Gamma_2\) add a further complete level with inputs affine in genuine earlier selectors. For a prescribed old functional \(\lambda\), write

\[ \mathcal E_j(\lambda)= \{\Lambda\in{\rm Ann}(\mathcal C_D(\Gamma_j)): \Lambda|_{\mathcal P_{\le D}^{\rm old}}=\lambda\}. \]

The previous theorem supplies \(\mathcal E_1(\lambda)\ne\varnothing\) for every \(J_D\)-compatible \(\lambda\) under its finite bounds. The next sufficient statement would give \(\mathcal E_2(\lambda)\ne\varnothing\), with parameters that survive later composition. A proof of refutation exclusion needs even less: at least one normalized compatible choice. It need not extend every arbitrarily chosen member of \(\mathcal E_1(\lambda)\).

This is the same finite-dimensional extension criterion used earlier: a functional on a subspace \(U\) extends to annihilate a subspace \(S\) exactly when it annihilates \(U\cap S\). Replacing \(U\), the old polynomial window, by all previous joint variables changes that intersection. The one-level theorem makes no assertion about the new intersection.

The actual costed modular source asks for still less than an annihilator of every concrete ENS consequence: it suffices to annihilate all supplied source-module multiples, while charging their witness ceilings. This is a possible endpoint to retain. It does not require arbitrary raw coefficient moments or an augmented NS/PC equality.

Two existing controls prevent an unjustified induction. The rank-cutoff prescription violates an actual flat comparison. In the earlier module-band example, a chosen degree-\(6h+u\) functional, \(u<2h\), fixes a triple moment to zero and cannot preserve it when the degree-\(8h\) multiple \(Z_C(Z_C-Z_AZ_B)\) becomes available. That is a counterexample to that chosen degree-extension prescription. It does not by itself refute a same-ceiling extension for the present next ENS level.

The singleton equations solve a restricted module band only. The full compiler is not known to remain in that band, and later inputs are not old-affine. The factorial-inventory matching tree also shows that local consistency alone cannot yield an inventory-independent global extension. Its inventory is outside the current polynomial-source regime.

Audit outcome. No multilevel extension was constructed. A useful next construction must select the mixed moments jointly, or directly exclude the supplied old-target module identity with a dependence on inventory and source depth that fits the old barrier. Requiring universal preservation of every earlier selector choice is a stronger convenience, not an established route requirement.

2. An elementary proof of the exact old filling statement

Let \(\Delta_{r,N}\) be the simplicial complex whose faces are partial injections from \(r\) labelled rows into \(N\) columns. Use augmented oriented simplicial chains over a field \(\mathbb K\), including \(C_{-1}=\mathbb K\) and the usual augmentation of vertices.

Known vanishing statement, new proof in this record. For \(r\ge1\) and \(N\ge2r-1\), every reduced \((r-2)\)-cycle in \(\Delta_{r,N}\) is the boundary of an \((r-1)\)-chain:

\[ \widetilde H_{r-2}(\Delta_{r,N};\mathbb K)=0. \tag{EF-fill} \]

This is the portion of the Björner–Lovász–Vrećica–Živaljević chessboard-complex theorem used by our old matching-extension proof. The argument below proves it directly from the row-trade lemma. It does not assert a new topological theorem or prove the source-level extension in Section 1.

Proof. Induct on \(r\), for all \(N\ge2r-1\). If \(r=1\), any scalar reduced \((-1)\)-chain is the augmentation of that scalar times one vertex, since \(N\ge1\).

Let \(r\ge2\) and let \(z\) be a reduced \((r-2)\)-cycle. Write \(v_j=(r,j)\). Separate its faces according to whether they use the last row:

\[ z=z_0+\sum_{j=1}^N v_j*y_j . \]

Here \(z_0\) avoids row \(r\), and \(y_j\) is a chain of dimension \(r-3\) in the link of \(v_j\), namely \(\Delta_{r-1,N-1}\) with column \(j\) deleted. The notation \(v_j*c\) places \(v_j\) first in the orientation; it obeys

\[ \partial(v_j*c)=c-v_j*\partial c. \tag{EF-cone} \]

The components of \(\partial z=0\) containing \(v_j\) show that \(\partial y_j=0\). For \(r=2\), these are reduced \((-1)\)-cycles, as intended. Since \(N-1\ge2(r-1)-1\), row induction gives a chain \(w_j\) in the same link with \(\partial w_j=y_j\). Add the corresponding cone boundaries:

\[ z'=z+\sum_j\partial(v_j*w_j) =z_0+\sum_jw_j. \]

Thus \(z'\) is a cycle avoiding the last row, in top dimension \(r-2\) of \(\Delta_{r-1,N}\). Orient its top faces by increasing row number. Its boundary equations are exactly the zero row marginals, with the fixed alternating row signs. The row-trade lemma applies because \(N\ge2(r-1)\), and expresses

\[ z'=\sum_a c_aT_a \]

as a linear combination of signed disjoint two-label trades on the first \(r-1\) rows. Each trade uses \(2r-2\) columns. There is a spare column \(j_a\), since \(N\ge2r-1\), so \(v_{j_a}*T_a\) is a valid chain and its boundary is \(T_a\). Consequently

\[ W=\sum_a c_a(v_{j_a}*T_a)-\sum_jv_j*w_j \qquad\text{satisfies}\qquad \partial W=z. \]

This completes the induction. Every cone uses a vertex outside the other chain's rows and columns. The two uses of the width hypothesis are explicit: the links meet the induction range, and every top trade has a spare column. The proof uses no division, so the same construction also works with coefficients in any commutative ring; the field statement suffices here.

3. Boundary controls and consequence for the existing endpoint

At \(r=2,N=3\), the reduced cycle \([(1,1)]-[(2,1)]\) is filled by

\[ -[(1,1),(2,2)]+[(1,3),(2,2)]-[(1,3),(2,1)]. \]

Its boundary is the stated cycle, with both intermediate vertices cancelling. At \(r=2,N=2\), the complex consists of the two disjoint edges \(\{(1,1),(2,2)\}\) and \(\{(1,2),(2,1)\}\). The same vertex difference joins different components and is not a boundary. Summing coefficients in the first component gives a linear functional that is zero on every edge boundary but one on this cycle. This shows why a width condition cannot simply be dropped, over every field.

For each \(s\)-row set in the old matching-moment construction, apply (EF-fill) to the prescribed oriented \((s-2)\)-cycle. The earlier compatibility proof shows it is a cycle, and the filling supplies its degree-\(s\) moments. Hence the existing conclusions

\[ \mathcal I_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le t}=\mathcal I_t, \qquad \mathcal C_B=\mathcal I_B \quad(m\ge B,\ N\ge\max(1,2B-1)) \]

now have a proof whose filling input is entirely in the notebook. This is a replacement proof of a known dependency, not a stronger degree barrier. It also applies to the residual boards used in the preceding cycle. No augmented ENS stability or new Frege bound follows automatically.

No new numerical suite was needed: the cone identities and the two boundary controls are explicit. The prior exact row-trade matrices are retained in their original checkpoint and were not rerun. The evidence note records the dependency and scope audit.

Process assessment. Reading the existing module controls prevented a repeated greedy-moment construction; the short general filling proof removes an imported proof dependency, while the main mixed-selector obligation remains open and needs no additional framework rule.

15 September 2026 — Testing a functional route from the source's small matrix programs

Status: source-specific application of a known finite-field limitation; no new coupled module functional or Frege bound. Cycle 153.

Question and stopping point. The formal source certificate has polynomial-width read-once oblivious algebraic branching programs (ROABPs) in every variable order. Could functional lower bounds for this model supply the missing PHP-relative module argument? This cycle checked the actual source representation against the relevant finite-field limitation before attempting a rank computation.

1. A distinguished module has an easy semantic inverse

The known fixed-field obstruction is stated in Elbaz–Govindasamy–Lu–Tzameret (2025), Section 5.4, Theorem 49. Its ROABP lower bounds use instances that are themselves hard for that model; they do not directly apply to our small module equations.

Here is its application to the present source. Fix \(\mathbb F_p\) and one variable order. If \(F\) has a width-\(W\) ROABP, then

\[ G={\rm ml}(F^{p-2}) \quad\text{has width at most }W^{p-2},\qquad G(u)F(u)=1\quad\text{whenever }u\in\{0,1\}^{V},\ F(u)\ne0. \]

For \(p=2\), take \(G=1\). For \(p>2\), tensor \(p-2\) copies of each matrix in the same order. Multilinearization replaces its univariate matrix \(M_i(u_i)\) by \(M_i(0)+(M_i(1)-M_i(0))u_i\), preserving width and Boolean values. Fermat's identity gives the last equality.

Our OR modules have \(F=c-ab\), with affine \(a,b,c\), so width six suffices by the existing affine-factor construction. Thus even on the Boolean zero set of all other module equations, this inverse remains cheap wherever \(F\ne0\). A lower bound on that one semantic cofactor cannot be the missing argument.

Certificate limitation. This does not give a low-cost joint proof. Certifying \(1-GF\) from the other modules may require large witness degree or large coefficients. The fixed-field identity removes the prospective difficulty of the distinguished inverse; it does not remove the difficulty of those residual certificates.

2. What the source representation does and does not supply

The recorded source refinement gives an ordinary identity

\[ 1=\sum_\alpha Q_\alpha(u)H_\alpha(u),\qquad \deg_w Q_\alpha+\nu_\alpha\le D, \]

where the \(Q_\alpha\) are polynomially many sums of products of \(O(\log S_{\rm proof})\) affine forms, and \(\nu_\alpha\) is the supplied concrete witness ceiling. The resulting polynomial-width matrix program is real additional structure, but it lives over the old and formal selector coordinates. It has not been transferred to a certificate over the original PHP variables at a sufficient cost.

A direct lower-bound application would therefore need both a theorem for these actual, source-dependent equations and control of their concrete witnesses. A theorem for a different hard axiom family, or a degree bound on the displayed quadratic targets alone, supplies neither. The joint moment endpoint remains available: annihilate all legal costed module multiples with one normalized functional. This cycle did not construct it.

The earlier query-rate obstruction also remains relevant. Generic polynomial description size, fixed arithmetic depth, and degree bounds on queries do not suffice. The source's exact relations and their witness costs must participate in a new argument.

The audit note records the exact source version, inspected sections, representation checks, and limitations. No new numerical suite or paper download was needed. One redundant local excerpt request used an invalid end anchor and was rejected before producing text; it did not affect mathematical evidence.

Process assessment. Checking the fixed-field inverse limitation before writing matrix experiments avoided a route that cannot yield the intended single-cofactor lower bound; no new main-route construction was obtained, and the existing generic falsification rule covers this case.

15 September 2026 — Why a fixed filling rule cannot handle all selector coefficients

Status: exact coupled-moment presentation and working obstruction to a universal conditioning-compatible filling rule; finite all-prime controls. Cycle 154.

Question. Can the elementary row-set filling construct the missing joint source functional simply by taking selector moments as vector coefficients? Constant coefficient relations allow that operation. The old-variable-dependent source relations require more, and the proposed uniform commutation property is impossible. This identifies a failure of the automatic construction; source-dependent simultaneous corrections remain open.

1. The exact coupled linear equations

Use the binary costed modular source interface, with old functional unary variables \(X\), formal Boolean selector variables \(Z_a\) of weights \(w_a\), and source modules \(H_\alpha\) of supplied witness costs \(\nu_\alpha\). Include selector Booleanity at cost \(2w_a\), as justified for this binary source. Keep \(\deg_w H_\alpha\le\nu_\alpha\); the smaller degree of a reduced target does not replace its cost.

After the ordinary Boolean/exclusion normal forms, a joint degree-\(D\) functional is specified by

\[ z_{T,R}=\Lambda(X_T Z_R),\qquad |T|+w(R)\le D,\qquad w(R)=\sum_{a\in R}w_a, \]

where \(T\) is a partial matching and \(R\) a set of distinct selectors. Repeated powers reduce to their supports. The old constraints are exactly

\[ \sum_{j\notin{\rm col}(T)} z_{T+(i,j),R}=z_{T,R}, \quad i\notin{\rm row}(T),\quad |T|+w(R)<D, \qquad z_{\varnothing,\varnothing}=1. \tag{CM-old} \]

Write the reduced target of a module as \(H_\alpha=\sum_{A,S}c^\alpha_{A,S}X_AZ_S\). Its remaining constraints are

\[ \sum_{\substack{A,S\\T\cup A\ {\rm compatible}}} c^\alpha_{A,S}\,z_{T\cup A,R\cup S}=0, \qquad |T|+w(R)+\nu_\alpha\le D. \tag{CM-source} \]

Compatibility allows identical cells in both matchings, but excludes different cells sharing a row or column. These equations are necessary and sufficient for the stated formal costed-module annihilator: test monomial cofactors, reduce old powers/exclusions and selector powers within the original budget, and use linearity. This is the old normal-form argument with every selector component and every supplied module multiplier retained. It is not an augmented PC-stability assertion.

For each fixed \(R\), (CM-old) is an ordinary old design problem through \(D-w(R)\). Equation (CM-source) couples different \(R\)'s and changes the old matching index \(T\). Solving the first family separately does not solve the second.

2. Constant coefficients work; old multiplication is different

If chains take values in one fixed finite-dimensional vector space \(V\), the elementary filling theorem works coordinatewise. A chosen linear scalar filling map tensored with \({\rm id}_V\) commutes with every fixed linear map on \(V\). Hence constant coefficient relations that are already satisfied by the boundary are preserved by that construction.

The genuine source also contains comparisons such as \(Z_C-(1-x)Z_B\), where \(x\) is an old value; the affine-flat instance was explicitly certified through \(4h+1\) in the codimension-one comparison. Its moment equation involves multiplication by \(x\) on the old component. In unary normal form, multiplying by an old cell changes \(T\) to \(T\cup\{e\}\), with the collision and idempotence cases. This is not a fixed operation on the selector coefficient space alone.

A tempting automatic repair is to choose old extension maps that commute with these conditioning operations. The following obstruction rules out the uniform version of that repair.

3. No universal linear sections commuting with row conditioning

Over any field, let \(\mathcal A_s={\rm Ann}(\mathcal I_s(\mathcal F^{\rm fun}_{m,N}))\), and let \(R_s:\mathcal A_s\to\mathcal A_{s-1}\) be restriction. These are spaces of possibly unnormalized functionals. For a cell \(e\), define the unnormalized conditioning map

\[ M_e^{(s)}:\mathcal A_s\longrightarrow\mathcal A_{s-1}, \qquad (M_e^{(s)}\lambda)(q)=\lambda(X_e q). \]

It is well-defined because an old generator multiple through \(s-1\), multiplied by \(X_e\), remains an old generator multiple through \(s\). The row equations imply, for every row \(i\),

\[ \sum_{j=1}^N M_{ij}^{(s)}=R_s. \tag{NC-row} \]

Working proposition. Let \(d\ge1\), \(m\ge d+1\), and \(N\ge2d+1\). The restriction maps through degree \(d+1\) have linear sections, but there is no pair of linear sections

\[ E_{d-1}:\mathcal A_{d-1}\to\mathcal A_d,\qquad E_d:\mathcal A_d\to\mathcal A_{d+1}, \qquad R_dE_{d-1}={\rm id},\quad R_{d+1}E_d={\rm id}, \]

that satisfy, for every cell of even one fixed row \(i\),

\[ M_{ij}^{(d+1)}E_d=E_{d-1}M_{ij}^{(d)} \quad(j=1,\ldots,N). \tag{NC-commute} \]

Proof. Individual sections exist by the old extension theorem and linear algebra. If (NC-commute) held, sum it over \(j\), using linearity and (NC-row). This gives

\[ {\rm id}_{\mathcal A_d}=E_{d-1}R_d. \]

It would make \(R_d\) injective. But choose \(d\) rows with disjoint two-label supports. Assign zero to every matching moment below degree \(d\); at degree \(d\), assign the signed row-trade coefficients on these rows and zero to every other matching. All row marginals vanish, so this is a nonzero member of \(\mathcal A_d\) whose restriction is zero. The \(2d\) required labels exist. This contradicts injectivity.

The obstruction applies at every stated degree, including well inside the old stable range. It does not require the old system to be unsatisfiable: the issue is loss of higher moments under restriction. It rules out a fixed family of linear sections with the universal commutation requirement, not every source-dependent choice of fillings.

4. A complete small control, over three fields

For functional PHP with four rows and three labels, set \(\lambda(1)=1\), and give every row first moments \((1,0,0)\). For every ordered row pair \(i<i'\), set its joint label-moment matrix to

\[ A=\begin{pmatrix} 0&1&0\\ 0&0&0\\ 1&-1&0 \end{pmatrix}. \]

For the reversed pair use the transpose. Within one row, repeated cells have their first moment and different cells have moment zero. Matrix \(A\) has zero diagonal and both row and column sums \((1,0,0)\). Thus these rules give a complete normalized degree-two old design over every field.

Its same-column moment \(\lambda(X_{1,1}X_{2,1})=0\) differs from the product of its two means, which is one. At \(d=1\), a universal conditioning-compatible pair of sections would force \(\lambda_2(X_eX_f)=\lambda_1(X_e)\lambda_1(X_f)\) for \(\lambda_1=E_0(1)\), \(\lambda_2=E_1(\lambda_1)\). In an unsatisfiable Boolean quadratic system that would yield a satisfying point: Booleanity makes the means zero or one, and every quadratic equation evaluates to its prescribed zero moment. For functional PHP it would give an injection of too many rows into too few labels. This is another view of the failure; the row-sum proof above covers every \(d\).

The compiled checker verified all 94 ordinary degree-two generator multiples for this design over each of \(\mathbb F_2,\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\). It also verified all 57 such constraints for a three-row, three-label injection in each field. The injection has factorized moments on its point-functional subspace. This does not give sections on the full moment spaces.

All six systems and all 453 constraints passed. Replacing \(-1\) in \(A\) by \(+1\) leaves the binary case unchanged and violates a row marginal over \(\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\), as expected. Complete first and second moments, every constraint evaluation, and the controls are in the JSONL evidence; the reproduction note gives commands and scope.

5. Remaining obligation

The exact task is feasibility of (CM-old) and (CM-source) together, with the original witness ceilings. Fixed coordinatewise extension plus universal conditioning commutation cannot supply it. This does not show that the actual compiled source requires such sections, or that a jointly chosen normalized functional is impossible.

Different scalar fillings differ by zero-boundary cycles. On an \(r\)-row set with \(N\ge2r\), the row-trade spanning result describes all those directions; retain this extra column of room beyond the minimal filling range. A source-dependent construction could try to use them to correct the module defects. No quantitative rank or compatibility bound making those corrections possible for the full source is proved here.

15 September 2026 — Finite augmented chain spaces for the chessboard formalization

Status: verified foundational API (H01); no filling theorem is asserted.

Statement and conventions

For a finite vertex type \(V\), let \(K\) be a downward-closed family of finite subsets containing the empty set. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), write \(C(K,k)\) for coefficient functions on all subsets of \(V\) supported on \(k\)-element faces of \(K\). The cell count \(k\) corresponds to reduced simplicial degree \(k-1\). The ambient boundary is \((\partial c)(T)=\sum_{v\notin T}c(T\cup\{v\})\). It is linear, maps \(C(K,k+1)\) into \(C(K,k)\), and vanishes on \(C(K,0)\). In particular, on a vertex chain its empty-face coordinate is the sum of the vertex coefficients, including when \(V\) is empty.

Proof. Each boundary coordinate is a finite sum of coordinate projections, hence preserves addition and scalar multiplication. If \(T\) is not a face, every superset \(T\cup \{v\}\) is not a face by downward closure. If \(|T|\ne k\) and \(v\) is outside \(T\), then \(|T\cup \{v\}|=|T|+1\ne k+1\). In either case every summand vanishes for a supported input. For a chain supported at cell count zero, every insertion outside \(T\) has positive cardinality and therefore contributes zero. These arguments establish all stated endpoint cases without treating the empty face as a vertex.

Restriction to the \(k\)-element faces and extension by zero are inverse linear maps: on a face they leave the coefficient unchanged; off that set the support condition forces zero. Thus \(C(K,k)\) agrees exactly with the usual finite coefficient space on \(k\)-faces. Taking \(K\) to be sets of cells with injective row and column projections gives the chessboard complex: injectivity is inherited by subsets, and both projections are vacuously injective on the empty set. Reordering the three face conditions identifies its exact-face coefficient functions with the existing ChessboardChain interface.

Verified scope. AugmentedChains.lean implements these definitions, linear maps, support proofs, and linear equivalences. This is standard finite simplicial-chain algebra extracted for the BLVZ route, with a full elementary proof here. Boundary squared zero is the next H02 obligation. Compatibility of this insertion formula with the original chessboard incidence-sum boundary is explicitly reserved for H03; a vector-space equivalence alone does not establish it. \(H\) remains a statement-only proposition.

15 September 2026 — The finite augmented boundary squares to zero

Status: verified standard chain identity (H02); no acyclicity or filling existence is claimed.

Statement and full proof

For every finite vertex type \(V\) and every coefficient function \(c\) on finite subsets of \(V\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), the insertion boundary from H01 satisfies \(\partial (\partial c)=0\). Consequently its restricted maps \(C(K,k+2)\longrightarrow C(K,k+1)\longrightarrow C(K,k)\) compose to zero for every downward-closed complex \(K\) and every \(k\ge 0\).

Proof. Fix a subset \(T\). Expanding the two boundary sums gives one term \(c(T\cup \{v,w\})\) for each ordered pair of distinct vertices \(v,w\) outside \(T\), and zero for every other pair. Swap \(v\) and \(w\). This is an involution with no fixed point among the nonzero summands; the underlying union and hence its coefficient are unchanged. Each pair of equal coefficients sums to zero in \(\mathbb F_2\). The entire finite sum is therefore zero. Restricting this identity to supported chains proves the graded assertion. When \(k=0\) this includes edges followed by vertex augmentation; the outgoing boundary on chains supported on the empty face is already zero by H01. Empty vertex types and empty sums require no exception.

Verification and route. AugmentedBoundarySquared.lean uses a finite-sum involution to verify exactly this proof. The full audit records both the ambient and graded theorem types and their axioms. The next assigned obligation is H03 naturality and the original chessboard-boundary bridge. The main Frege goal, working context, and discrepancy list remain unchanged.

15 September 2026 — Chain maps, chessboard transpose, and the exact boundary bridge

Status: verified H03 interfaces and identities; H01–H03 are complete. The filling theorem \(H\) remains unproved.

Statements and complete human-readable proofs

Use the supported augmented coefficient spaces from H01. Let \(e:V\longrightarrow W\) be an injective map of finite vertex types. For an ambient coefficient function \(c\), define \(e_*c(T)=c(e^{-1}T)\) when every vertex of \(T\) belongs to the image of \(e\), and zero otherwise. This map is linear, injective, and commutes with the augmented boundary. If \(e\) sends every face of \(K\) to a face of \(L\), it restricts to a linear chain map \(C(K,k)\longrightarrow C(L,k)\) in every cell count \(k\). For an inclusion of face families on the same vertex type, the chain map is simply the unchanged coefficient function. A bijective relabeling has the inverse induced by the inverse vertex map.

Proof of naturality. If \(T\) contains a vertex outside the image of \(e\), then every \(T\cup \{w\}\) does too, so both \(\partial (e_*c)(T)\) and \(e_*(\partial c)(T)\) are zero. Otherwise restrict the boundary sum to \(w\) in the image of \(e\): all other terms are zero by definition. Write \(w=e(v)\), uniquely. The condition \(w\notin T\) becomes \(v\notin e^{-1}T\), and the preimage of \(T\cup \{e(v)\}\) is \(e^{-1}T\cup \{v\}\). Thus the remaining sum is exactly \((\partial c)(e^{-1}T)\). This proves naturality including augmentation. Linearity follows coordinatewise from the definition. Also \(e_*c(e(S))=c(S)\), proving injectivity. If a potentially nonzero target coefficient is at \(T\), then \(T=e(e^{-1}T)\); its preimage must be a face of \(K\) of cell count \(k\), so the target is a face of \(L\) of the same count. This proves preservation of support. The inclusion identity and its commutation with the boundary are immediate. For a bijection, the induced map evaluates at the inverse image of \(T\); applying the inverse bijection restores every coefficient, proving the two-sided inverse.

Chessboard transpose. The cell swap \((i,j)\mapsto (j,i)\) exchanges the two injective-projection conditions defining a matching. Thus it sends every face of the \(s\times N\) chessboard complex to a face of the \(N\times s\) complex. Apply the preceding chain-map construction; applying the swap twice is the identity. Consequently the resulting transpose map preserves cell count, commutes with the boundary, and is invertible. Generic injective maps and face-preservation witnesses likewise permit deleted rows or column complements to be embedded and relabeled without changing incidence.

Exact bridge to the existing interface. If \(T\) is a \(k\)-face, the insertion-boundary formula on an extension-by-zero chain equals the sum of coefficients on all \((k+1)\)-faces \(S\) containing \(T\). Indeed a nonzero insertion term has \(S=T\cup \{v\}\), with \(v\) outside \(T\) and \(S\) a face; conversely \(|S|=|T|+1\) and \(T\subseteq S\) give a unique such vertex \(v\). Reindexing this bijection proves equality of the two finite sums. Applying the checked chessboard face equivalence therefore identifies the supported differential with the original chessboardBoundary. At cell count zero the original outgoing boundary and the supported outgoing boundary are both zero. Hence for every \(k\), the boundary of the supported chain corresponding to \(c\) is exactly the supported chain corresponding to its original boundary. In particular, the original boundary vanishes if and only if the ambient supported boundary vanishes. This last implication uses injectivity of the chain-space equivalence, not merely equality of dimensions.

Checked interfaces. The full verification report records all claimed declaration types and axioms. No axiom, placeholder proof, or filling assumption was introduced.

15 September 2026 — Lean verification of chessboard induction arithmetic (H11)

Status: complete Lean formalization of the extracted arithmetic claim; no chessboard homology or filling theorem is asserted.

Assignment and stopping point. Execute Spin-formalize on H11 of the bit-PHP formalization route, independently of the parallel chain and topology branches. Discharge the parameter inequalities and induction measure needed by H12, with explicit reduced-degree conventions, then stop after verification and a local checkpoint. The arithmetic is extracted from the recorded classical star-cover proof and the publication's topology appendix. It is supporting arithmetic for the BLVZ argument, not a new connectivity result.

Claim: chessboard parameter arithmetic

For natural numbers \(a,b\), let \(\nu(a,b)=\min\{a,b,\lfloor(a+b+1)/3\rfloor\}\). This parameter is symmetric, satisfies \(\nu\le a,b\) and \(3\nu\le a+b+1\), and is positive when both sides are positive. A zero side gives \(\nu=0\); a one-row board with positive column count has \(\nu=1\). For \(2\le a\le b\),

\[ \nu(a,b)\le b-1. \]

If also \(2\le t<b\), put \(\mu=\nu(a-1,b-t)\). Then

\[ \nu(a,b)+1\le\mu+t, \qquad (\nu(a,b)-2)-t+1\le\mu-2, \]

where the second formula is an integer inequality. For \(1\le a\le b\) and every natural \(t\), both \(\min(a-1,b-t)\) and \(\min(b-t,a-1)\) are strictly below \(\min(a,b)\), with natural truncated subtraction for board sizes. Finally \(2s-1\le N\) implies \(\nu(s,N)=s\); the Lean version uses natural subtraction and also holds for \(s=0\).

Full arithmetic proof. Symmetry follows by exchanging the first two minimum entries and commuting addition. The three bounds are immediate from the minimum and the defining floor inequality. If \(a,b\ge1\), then all three entries are at least one; if one side is zero their minimum is zero. When \(a=1\) and \(b\ge1\), the minimum is therefore exactly one.

For the ordered bound, if \(a<b\) then \(\nu\le a\le b-1\). If \(a=b\ge2\), then \(2b+1<3b\), so \(\lfloor(2b+1)/3\rfloor\le b-1\). For the intersection inequality let \(r=\nu-t+1\), regarded as an integer. If \(r\le0\), the nonnegativity of \(\mu\) suffices. Otherwise, \(\nu\le a\) and \(t\ge2\) give \(a-1\ge r\), while \(\nu\le b-1\) gives \(b-t\ge r\). The numerator of the third minimum entry is exactly \(a+b-t\), because \(a\ge2\) and \(t<b\). Moreover

\[ a+b-t\ge3\nu-t-1\ge3\nu-3t+3=3r, \]

the second inequality being equivalent to \(2t\ge4\). Hence its floor after division by three is at least \(r\), and so is their minimum \(\mu\). Rearranging gives the additive natural inequality and the stated integer-degree inequality. Either orientation of the intersection has smaller side at most \(a-1<a=\min(a,b)\), proving the induction decrease. For the stable range, \(s=0\) is immediate. For \(s\ge1\), the assumption gives \(N\ge s\) and \(s+N+1\ge3s\); thus all entries of the minimum defining \(\nu(s,N)\) are at least \(s\), and its first entry equals \(s\). This proves every parameter assertion.

Reduced-degree boundaries. If \(k\) counts cells, its reduced simplicial degree is the integer \(k-1\). For natural \(k,n\), the interval condition \(-1\le k-1\le n-2\) is equivalent to \(k<n\), simply by adding one and using integrality. For an integer \(q<-1\), no natural \(k\) satisfies \(k-1\le q\), since \(k-1\ge-1\). In particular \(n=0\) requests no degree, and \(n=1\) requests only \(k=0\), the augmentation coordinate. These are arithmetic facts, not assertions that an empty-face-only complex is acyclic. The restriction \(t<b\) in the intersection theorem is the nonempty-board case; \(t=b\) is deliberately excluded from the inductive homology application.

Formal scope and checks. The new indexed claim third-party:chessboard-parameter-arithmetic is implemented in ChessboardParameterArithmetic.lean, importing only Lean's checked omega tactic. Its thirteen theorem declarations cover the complete statement above. The full verification report preserves their explicit types and axiom reports alongside the existing claim audit; the pre-proof scope map and reproduction record describe dependencies and setup. No assumption of \(H\) or custom axiom is used.

15 September 2026 — Explicit augmented cone contraction

Status: H04 finite \(\mathbb F_2\) cone contraction and exactness; entire stated claim verified with its dependencies.

Statement and full proof

Let \(K\) be a downward-closed family of finite subsets of a finite vertex set \(V\), containing the empty face. Assume \(v\) is a cone vertex: \(S\cup \{v\}\) belongs to \(K\) for every \(S\) in \(K\). Use the augmented supported chain spaces and insertion boundary from H01. Then every supported \(k\)-cell cycle \(c\), for every \(k\ge 0\), has a supported \((k+1)\)-cell filler. This includes the empty-face augmentation \(k=0\). A complex containing only the empty face has no cone vertex and is not covered by the hypothesis.

Construction. On every ambient coefficient function define \(h(c)(S)=c(S\setminus \{v\})\) if \(v\in S\), and zero otherwise. We prove the full identity \(\partial h(c)+h(\partial c)=c\), without a cycle or support assumption. If \(v\notin S\), the only potentially nonzero insertion term of \(\partial h(c)(S)\) inserts \(v\), and gives \(c(S)\); \(h(\partial c)(S)=0\). If \(v\in S\), the insertion terms of \(\partial c(S\setminus \{v\})\) split into the \(v\) term \(c(S)\), and terms inserting a vertex \(w\) outside \(S\). Each latter term is exactly \(h(c)(S\cup \{w\})\), so \(\partial c(S\setminus \{v\})=c(S)+\partial h(c)(S)\). These repeated terms cancel over \(\mathbb F_2\), proving the identity at \(S\).

If \(c\) is supported on \(k\)-cell faces, a nonzero coefficient of \(h(c)\) at \(S\) implies \(v\in S\) and \(S\setminus \{v\}\) is a \(k\)-cell face. Thus \(S=(S\setminus \{v\})\cup \{v\}\) is a face by the cone hypothesis and has \(k+1\) cells. Hence \(h\) preserves the required shifted support. For \(\partial c=0\) the contraction identity gives \(\partial h(c)=c\). This proves exactness in every cell count, and in particular for a full simplex with a chosen vertex. No homotopy or homology-group machinery is assumed.

Interfaces and scope. ExactAt K k means precisely the supported cycle-filling assertion above; AcyclicThrough K n requires it for all \(k\lt n\), corresponding to reduced degrees \(-1\) through \(n-2\). The \(n=0\) case is vacuous, while \(n=1\) requires augmentation exactness. IsCone, cone_identity, cone_supported, and cone_exact live in AugmentedCone.lean. These project interfaces adapt standard elementary cone contraction; their location implies no claim of novel topology. H05–H07 and the chessboard filling theorem remain separate obligations.
